Comment on “A remote intervention to improve medication nonadherence guided by a marker of risk derived from the electronic health records of adolescent transplant recipients”
Enhancing protection against herpes zoster in solid organ transplant recipients
Long-term patient and graft survival for children and young adults after kidney transplantation and re-transplantation – results from the ERA Registry
items.abstract: Long-term outcomes after kidney re-transplantation in patients with childhood-onset kidney replacement therapy (KRT) are poorly characterized. Using European Renal Association Registry data, we studied 12,623 patients who started KRT before age 20 years and received one (n = 11,078), two (n = 2,962) or three (n = 718) kidney transplants (KTs) between 1978 and 2019. In this descriptive study, 5-, 10- and 15-year patient survival was 97, 94 and 90 % after first, 97, 95, 94 % after second and 96, 94, 92 % after third KT; corresponding graft survival was 79, 63, 50 %, 69, 52, 38 %, and 67, 51, 38 %, respectively. After first KT, mortality and graft failure risks were lower after pre-emptive transplantation (adjusted hazard ratio: 0.66 [95% CI 0.54-0.80] and 0.89 [0.82-0.97], respectively) and after living donor (LD) transplantation (0.71 [0.61-0.83] and 0.76 [0.70-0.81], respectively). Additionally, graft failure risk was higher between ages 10-24 years, and for patients with glomerulonephritis, metabolic diseases or recurrent nephropathies, and females. In re-transplants, LD and pre-emptive KTs (particularly for second KT) and prior graft survival > 5 years were associated with reduced graft failure. Overall, LD, pre-emptive transplantation, and durable prior grafts were associated with the best outcomes.

items.title: The Global Lung Initiative Race-neutral Equations and Lower Limits of Normal Refine Baseline Lung Allograft Dysfunction Risk Stratification after Lung Transplantation
items.abstract: Baseline lung allograft dysfunction (BLAD) contextualises peak post-transplant lung function, but the prognostic impact of GLI-2012 versus GLI-2022 and respective 80% predicted versus LLN classification remains unclear. In 1283 adult bilateral first lung transplant recipients from three European centres, baseline FEV 1 was defined as the mean of the two highest post-transplant values at one year after transplantation or beyond, with corresponding FVC values. Percent-predicted values and LLN were calculated using GLI-2012 and GLI-2022, and subnormal lung function was evaluated for graft survival, CLAD-free survival, and survival after CLAD diagnosis using Kaplan-Meier and adjusted Cox models. GLI-2022 classified fewer patients as below normal than GLI-2012. Using the 80% threshold, 412 patients (32%) were classified as BLAD by GLI-2022, while 112 (9%) were reclassified from BLAD to No BLAD compared with GLI-2012. Using LLN, 300 patients (23%) were Below LLN by GLI-2022, while 146 (11%) were reclassified from Below to Above LLN. Outcomes after normality reclassification varied by endpoint. Persistent BLAD and Below LLN were associated with worse graft and CLAD-free outcomes, with risk further refined by FEV 1 /FVC impairment patterns and BLAD severity. These findings support BLAD's prognostic relevance and the importance of using race-neutral equations and LLN-based definitions after transplantation.

items.title: Staged acellular perfusion, rewarming, and seamless transition to blood-based normothermic machine perfusion of the kidney: a paired porcine study
items.abstract: Normothermic machine perfusion (NMP) is a promising platform for assessment and treatment of kidneys prior to transplantation. Initial cool acellular perfusion with a graduated transition to normothermia might offer advantages over direct NMP reperfusion by 1) reducing ischaemia reperfusion injury, and 2) flushing donor-derived blood components from the microvasculature prior to the addition of red cells. 8 pairs of porcine kidneys were assigned randomly to up to 24 hours of NMP, or to an adapted protocol including initial sub-normothermic acellular (SNAP) and transition phases prior to NMP. Outcomes were assessed in six included pairs using injury markers (GST-Pi, IL-18, extracellular cardiolipin), NMP assessment metrics (urine production, vascular resistance), and histological and perfusate markers of microthrombosis, with comparison to human trial samples. Kidneys exposed to the intervention produced more urine but had higher vascular resistance and showed more evidence of mitochondrial injury, with no improvement in damage markers that in our human trial were correlated with outcome. Standard NMP provided better flush-out of donor derived intravascular debris, however the overall pre-perfusion burden of microvascular thrombosis was unexpectedly low, which was supported by analysis of human trial samples. Staged reperfusion by this protocol did not demonstrate an advantage compared to direct NMP.

items.title: Outside Front Cover
Reply to 'Comment on “Effectiveness of respiratory syncytial virus vaccination in solid organ transplant recipients in the United States'
Graft Localized Immunomodulation with Rapamycin-Eluting PLGA Microparticles Promotes Murine Islet Allograft Survival and Induces Operational Tolerance
items.abstract: Islet transplantation effectively restores physiologic glycemic regulation in a subset of individuals living with type 1 diabetes; however, lifelong systemic immunosuppression remains a major barrier to broader patient inclusion. Herein, we explored the use of a localized drug delivery system to preserve islet allograft function, circumventing systemic immunosuppression. Rapamycin (Rapa) was effectively encapsulated within poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) microparticles (MP), which facilitated sustained and localized drug release to the islet grafts, modulating the immune environment and significantly prolonging allograft survival (p<0.05). Long-term outcomes were further enhanced when Rapa-MP was combined with low-dose, acute systemic CTLA-4-Ig therapy. Combination therapy induced operational tolerance, with 100% allograft survival for more than 200 days. Our localized MP drug delivery system, whether used as monotherapy or as part of combination therapy, has the potential to favourably modulate the immune environment, protect islet grafts, and serve as a safe adjuvant to clinical islet transplantation.

items.title: Lower waitlist failure without loss of transplant or exception access after the 2023 pediatric liver allocation update: a national interrupted time-series study
items.abstract: The 2023 Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network pediatric medical urgency update revised the Pediatric End-Stage Liver Disease (PELD) calculation, pediatric Status 1A/1B rules, and National Liver Review Board guidance. Using registry data linked to exception records, we performed an interrupted time-series analysis among candidates younger than 12 years listed from January 2019 through December 2024, excluding June-July 2023 as the implementation interval (2,791 registrations; 368,761 person-days). The primary outcome was waitlist death or delisting for clinical deterioration. The update was not associated with an immediate change in this outcome (incidence rate ratio [IRR], 1.19; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.57-2.46), but was associated with a lower post-policy trajectory (slope-change IRR, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.89-0.99; P=0.047). This association attenuated when severity was measured identically in both eras (IRR, 0.96; 95% CI, 0.90-1.01; P=0.14). Removal for death was unchanged (0.21 vs 0.20 per 1,000 person-days), whereas removal as too sick to transplant fell (0.21 vs 0.09). Transplant rates, exception request rates, and exception approval probability did not decline. The update was associated with lower severity-adjusted waitlist death/delisting without detectable loss of transplant or exception access; however, era-invariant severity adjustment and component analyses indicate that the magnitude and mechanism of this association remain uncertain.

items.title: Single-Port Robotic Extraperitoneal Donor Nephrectomy: Technique and Initial Case Series
items.abstract: Minimally invasive donor nephrectomy is the gold standard for reducing donor morbidity, yet transperitoneal approaches carry inherent risks. The extraperitoneal approach offers a potentially safer alternative. We present our initial experience with Single-Port Robotic Extraperitoneal Donor Nephrectomy (SP-REDN), a novel technique utilizing the da Vinci SP system to navigate the retroperitoneal space through a single 5-cm incision that serves as both the operative port and the graft extraction site. Between September 2025 and March 2026, 13 living donors underwent SP-REDN. Five donors (38.5%) had a history of prior abdominal surgery. Our technique utilizes a muscle-sparing anterior rectus sheath incision in supine position. Mean operative time was 180.5 minutes (SD 42.9), with a mean WIT of 6.2 minutes (SD 6.7). There were no open conversions or immediate complications, and the median hospital stay was 2.0 days (IQR 1.0-2.0). This series demonstrates that SP-REDN has the potential to optimize both donor safety and experience by avoiding peritoneal violation and offering a single-incision approach.

items.title: Impact of the Safety-Net Kidney-After-Heart Transplant Policy on Simultaneous Heart-Kidney Transplant Volume and Outcomes in the United States
items.abstract: On 6/29/2023, the Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network (OPTN) implemented a safety-net policy providing priority kidney transplant (KT) listing status to heart transplant (HT) recipients who develop persistent kidney dysfunction within one year of HT, with the intent of incentivizing isolated HT over simultaneous heart-kidney transplantation (sHKT) in patients with potentially reversible kidney dysfunction. The impact of this policy on sHKT utilization and post-transplant outcomes is unknown. We used interrupted time series analysis of quarterly sHKT volume and compared one-year mortality and kidney graft failure between pre- and post-policy sHKT recipients using multivariable Cox models. In this OPTN registry analysis of HTs performed from 1/1/2020-12/31/2025, among 21,688 HT recipients, 1,133 pre-policy and 877 post-policy recipients underwent sHKT, and 183 received a safety-net KT. We found that 1) following policy implementation, the quarterly change in slope of sHKT utilization was -4.45 procedures per quarter (95% CI -5.94, -2.95), with a concurrent rise in safety-net KT of 2.52 per quarter (95% CI 1.44, 3.59), 2) mortality and kidney graft failure were similar among sHKT recipients post- vs pre-policy implementation (hazard ratio [HR] 0.94, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.68, 1.29 and HR 0.91, 95% CI 0.67, 1.24, respectively).

items.title: Induction immunosuppression in kidney transplant recipients treated with early corticosteroid cessation: A propensity score case-matched analysis
items.abstract: Early corticosteroid cessation is recommended for low immune risk kidney transplant recipients, but the optimal induction immunosuppression is uncertain. We compared the outcomes of 4,770 first kidney only transplant recipients in the U.S. between 2010 and 2022 treated with tacrolimus and mycophenolate without corticosteroids induced with interleukin-2 receptor antagonists (IL-2Ra) to a matched cohort induced with anti-thymocyte globulin rabbit ( Thymoglobulin.) Only 13% of patients treated with early corticosteroid cessation were induced with IL-2Ra and these patients were more likely to be older and have diabetes. After 1:1 matching, patients treated with IL-2Ra had a higher adjusted risk of allograft loss from any cause (Hazard Ratio (HR) = 1.20, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.12 to 1.29), death with allograft function (HR = 1.20, 95% CI 1.10 to 1.31), and allograft loss with death as a competing risk (sub hazard ratio SHR = 1.20, 95% CI 1.04 to 1.38). We conclude that IL-2RA induction is selectively used in older, sicker patients but is associated with a higher risk of transplant failure compared to matched patients treated with Thymoglobulin. The findings highlight the need for prospective trials to define optimal induction in patients who may benefit most for early corticosteroid cessation.

items.title: Combined Rituximab and Daratumumab Induces Remission in Refractory Post-Transplant Crescentic IgA Nephropathy
items.abstract: Recurrent crescentic IgA nephropathy (IgAN) after kidney transplantation is rare, aggressive, and often refractory to standard immunosuppression. We report a 17-year-old recipient with biopsy-confirmed recurrent crescentic IgAN two years after transplantation despite corticosteroids and targeted-release budesonide. Rescue therapy comprised one rituximab infusion with daratumumab, followed by four daratumumab infusions. Proteinuria decreased from 5.21 to 0.06 g/g, serum albumin normalized, and allograft function remained stable through day 482 after the first rescue infusion. Longitudinal CyTOF and flow cytometry showed sustained peripheral B-cell depletion and transient NK-cell reductions. One mild upper respiratory infection occurred. Sequential biopsies showed resolution of the active cellular crescent, although mesangial IgA staining and electron-dense deposits persisted. These clinical, histologic, and immune changes were temporally associated with combined CD20- and CD38-targeted therapy. This single case cannot establish efficacy, distinguish the contributions of rituximab and daratumumab, or exclude effects of preceding and supportive treatments, but supports further study of this rescue approach.

items.title: Landscape Of Post-Donation Follow-up of Living Kidney Donors in the United States, 2013-2023
items.abstract: Post-donation follow-up is critical for living kidney donor (LKD) care, facilitating early detection of unusual decrease in renal function and providing opportunities for early intervention. Herein, we update and characterize temporal trends in LKD follow-up (LDF) using Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network data. We identified 64,488 LKDs (2/2013-12/2023) and used logistic regression to assess donor characteristics associated with complete and timely (defined per current OPTN policy) LDF at 6-months, 1-year and 2-years post-donation. The proportion of complete and timely LDF submissions was generally consistent since 2013 for clinical and laboratory data at each time point. Overall, complete and timely 6-month, 1-year, and 2-year LDF were 84%, 81% and 75% for clinical data, and 80%, 75% and 68% for laboratory data. Across all time points, LKDs with pre-donation BMI≥30, Black race, and of younger age had higher odds of incomplete follow-up. We also observed substantial center-level variation, with the proportion of transplant centers meeting 6-month LDF thresholds ranging from 56-81% each year. In this retrospective registry analysis, LDF remained suboptimal and varied by center and donor characteristics, demonstrating the need for targeted approaches to improve LDF, particularly among those at increased risk of kidney disease or facing barriers to care.

items.title: Reevaluation of the role of HBsAg testing in deceased tissue and cornea donor eligibility determination
items.abstract: The utility of hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) testing in deceased tissue and cornea donor eligibility screening is uncertain in the era of concurrent hepatitis B virus (HBV) nucleic acid testing (NAT) and hepatitis B core total antibody (anti-HBc) screening. We performed an analysis of 300,112 deceased tissue and cornea donors. screened for eligibility between January 2021 and May 2026. Donors were screened for HBV NAT, HBsAg, and anti-HBc; results were analyzed to characterize HBV screening profiles and evaluate the incremental yield of HBsAg reactivity among donors with nonreactive NAT results. Overall, 97.02% of donors (n=291,180) had HBsAg-nonreactive/HBV NAT-nonreactive results and 0.11% (n=318) of donors had HBsAg-reactive/HBV NAT-reactive results. In 0.57% of donors (n=1,697) HBsAg-nonreactive/HBV NAT-reactive results were obtained and 2.30% of donors (n=6,917) were HBsAg-reactive/HBV NAT-nonreactive. Among HBsAg-reactive/HBV NAT-nonreactive donors, 97.79% (n=6,764) were also anti-HBc-nonreactive. HBsAg testing identified 22.5 additional reactive screening results (per 1,000 donors) among donors without HBV NAT and anti-HBc reactivity. A subset of reactive HBsAg specimens were evaluated by supplemental confirmatory testing (n=1,131); only 17.28% were confirmed reactive. In this cohort, HBsAg testing identified potential donors for whom the biological significance of HBsAg reactivity remains uncertain, and current eligibility requirements result in donor exclusion.

items.title: CD154 Blockade Improves Polyfunctionality of T Cells Specific for a Murine Homolog of Epstein-Barr Virus
items.abstract: Anti-CD154 is a promising therapeutic for solid organ transplantation with ongoing clinical trials, but its impact on the immune response to EBV is unknown. Here, B6 animals were infected with a murine homolog of EBV (MHV68) and treated with anti-CD154 costimulation blockade. Results indicate that the ratio of virus-specific CD8 + T cells to MHV68-infected cells was not significantly reduced following in vivo anti-CD154. Interestingly, frequencies of multi-cytokine producing CD4 + and CD8 + T cells were increased following treatment with anti-CD154 compared to either CTLA4-Ig or tacrolimus. This increased polyfunctionality was mechanistically underpinned by an increase in the frequency of CD8 + T cells expressing the memory/stem-like transcription factors TCF-1 and Eomes in the anti-CD154 group compared to CTLA-4Ig, tacrolimus, or untreated controls. Moreover, anti-CD154-treated mice exhibited smaller spleens with a significant decrease in the number of MHV68-YFP + germinal center B cells compared to untreated mice. These data demonstrate that CD154 blockade does not significantly decrease the ratio of virus-specific T cells to infected cells and increases the quality of MHV68-specific CD8 + T cells in a mouse model. Overall, these findings suggest that an anti-CD154 costimulation blockade-based immunosuppression regimen may be beneficial regarding its ability to preserve protective anti-viral immunity during transplantation.

items.title: CD8 T cell phenotype diagnoses graft-versus-host disease after liver transplantation
items.abstract: Graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) is a rare but highly fatal complication following liver transplantation (LT). While donor T cell chimerism is a specific diagnostic indicator, its detection via short tandem repeat (STR) analysis is compromised in LT-GVHD. Here, peripheral blood from nine patients diagnosed with LT-GVHD by STR chimerism or histopathology was analyzed using HLA-specific antibody-based flow cytometry for simultaneous donor T cell chimerism and immunophenotyping. Flow cytometry detected macrochimerism in all patients, including three with negative leukocyte STR results. All patients exhibited lymphocytopenia, with the three cases specifically exhibiting significantly elevated granulocyte-to-lymphocyte ratios, suggesting donor DNA dilution by recipient granulocytes underlies STR false-negatives. Donor-derived CD8 + T cells were predominant and exhibited a TEM-biased phenotype with heightened proliferation, activation, exhaustion, and cytotoxicity compared to GVHD recipient-derived T cells or non-GVHD donor-derived T cells. This immunophenotypic signature was readily detectable within the total CD8 + TEM population, allowing Ki-67-based diagnosis without requiring HLA-specific antibodies. Its diagnostic relevance was further confirmed in an independent external cohort. We conclude that lymphocyte enrichment is essential for reliable STR-based chimerism detection in LT-GVHD. HLA-specific flow cytometry or Ki-67 assessment on total CD8 + TEM cells offers a practical alternative tailored to the lymphopenia context of LT-GVHD.

items.title: Varied trajectories through the transplant evaluation process: Results of a sequence analysis among a national cohort of Veterans with advanced kidney disease
items.abstract: Efforts to improve access to kidney transplant are limited by an incomplete view on the full arc of the evaluation process. We performed a retrospective cohort study among 39,691 adults receiving care within the US Veterans Affairs Health Care System (VA) with incident advanced kidney disease (eGFR≤20 mL/min/1.73 m 2 ) between 10/1/2011 and 12/31/2018. We used sequence analysis to describe sequential steps in the transplant process over 5 years of follow-up. Cohort members' median age at cohort entry was 70.1 (IQR 63.9, 80.2) years and 97.2% were men. Sequence analysis yielded 7 distinct trajectories through the transplant process: 1) early death (50.5%), 2) transplant not mentioned (24.6%), 3) not pursuing transplant (6.2%), 4) prolonged deliberation (4.6%), 5) prolonged evaluation (8.9%), 6) timely waitlisting (3.3%), and 7) timely transplant (1.9%). Older age, higher comorbidity index, and higher area deprivation index were associated with a lower likelihood of experiencing trajectories representing timely progression through the transplant process and a greater likelihood of not engaging with the process or spending prolonged periods of time in early steps. Our findings suggest that current efforts to encourage broader referral for transplant should be complemented by a more streamlined evaluation process and support for shared decision-making.

items.title: Risk Assessment for Transmission of Porcine Endogenous Retrovirus in Clinical Xenotransplantation
items.abstract: Porcine to human xenotransplantation clinical trials are underway. Concerns remain regarding potential transmission of infections including porcine endogenous retroviruses (PERVs) to human xenotransplant recipients with adverse health outcomes. All pigs contain subtypes PERV-A and PERV-B, and some also carry PERV-C. Human cells carry receptors for PERV-A and -B but not for PERV-C. PERV-A can recombine with PERV-B to form PERV-A/B hybrids and recombine with PERV-C to form PERV-A/C hybrids in vivo and in vitro. No evidence of PERV transmission to non-human primates or other laboratory animals, human primary cells, or to humans from surgical or non-surgical exposures has been reported, although transmission of PERV A/C hybrids has been observed in certain permissive transformed human cell lines. PERV inactivation has been achieved via genetic editing in some pig lines. Here, we review the data related to the potential for PERV infection in human xenograft recipients based on published data on PERV structure and host cellular and species tropisms. Despite the lack of evidence regarding transmissibility of PERVs to humans, we advocate the rigorous monitoring of patients and, possibly, their close contacts in initial clinical trials for possible PERV transmission following xenotransplantation.

items.title: Targeted inhibition of Bcl6 effectively suppresses alloactivation of CD4+ T cells with potential for T cell-directed immunosuppression
items.abstract: Bcl6 is a key transcriptional repressor regulating T cell fate; however, its role in T cell alloimmune responses is largely unknown. We investigated Bcl6 expression in T cells within allografts and the potential of targeting Bcl6 to modulate CD4 + T cell alloactivation. Using mIFISH, we found that Bcl6 + CD4 + T cells were highly prevalent in kidney transplant biopsies during rejection. In mixed lymphocyte reactions, pharmacological Bcl6 inhibition (Bcl6i) potently suppressed proliferation and effector cytokine production of human CD4 + T cells in a dose-dependent manner. Acting in PBMC and isolated T cell subsets alike, Bcl6i effects were direct, T cell-specific and irrespective of T cell differentiation state. Gene expression and flow cytometry showed Bcl6i reshaped T cell fate by altering key transcriptional programs. Bcl6i suppressed Th1, Th2 and Th17 transcription factors and upregulated TCF1. In addition, T cell inhibitory receptor TIGIT was up- and costimulatory receptor ICOS downregulated. Importantly, we validated the response to Bcl6i in donor-reactive CD4 + T cells from kidney transplant patients, highlighting the translational potential of Bcl6 as a target for T cell-directed immunosuppression in transplantation.

items.title: Governance Before Technology: Building Japan’s National Pathway for Controlled Donation After Circulatory Death
How I Do It: Recurrent IgA Nephropathy After Transplant—Integrating Emerging Therapies Into Practice
Combination of Serum Leucine-rich Alpha-2-Glycoprotein 1 and Citrulline as Biomarkers of Graft Monitoring and Response to Antirejection Treatment in Intestinal Transplantation
items.abstract: Background. Intestinal transplantation (ITx) has the highest rejection rate among solid organ transplantations. Nevertheless, convenient, reliable, and noninvasive biomarkers for rejection surveillance are lacking. Leucine-rich alpha-2-glycoprotein 1 (LRG-1) has been developed as a new serum biomarker of disease activity in numerous gastrointestinal inflammatory pathologies. Therefore, this study aimed to evaluate the utility of serum LRG-1 as a biomarker for predicting post-ITx rejection, using citrulline as a known marker. Methods. Serum LRG-1 (n = 77) and citrulline (n = 64) samples were obtained from 5 post-ITx patients. We analyzed the correlation between these serum levels and the “villi appearance, erythema, capillary network, crypt widening, and heterogeneity (VENCH)” score according to the endoscopic findings of the intestinal graft evaluated on the same day as serum sample collection, as well as histopathological diagnosis. Results. We observed a negative correlation between serum LRG-1 and citrulline levels. LRG-1 values in the VENCH score ≥4 group were significantly higher than those in the VENCH <4 group ( P < 0.0001). The area under the curve of the citrulline/LRG-1 (C/L) ratio for detecting endoscopic abnormalities was 0.896 (sensitivity: 0.87; specificity: 0.89). In addition, LRG-1 values in the pathological rejection group were significantly higher than those in the nonrejection group ( P < 0.0001). The area under the curve of the C/L ratio for detecting rejection was 0.992 (sensitivity: 1.0; specificity: 0.94). Conclusions. The present data support the hypothesis that LRG-1 is an attractive noninvasive biomarker of rejection after ITx, especially as an indicator, such as the C/L ratio. Routine serum LRG-1 monitoring may help to reduce the frequency of invasive endoscopic surveillance.

items.title: Glucagon-like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists in Heart Transplant Recipients With Type 2 Diabetes: A Multicenter Study
items.abstract: Background. Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is frequent after heart transplantation (HT) and is exacerbated by immunosuppressive therapy. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) may improve metabolic control, but data in HT recipients are limited. Methods. We performed a retrospective, multicenter study including HT recipients with T2DM from 14 Spanish centers. In patients treated with GLP-1 RAs, we assessed antidiabetic and immunosuppressive therapies, adverse events, and changes in metabolic parameters, insulin dose, and immunosuppressant trough levels during the first year after GLP-1 RA initiation. Results. Among 734 HT recipients with T2DM (2011–2021), 108 (14.7%) received GLP-1 RAs (mean age 55.4 ± 9.0 y; 79.6% male), initiated 4.0 ± 3.1 y post-HT. At baseline, 64.8% had obesity. Semaglutide was used in 59%, dulaglutide in 27%, liraglutide in 13%, and tirzepatide in 1%; 41.7% achieved the maximum therapeutic dose. After 1 y, significant reductions were observed in body weight (–6.2 kg; 95% confidence interval [CI], –7.7 to –4.5 kg), fasting glucose (–27 mg/dL; 95% CI, –41 to –7 mg/dL), glycated hemoglobin (–0.74%; 95% CI, –1.12% to –0.35%), total cholesterol (–12 mg/dL; 95% CI, –19 to –6 mg/dL), low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (–8 mg/dL; 95% CI, –14 to –2 mg/dL), triglycerides (–29 mg/dL; 95% CI, –53 to –5 mg/dL), and systolic blood pressure (–3.6 mm Hg; 95% CI, –6.4 to –0.9 mm Hg). Tacrolimus trough levels decreased modestly (–0.7 ng/mL; 95% CI, –1.4 to –0.1 ng/mL; P = 0.025), without episodes of acute rejection. Gastrointestinal adverse events occurred in 12.0%, leading to discontinuation in 3.7%. Conclusions. In HT recipients with T2DM, GLP-1 RAs were associated with improved glycemic and cardiometabolic parameters and were generally well tolerated. These findings support the use of GLP-1 RAs as a valuable therapeutic strategy for the management of T2DM after HT.

items.title: Incidence and Risk Factors of Hepatic Artery Thrombosis and Stenosis After Pediatric Liver Transplantation: Results From the HEPATIC Registry
items.abstract: Background. The incidence and risk factors of hepatic artery complications (HACs), including thrombosis (HAT) and stenosis (HAS), after pediatric liver transplantation (pLT) are not well characterized. This study aimed to assess the incidence and risk factors of HACs after pLT and quantify the screening effort required to identify a single HAC. Methods. We performed a retrospective multicenter analysis using the HEPATIC registry, including pLTs from 32 centers over a 20-y period. HAC incidence was assessed across subgroups defined by pLT indication, recipient age, donor type, transplant era, and annual center volume. Timing of HAC occurrence and the number needed to screen were analyzed. Results. Among 11 443 pLTs, HACs occurred in 4.8% (HAT 3.6%; HAS 1.2%). Most HACs developed within the first-month posttransplant (82.4%), with HAT peaking in the first 2 wk, whereas HAS was more evenly distributed. The overall incidence increased in 2012–2021 (5.3%), with rising HAS and stable HAT rates. Modifiable factors included living donor transplantation (3.4%) and high-volume centers (3.8%), both associated with lower HAC rates, whereas whole grafts in infants <1 y with biliary atresia (15.3%) were associated with higher incidence (all P < 0.001). Patient-related risk factors included retransplantation following previous HACs (11.3%) and noncirrhotic metabolic diseases (7.6%, both P < 0.001). The number needed to screen ranged from 173 to 1907 and was lower in high-risk groups. Conclusions. HACs occurred in 4.8% of pLTs, with recent increases driven by HAS. Infants <1 with biliary atresia receiving whole grafts and patients undergoing retransplantation after prior HACs were at the highest risk.

items.title: Beyond FEV1: Alveolar Nitric Oxide Within an Integrated, Noninvasive Model for CLAD Surveillance
items.abstract: Background. Chronic lung allograft dysfunction (CLAD) remains the major limitation to long-term survival after lung transplantation. Fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO) is a noninvasive marker of airway inflammation, but its clinical role after lung transplantation remains uncertain. This study investigated whether multiple-flow FeNO parameters may support CLAD risk stratification in lung transplant recipients. Methods. We performed a retrospective observational study of 114 lung transplant recipients. At the time of FeNO assessment, 45 patients had CLAD, 9 had acute cellular rejection, and 60 were clinically stable. FeNO was assessed at multiple expiratory flows to derive proximal and distal nitric oxide parameters. Results. Alveolar nitric oxide concentration (CalvNO) was significantly higher in patients with CLAD than in clinically stable recipients and showed the best discrimination among FeNO-derived variables for prevalent CLAD (area under the curve [AUC], 0.849; optimal cutoff, 7.7 ppb). A model combining CalvNO, diffusing capacity of the lung for carbon monoxide, residual volume/total lung capacity, and forced expiratory volume in 1 s showed good diagnostic performance (AUC, 0.88). Among initially stable recipients, 9 developed CLAD during follow-up. Baseline CalvNO was associated with incident CLAD in exploratory time-to-event analysis (hazard ratio, 1.35 per 1 ppb increase), with an AUC of 0.889 and a cutoff of 7.12 ppb. Microbiological status modified FeNO interpretation, particularly for proximal indices, whereas CalvNO remained more consistently associated with CLAD in colonized and microbiologically negative patients. Conclusions. Multiple-flow FeNO-derived CalvNO is a biologically plausible and clinically promising noninvasive biomarker for CLAD risk stratification. Its most defensible application is as part of integrated surveillance combining FeNO-derived parameters, pulmonary function, lung volumes, diffusion capacity, and structured assessment of infection or other reversible conditions.

items.title: Cell Therapy Protocol Recommendations (Liver) From the Salzburg Regulatory Cell Therapy in Organ Transplantation Expert Meeting
Beyond Abstinence: How Integrated Multidisciplinary Management Improves Long-term Post Liver Transplant Outcomes
items.abstract: Background. Alcohol-associated liver disease is the leading indication for liver transplantation (LT). We assessed long-term alcohol relapse after LT within a program using an integrated multidisciplinary team for relapse monitoring and prevention before and after transplantation, without requiring a predefined abstinence period. Methods. In 2018, we established a prospective program in which all patients with associated liver disease were evaluated and followed before and after LT by a multidisciplinary team embedded within the transplant program. We reviewed long-term outcomes as part of this program between 2018 and 2023. Results. A total of 165 recipients were transplanted since the inception of the program. Posttransplant alcohol relapse occurred in 21 patients (12.7%), of whom 57.1% had mild alcohol consumption, 4.8% moderate, and 33.3% severe. Median time to relapse was 9.4 mo (5.9–30.2). Ethyl glucuronide positivity confirmed relapse in 20 of 21 patients, and 17 endorsed alcohol use. All patients had access to addiction psychiatry follow-up and relapse prevention therapy embedded within their posttransplant care. Those who relapsed were offered intensification of relapse prevention therapy and 16/21 engaged in regular follow-up. Only 6 patients (3.6%) reported ongoing alcohol consumption at last follow-up, while all others reestablished abstinence. No significant differences in outcomes were observed between groups. No alcohol-related deaths or graft losses occurred. Conclusions. A multidisciplinary fully integrated team along with individualized approach to candidate evaluation with follow-up pre- and post-LT is critical to successful outcomes and results in a much lower rate of relapse at long-term post-LT.

items.title: The Benefit of Modulating Costimulatory Signals to Boost Transplant Survival: Hitting two Birds With one Stone?
MASLD Liver Transplant: Evolution of Frequency, Age Trends, and Factors Associated With Outcomes
items.abstract: Background. Metabolic dysfunction–associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) has rapidly emerged as a leading indication for liver transplantation (LT) in the United States. There remains a need to understand the evolution of transplant volumes and recipient profiles and outcomes. In this study, we aim to analyze current MASLD LT trends to aid in identifying opportunities for this patient population. Methods. We analyzed UNOS data for primary liver transplants (2010–2024), identifying MASLD by diagnosis codes and stratifying transplants into three eras (2010–2014, 2015–2019, and 2020–2024). Analyses included annual MASLD transplant counts and proportions, era-specific annual percent change, comparisons of donor, operative, and recipient characteristics, Kaplan–Meier curves, multivariable Cox regression for overall post-LT mortality, and competing-risk regression for waitlist outcomes. Results. In total, 18 153 MASLD LT recipients were included (Era 1: 2734; Era 2: 6127; Era 3: 9292). Annual MASLD LT volume increased from 461 in 2010 to 2090 in 2024. Annual percent change was +10.6% (Era 1), +20.1% (Era 2), and +5.9% (Era 3). In Era 3, recipients were as young as 8 y. Era 3 waitlist candidates had significantly higher likelihood of transplant (sHR 1.52; 95% CI, 1.46–1.58) and lower risk of waitlist mortality (sHR 0.44; 95% CI, 0.40–0.48). Recipient survival increased from 97.0% to 98.3% at 30 d, and 90.5% to 92.6% at 1 y (both P < 0.01). Conclusions. From 2010 to 2024, MASLD LT rose markedly but relative growth plateaued. Increasing age diversity, including pediatric recipients, highlights the need for earlier recognition and optimized management.

items.title: Beyond Conventional Immunosuppression: Targeting the Peptidylprolyl Isomerase A-CD147 Axis in Porcine Cardiac Xenotransplantation
Analysis of Preformed Anti-DQα Donor-specific Antibodies in the Context of the Intact HLA-DQ Heterodimer
From Ischemic Thresholds to Dynamic Assessment: How NRP Is revolutionizing DCD Liver Transplantation
Building a National Heart Transplant Program in the United Arab Emirates: Organization, Challenges, and Lessons Learned
A Review: Handbook of Clinical Transplantation. Editor: Gabriel M. Danovitch
Uterus Transplant Living Donor Evaluation and Selection: An Approach to Optimizing Donor and Recipient Outcomes
items.abstract: Background. Since the first live birth from uterus transplantation (UTx) in 2014, there has been an ever-growing interest in the technique from patients and transplant programs worldwide. The Dallas UTx program first reported a live birth in the United States in 2017 and has subsequently completed 40 transplants with a living-donor–predominant approach. To date, the published scientific literature has focused on recipient and newborn outcomes, with relatively limited discussion surrounding living donor evaluation. Methods. The aim of this study was to describe the methodology, evolution, and outcomes from living donor evaluation at the Dallas UTx program. Results. Over a 9-y period, 1329 women volunteered for living donation evaluation. A total of 72 women proceeded to full evaluation, with 38 deemed eligible (37 nondirected donation, 97%). Six women withdrew following evaluation, and 28 were deemed ineligible. Thirteen were declined for vasculature concerns (the main reason for exclusion), and 8 because of other abnormalities found on imaging. Two potential candidates were deemed ineligible because of medical comorbidities, and a further 3 on psychological evaluation. An additional 2 candidates were ineligible following committee review. Twenty-seven (68%) recipients have delivered a child, 4 have delivered 2 children, and 6 are currently pregnant. Conclusions. Successful living donor UTx requires thorough donor evaluation. Favorable donor, recipient, and newborn outcomes were observed within the context of this comprehensive donor evaluation and selection process.

items.title: Reply: Addressing the Role of Glucagon-like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists in Liver Transplant Recipients
Offered Deceased Donor Kidneys With Little or No Chance of Being Transplanted
items.abstract: Background. With a broadening deceased donor pool and recent allocation policy changes, US transplant programs have reported challenges managing an influx of suboptimal kidney offers. We hypothesized that the number of offered kidneys with a minuscule chance of being transplanted has risen. If so, targeted innovations may be needed to reduce administrative burden and improve system efficiency. Methods. Using Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network data on kidneys offered in 2016–2024, we developed a multivariable model to predict the probability that an offered kidney was transplanted (PrTx). We examined trends in the number and proportion of offered kidneys having PrTx ≤2%, ≤5%, and ≤10%. Results. Donor factors most predictive of PrTx were age, donation after circulatory death, serum creatinine (terminal, peak, nadir), presence and duration of diabetes and hypertension, infectious disease test results, and body mass index. From 2016 to 2024, the annual number of kidneys offered with PrTx ≤2%, PrTx ≤5%, and PrTx ≤10% increased 13-fold (from 18 to 236), 12-fold (84 to 1055), and 10-fold (299 to 2856), respectively. Of the 236 offered kidneys with PrTx ≤2% in 2024, none was transplanted. The 2856 kidneys with PrTx ≤10% accounted for 7.9% (n = 1 208 883) of manually refused offers but just 1.1% (n = 239) of transplanted kidneys. Organ procurement organizations and centers varied substantially in offering and transplanting low-PrTx kidneys. Conclusions. The number of offered kidneys with extremely low predicted transplant probability has risen sharply, most notably in 2024. Innovations, such as improved offer filtering capabilities and standardized expedited allocation pathways, are needed to improve kidney placement efficiency.

items.title: Research Highlights
Incidence and Risk Factors for Early Major Neurologic Complications in Lung Transplantation: From Restrictive Cardiopulmonary Bypass to ECMO by Criteria
items.abstract: Background. Intraoperative hemodynamic instability and hypoxemia may contribute to early major neurologic complications (EMNC) following lung transplantation. Mechanical circulatory support can mitigate cerebral hypoperfusion, but cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) is an independent risk factor for EMNC. This study examines the incidence of EMNC transitioning from a restrictive CPB strategy to criteria-based use of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO-BC). Methods. We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study on 389 lung transplant recipients comparing patients managed with restrictive CPB (PRE-ECMO, 2012–2017, n = 288) to those managed with criteria-based ECMO (ECMO-BC, 2022–2024, n = 101). The incidence of EMNC was compared between groups. Results. EMNC occurred in 29 of 280 patients in the PRE-ECMO group and in 5 of 101 patients in the ECMO-BC group (10% versus 5%; P = 0.152), with 78 versus 8 total events, corresponding to an incidence rate ratio of 3.5 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.7-7.4, P < 0.001). Ischemic stroke was significantly less frequent in the ECMO-BC group (2% versus 9%; P = 0.022). Intraoperative mechanical circulatory support was used in 20% of PRE-ECMO and 43% of ECMO-BC cases ( P < 0.001). Patients in the ECMO-BC group were older, had more cardiopulmonary comorbidities, greater intraoperative blood loss (2489 versus 1861 cc; P < 0.001), and more severe primary graft dysfunction at 24 and 72 h ( P < 0.001). Conclusions. Transition to ECMO-BC was associated with lower EMNC events and fewer ischemic strokes, but increased intraoperative blood loss and worse early graft function, generating hypotheses for prospective studies that define optimal ECMO indications in lung transplantation.

items.title: Prognostic Significance of Early Donor-derived Cell-free DNA Trajectories After Kidney Transplantation
items.abstract: Background. Early post-transplant elevations in donor-derived cell-free DNA are often attributed to ischemia–reperfusion injury, with uncertain prognostic significance. We assessed whether donor-derived cell-free DNA (dd-cfDNA) results during the first 4 mo post-transplantation are associated with long-term graft outcomes. Methods. We analyzed 1137 kidney transplant recipients enrolled in the prospective multicenter Kidney Outcomes AlloSure Registry. Recipients were categorized into 4 trajectory groups based on dd-cfDNA measurements obtained within the first 4 mo post-transplant: consistently low, transient-elevation, late-elevation, and persistent-elevation. Associations with donor-specific antibody (DSA) development, rejection, graft dysfunction, and graft loss were evaluated over 3 y using hazard regression, with multivariable models adjusted for calculated Panel Reactive Antibody (cPRA) and retransplant. Results. Among the 1137 recipients, 83.7% exhibited consistently low dd-cfDNA, 9.8% transient-elevation, 3.2% late-elevation, and 3.3% persistent-elevation. Late elevation was associated with the highest cumulative incidence of DSA development, whereas persistent-elevation had the highest incidence of rejection, graft dysfunction, and graft loss. Graft loss occurred in 20.0% of recipients with persistent-elevation and 8.8% with late-elevation and was uncommon among consistently low (2.2%) and transient (2.9%) groups. On multivariable analysis, late elevation was independently associated with DSA development, rejection, and graft loss, and persistent-elevation with rejection, graft dysfunction, and graft loss, regardless of prior transplantation or sensitization status. Conclusions. Early dd-cfDNA trajectories stratify kidney transplant recipients into clinically meaningful risk phenotypes. Persistent or late-emerging elevation identifies patients at independently increased risk of rejection and graft loss, with persistent-elevation also associated with graft dysfunction, supporting serial dd-cfDNA monitoring as a tool for early post-transplant risk stratification.

items.title: Response to the Letter to the Editor: “Donor and Recipient age in Liver Transplantation: Does Absolute age Matter More Than age Mismatch?”
Risk Factors for Posttransplant Lymphoproliferative Disorder in Children: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
items.abstract: Posttransplant lymphoproliferative disorder (PTLD) is the most frequent malignancy in pediatric patients following transplantation. This systematic review aimed to identify risk factors for PTLD in pediatric recipients of solid organ transplantation (SOT) and hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. Following PRISMA guidelines, a literature search was conducted in Medline, Embase, and Cochrane databases for studies published up to August 2025. Study characteristics were extracted, and data on potential risk factors were collected when available. Methodological quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale for observational studies. Meta-analyses were performed when feasible. Of 4917 records identified, 80 studies were included. Among the investigated variables, negative recipient Epstein–Barr virus (EBV) serology before transplantation emerged as the most significant risk factor for PTLD. The pooled relative risk for PTLD in EBV-seronegative SOT recipients was 3.35 (95% confidence intervals, 2.43–4.60), and this association remained consistent across organ-specific subgroups. Additional variables, such as demographic characteristics, EBV viral load, immunosuppressive therapy, and rejection episodes, showed discordant results across studies, likely reflecting limited data and methodological heterogeneity. Negative pretransplant EBV serology is confirmed as a major risk factor for PTLD in pediatric transplant recipients. Moreover, the findings of this review provide a comprehensive synthesis of the available evidence regarding risk factors of PTLD in pediatric recipients of both SOT and hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, highlighting the need for further large-scale studies to clarify additional determinants.

items.title: Serum Periostin at 1 y Is Associated With Subsequent Chronic Lung Allograft Dysfunction After Lung Transplantation: A Multicenter Validation Study
items.abstract: Background. Chronic lung allograft dysfunction (CLAD) remains the leading cause of late morbidity and mortality after lung transplantation, yet clinically useful biomarkers capable of identifying recipients at risk before overt functional decline are lacking. We previously identified serum periostin as a potential biomarker associated with bronchiolitis obliterans syndrome in a single-center cohort. Methods. In this multicenter validation study, we analyzed prospectively biobanked serum samples from the Korean Organ Transplant Registry. Serum periostin, transforming growth factor-beta 1, and interleukin-13 were measured in samples obtained 1 y after lung transplantation. Time-to-event analyses were landmarked at the 1-y biomarker measurement to evaluate associations with subsequent CLAD development. Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for prespecified clinical covariates were used. A periostin cutoff derived from the prior discovery cohort (66.2 ng/mL) was prespecified for validation. Results. Among 202 lung transplant recipients who survived to 1 y, 33 (16.3%) developed CLAD during follow-up. One-year periostin levels were significantly higher in recipients who developed CLAD than in those who remained CLAD-free (84.4 [73.0-114.6] versus 38.2 [26.6-54.3] ng/mL; P < 0.001). In multivariable analyses, higher periostin levels remained associated with increased CLAD risk (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.26 per SD increase; 95% confidence interval, 1.08-1.47; P = 0.003). The prespecified periostin cutoff effectively stratified CLAD-free survival. Conclusions. Serum periostin levels measured 1 y after lung transplantation were associated with subsequent CLAD development. These findings support serum periostin as a clinically informative biomarker for risk stratification among lung transplant recipients who survive the early posttransplant period.

items.title: Mechanotransduction Reshapes Epithelial Fate in Lung Ischemia/Reperfusion Injury Through Piezo1-dependent Calcium Signaling
items.abstract: Background. Lung ischemia/reperfusion injury (IRI) remains a major cause of primary graft dysfunction after lung transplantation. Although oxidative stress and inflammation are well-established contributors, the role of biomechanical stress and mechanotransduction in lung IRI has not been fully elucidated. Methods. Public transcriptomic datasets were integrated for differential expression and functional enrichment analyses. Cross-referencing with mechanosensitive ion channel genes identified 5 candidates associated with lung IRI, with Piezo-type mechanosensitive ion channel component 1 (Piezo1) prioritized following independent dataset validation. Rat lung transplantation and in vitro oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) models were used to investigate the role of Piezo1 in lung IRI. Piezo1 expression, epithelial injury, calcium accumulation, mitochondrial membrane potential, and apoptosis were evaluated. Genetic knockdown and pharmacological modulation of Piezo1 were performed to determine its functional role. Results. Piezo1 was identified as a mechanosensitive gene associated with lung IRI and was increased following reperfusion. In transplanted lungs, increased Piezo1 expression was accompanied by pulmonary epithelial apoptosis. In human bronchial epithelial cells, OGD/R induced Piezo1 upregulation, intracellular calcium overload, mitochondrial membrane depolarization, and apoptosis. Piezo1 silencing or inhibition alleviated calcium accumulation, preserved mitochondrial membrane potential, reduced apoptotic signaling, and improved cell viability, whereas pharmacological activation of Piezo1 with Yoda1 partially restored the OGD/R-induced injury phenotype in Piezo1-knockdown cells. Conclusions. This study suggests Piezo1 as a potential mechanosensitive regulator of pulmonary epithelial injury during lung IRI, linking biomechanical stress to calcium overload, mitochondrial dysfunction, and apoptosis. Targeting Piezo1-mediated mechanotransduction may represent a potential therapeutic strategy for mitigating graft injury after lung transplantation.

items.title: The Impact of the Modified Kidney Donor Profile Index on the Nonuse of Kidneys From Donors With Hepatitis C
items.abstract: Background. Donor hepatitis C virus (HCV) status was removed from the Kidney Donor Profile Index (KDPI) in October 2024 to better align the score with contemporary outcomes. Little is known about patterns in nonuse and utilization of HCV-exposed kidneys following this revision. Methods. We analyzed Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network data for 145 425 deceased donor kidneys recovered for transplantation between January 2020 and June 2025. Donor HCV status was categorized as nucleic acid test (NAT) + , NAT − /antibody (Ab) + , or NAT − /Ab − . Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for donor characteristics was used to evaluate kidney nonuse. Multinomial logistic regression adjusted for donor and recipient characteristics was used to assess donor HCV status among transplanted kidneys. Results. Through 2024, kidneys from both NAT + and NAT − /Ab + donors had higher adjusted odds of nonuse than NAT − /Ab − kidneys. In early 2025, NAT + kidneys had their lowest observed adjusted odds ratio (aOR) of nonuse during the study period but remained significantly higher than NAT − /Ab − kidneys (aOR, 1.30; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.01-1.67), whereas NAT − /Ab + kidneys attenuated to nonsignificance (aOR, 1.19; 95% CI, 0.84-1.72). Despite increased candidate willingness to accept both NAT + and NAT − /Ab + kidneys from 2020 to 2025, the odds of transplanting NAT + compared with NAT − /Ab − kidneys did not increase after the KDPI revision (aOR, 0.99; 95% CI, 0.88-1.12). However, transplanting NAT − /Ab + kidneys increased (aOR, 1.27; 95% CI, 1.13-1.43). Conclusions. Removal of HCV from the KDPI equation has improved utilization of NAT − /Ab + kidneys, whereas NAT + kidneys continued to experience excess nonuse despite rising candidate willingness to accept HCV-exposed kidneys.

items.title: Mental Health, Disorders and Symptoms in Living Donors: Where are Areas for Improvement?
items.abstract: The success of living donor transplantation is a testament to the dedicated transplant clinicians and programs who make donor safety and wellbeing their utmost priority. From a psychosocial perspective, additional safeguards are provided by national and international organizations requiring a comprehensive psychosocial assessment by qualified professionals to identify and address any psychosocial issues, including mental health issues, that could complicate post-donation recovery. Overall, in carefully selected donor cohorts, the literature shows donor psychologic wellbeing and mental health, on average, is similar to or exceeds that reported in the general population. However, the literature also reveals clinically relevant higher-risk subgroups, a consistent pattern across liver and kidney donors of risk factors for poorer mental health outcomes: pre-donation characteristics and post-donation events and experiences related to donation. In this overview, we review the literature primarily from the past decade and also additionally use earlier key articles to highlight important mental health outcomes (eg, depression, anxiety). We focus on poorer mental health outcomes with the intent of learning how to improve pre-donation evaluation and post-donation care. We suggest ways to improve donor psychosocial assessments, consider strategies across the donation process that could be used to improve donor follow-up clinical care, and review donation-specific interventions. Closer follow-up of donors’ mental health after donation and interventions applied either before or following donation are important areas for future work.

items.title: Impact of Removing the Mandatory Sobriety Period on Waitlist and Posttransplant Outcomes of Patients With and Without Alcohol-associated Liver Disease
items.abstract: Background. This single-center study assessed the impact of eliminating the mandatory 6-mo sobriety requirement on waitlist and post-liver transplant (LT) outcomes among patients with and without alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD). Methods. Adult patients listed for LT from 2010 to 2023 and followed through 2025 were analyzed. Era 1 (<2018) required ≥6 mo of sobriety, whereas era 2 (≥2018) did not. Competing risk models compared waitlist outcomes across eras. Post-LT survival was compared across eras, followed by a subgroup analysis of era 2 ALD recipients stratified by pre-LT sobriety duration. Results. ALD listings increased (26% versus 42%), whereas non-ALD declined in era 2 (74% versus 58%). In era 2, listed ALD candidates had a higher likelihood of transplant (hazard ratio, 1.90; P < 0.001), lower likelihood of death/deterioration (hazard ratio, 0.48; P = 0.03), and shorter listing-to-LT time (204 versus 98 d; P = 0.004), whereas non-ALD likelihood of transplant, death/deterioration, and time-to-LT were unchanged. One-year post-LT survival was similar across eras, whereas 3- and 5-y survival were higher in era 2 (83% versus 91%; P = 0.01), driven by improved ALD survival with unchanged non-ALD survival. In a subgroup analysis of era 2 ALD transplant recipients, the <6-mo sobriety group had higher transplant Model of End-stage Liver Disease scores (34 versus 28; P < 0.001) lower unadjusted 1-y survival (88% versus 97%; P = 0.04) but similar survival after adjustment for Model of End-stage Liver Disease score ( P = 0.29) compared with the 6-mo sobriety group. Recidivism, rejection, and nonadherence rates were similar between groups. Conclusions. Liberalization of sobriety policy improved access to LT and long-term survival for ALD patients without compromising non-ALD outcomes.

items.title: Operationalizing Cardiac Xenotransplantation: An Administrative Playbook
items.abstract: As the field of xenotransplantation advances, institutions must navigate a complex landscape of nonclinical challenges to ensure safe and ethical implementation. This article presents a detailed account of the planning and execution of the first 2 human cardiac xenotransplants performed at the University of Maryland School of Medicine and Medical Center. Beyond the surgical innovation, these procedures required extensive coordination across regulatory, ethical, financial, legal, administrative, and operational domains. Drawing from institutional experience—including after-action analyses and interdisciplinary collaboration—we outline key strategies for Food and Drug Administration authorization, staff education, infection control, financial structuring, and communications planning. We also explore ethical considerations in patient selection and consent, emphasizing transparency, autonomy, and public health safeguards. This article serves as a practical guide for institutions preparing to undertake xenotransplantation, offering insights into the infrastructure and foresight necessary to support this transformative but complex medical advance.

items.title: Early Cardiac Dysfunction in Pediatric Becker Muscular Dystrophy: A Prospective Cross-sectional Echocardiographic Study
items.containerTitle: Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography
items.abstract: Background Becker muscular dystrophy (BMD) is an X-linked disorder characterized by progressive muscle weakness and cardiac involvement, with cardiomyopathy being the leading cause of mortality. While cardiac dysfunction in adult BMD patients is well documented, the early cardiac phenotype in pediatric populations remains poorly understood. This prospective cross-sectional study aimed to characterize age-stratified differences in cardiac function among children with BMD, children with Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD), and healthy controls. Methods This prospective cross-sectional study included male children aged 3-18 years who were enrolled from June 2020 to December 2023 and met strict inclusion criteria: genetically confirmed BMD or DMD diagnosis, no prior cardiac medications, and absence of comorbid conditions affecting cardiac function. Participants were stratified into three age-matched groups: 3 to under 7 years (youngest group), 7 to under 10 years (middle group), and 10 to under 18 years (oldest group), with comparable mean ages across BMD, DMD, and healthy controls within each age stratum. Comprehensive echocardiographic assessments were performed, including conventional parameters, tissue Doppler imaging, and speckle-tracking echocardiography. Statistical comparisons were made between groups within each age range. Result The study comprised 86 BMD patients, 86 DMD patients, and 74 controls across three age groups. After normality testing and Bonferroni-corrected post hoc comparisons, BMD patients showed early left ventricular involvement, including lower LVEF (60.54±8.09% vs 65.56±3.04%, p Conclusion Pediatric BMD patients exhibit subclinical, age-associated cardiac dysfunction detectable across pediatric age groups. Because abnormalities in LVEF, LV GLS, RV FAC, and RV GLS were already present in the youngest group, the findings support early and regular cardiac surveillance incorporating advanced echocardiographic techniques from preschool age. Longitudinal studies are needed to determine whether these subclinical differences predict clinically overt cardiomyopathy or treatment response.

items.title: Transthoracic Echocardiographic Reference Values in Male Professional Major League Soccer Players Under 21 Years of Age
items.containerTitle: Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography
items.abstract: Objective To define sport-specific echocardiographic reference values in elite male soccer players Background Exercise-induced cardiac remodeling varies by sport and demographic factors. The use of general population reference values may lead to misclassification of physiological remodeling as pathology, particularly in young athletes. Normative echocardiographic data in elite adolescent soccer players remain limited. Methods We performed a cross-sectional echocardiographic analysis of 430 male Major League Soccer athletes on active rosters from 2018 to 2023. Standard echocardiographic parameters were assessed and compared with American Society of Echocardiography reference values. Results Athlete age ranged from 14 to 21 years (mean 18.8 years). The cohort was racially and ethnically diverse (28.6% Black, 33.0% Hispanic, 37.0% White). 29% of athletes had dilated left ventricular end-diastolic volume (> 74mL/m2), while right ventricular enlargement (>41 mm) was observed in 27.2%. Maximal left ventricular wall thickness ranged from 5.5 to 12.9 mm (mean 9.79 mm), with 43.0% of athletes demonstrating wall thickness >10 mm. Mean left ventricular mass index was 92.8 g/m 2 , with 9.7% meeting criteria for left ventricular hypertrophy. Eccentric hypertrophy was present in 5.8%, concentric hypertrophy in 3.9%, and concentric remodeling in 18.8%, while 71.5% demonstrated normal geometry. Conclusion In this large, racially diverse cohort of elite male soccer players under 21 years of age, we provide comprehensive sport-specific echocardiographic reference values that address critical gaps in adolescent and young adult male soccer players.

items.title: Increased Left Ventricular Wall Thickness without Increased Mechanical Dispersion: A Distinguishing Feature of Transthyretin Amyloidosis Cardiomyopathy
items.containerTitle: Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography
items.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Life-threatening ventricular arrhythmia (LTVA) is infrequent in patients with transthyretin cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) despite severe cardiac dysfunction. We aimed to assess left ventricular mechanical dispersion (LVMD), as a marker of arrhythmia substrate, in ATTR-CM in comparison to other phenotypes with increased left ventricular (LV) wall thickness and in relation to LTVA occurrence. METHODS: Patients with suspected cardiac amyloidosis (CA) and increased LV wall thickness (septal thickness ≥12 mm) were identified. Patients with other types of CA and obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy were excluded. Data from comprehensive clinical assessments, laboratory tests, echocardiography with speckle tracking, and Tc-99m labeled pyrophosphate scintigraphy (PYP) were retrospectively collected from each patient. Diagnosis of ATTR-CM was established based on current recommendations. Longitudinal follow-up was performed over 5 years for LTVA (ventricular tachycardia and sudden cardiac arrest). RESULTS: In ATTR-CM group (n=150) lower LV ejection fraction, impaired global longitudinal strain (GLS), higher LV mass index, smaller end-diastolic volume index and higher relative apical sparing (RAS) were observed compared to the non-amyloid LVH group (n=223). Significantly lower mechanical dispersion (LVMD) was a remarkable feature of ATTR-CM, additive to ESC echocardiography parameters for the differential diagnosis (net reclassification improvement: 0.74). Higher LVMD was associated with increased risk of LTVA, whereas ATTR-CM was associated with a lower risk of LTVA. Mediation analysis further supported the mediating role of LVMD in the association between ATTR-CM and LTVA. CONCLUSION: Lower LVMD seems to be a distinguishing feature of ATTR-CM in association with infrequent LTVA despite severe increased LV wall thickness.

items.title: Of bicuspid aortic stenosis, women, and fibrosis: at last, new computed tomography-derived insights into 2-sinus bicuspid aortic valve stenosis
Where the differences lie: sex and plaque burden
items.abstract: This editorial refers to ‘Sex Based Differences in Association Between Plaque Burden and Ischemia—a CREDENCE Trial Substudy’, by Y. Ding et al., https://doi.org/10.1093/ehjci/jeag212. Gender differences in coronary artery disease are well characterized.1,2 Across registries and observational studies, compared with women, men present with distinct risk factor profiles, symptoms, prevalence of disease, and prognosis. Some of these differences remain counterintuitive; for instance, women with obstructive CAD enrolled in the ISCHEMIA trial had more frequent angina despite less extensive CAD on anatomical imaging compared with men.3 Indeed, while sex-based differences in atherosclerosis have been extensively characterized across imaging modalities and multicentre patient populations, the sex-specific associations between plaque burden and ischaemia are less well understood. Ding et al.4 further enrich our understanding of gender disparities in coronary artery disease. In a post hoc exploratory analysis of the CREDENCE trial involving 612 patients and 1716 coronary arteries, the authors embarked on elucidating the interplay between coronary CT angiography (CCTA)-derived quantitatively assessed coronary atherosclerosis and invasively measured fractional flow reserve. Compared with men, women had a lower total burden of coronary atherosclerosis, characterized by a lower degree of stenosis, shorter lesion length, and a lower prevalence of high-risk plaques. Quantitative plaque analysis further confirmed that women had significantly lower plaque volume and burden across all components, with the exception of calcified plaque burden. Plaque burden and plaque volume were significantly associated with ischaemia in both sexes, but while a 5% increase in plaque burden was significantly associated with ischaemia in women for total/calcified/non-calcified plaque, in men, that was the case only for total and non-calcified plaque burden. The authors conclude that despite having a lower overall plaque burden, women exhibit a stronger association between plaque burden and ischaemia than men. While the clinical implications of these findings are not immediately obvious, the reported discrepancy in the associations between ischaemia and particular plaque type burden should be approached with caution. While in women these associations were significant across the total/calcified/non-calcified plaque burdens, among men they persisted only in relation to the total and non-calcified plaque burdens; yet, for the latter, it remained borderline significant [OR = 1.13, 95% CI (1.00–1.27), P = 0.047], which is actually similar to the non-significant association with calcified plaque burden [OR = 1.09, 95% CI (0.99–1.20), P = 0.066]. Although meeting the threshold of P < 0.05 remains decisive, we should recognize that these associations point in the same direction, and that the presence or lack of such borderline significance is secondary and largely depends on the number of patients analysed. Importantly, as demonstrated in previous studies and evidenced in the current report, ischaemia with non-obstructive coronary artery disease (INOCA) is nowadays increasingly recognized in women.5,6 For patients with INOCA, the absence of a robust evidence-based strategy for medical management leaves them exposed to a substantive burden of anginal symptoms and an increased risk of adverse outcomes, which ultimately reduces physical functioning and overall quality of life. With the advent of detailed atherosclerosis phenotyping, by means of quantitative plaque analysis, dedicated randomized controlled trials are now addressing the challenges posed by non-obstructive coronary disease in women with suspected INOCA. For instance, the Women’s Ischaemia Trial to Reduce Events in Non-Obstructive Coronary Artery Disease (WARRIOR) aims to determine whether a combined intensive medical treatment regimen could reduce the incidence of adverse cardiovascular outcomes compared with usual care in this population.7,8 In a recent sub-analysis of the study, Wolny et al. showed that women with more frequent angina have a greater total plaque burden compared with those with milder symptoms and that this difference is mainly driven by a greater burden of non-calcified and low attenuation plaque.7 These findings are particularly relevant as, in the study by Ding et al., low attenuation plaque burden was not reported. However, according to large multicentre studies, low attenuation plaque burden is the strongest predictor of adverse outcomes.8 Indeed, in a post hoc analysis of SCOT-HEART, Williams et al. showed that patients with a low attenuation plaque burden exceeding 4% had an almost five-fold increase in the risk of myocardial infarction.8 Concordant findings were reported in a nested case-control study of acute coronary syndrome patients, as it demonstrated that low attenuation plaque acts as a precursor of downstream myocardial infarction.9 Furthermore, over a decade ago, studies bridging CCTA-based plaque analysis and myocardial flow and perfusion imaging with PET demonstrated that low attenuation plaque is associated with greater inducible myocardial hypoperfusion measured on PET.10 Moreover, CCTA-derived non-calcified and low attenuation plaque volumes have been linked to impaired myocardial flow reserve on 13N-ammonia positron emission tomography independent of stenosis severity.11,12 The strongest evidence supporting the rationale for quantifying low attenuation plaque, however, originates from an analysis of sex differences in coronary plaque among SCOT-HEART participants.2 In a study involving 1769 patients (772 females), Williams et al. demonstrated that while women are more likely to have normal coronary arteries and exhibit less low attenuation/non-calcified/calcified plaque, the low attenuation plaque burden remains a strong predictor of future myocardial infarction independent of sex, age, calcium score, and the presence of obstructive disease.2 Beyond the strong evidence for its predictive value, recently a randomized controlled trial demonstrated how quantitative plaque analysis can track response to therapy in women with INOCA. Among WARRIOR trial participants, intensive medical therapy led to favourable plaque composition changes.7 The unique ability of CCTA to track plaque stabilization, manifesting as decreasing low attenuation and non-calcified plaque, with/or without progression of calcified atherosclerosis, positions CT as the imaging modality of choice not only for dissecting the complex nature of INOCA but also for evaluating the response to therapy.7 Considered jointly, the available evidence strongly supports phenotyping coronary atherosclerosis in women with comprehensive quantitative plaque analysis, including the assessment of low attenuation plaque. Such assessments lend themselves to use in patients with INOCA and offer a framework for monitoring response to therapy. J.K. is supported by the Polish National Agency for Academic Exchange BPN/BEK/2025/1/00040.

items.title: Right Atrial Phasic Function Improves CMR-Based Prognostication in Patients with Heart Failure with Mildly Reduced Ejection Fraction: A Multicenter Study
items.abstract: Aims In multiple cardiovascular diseases, right atrial (RA) function can serve as an independent predictor for the clinical status and prognosis. However, the prognostic value of RA strain in patients with heart failure with mildly reduced ejection fraction (HFmrEF) remains considerably unknown. This study aims to explore the relationships between RA strain derived from cardiac magnetic resonance imaging-feature tracking (CMR-FT) and adverse outcomes in patients with HFmrEF. Methods and Results This retrospective study enrolled patients with HFmrEF who were referred for echocardiography and CMR at two tertiary medical centers from April 2016 to September 2024. The primary endpoint was a composite of all-cause mortality, HF-related hospitalization and cardiac transplantation. The findings were validated in a cohort of patients with HFmrEF enrolled from two additional tertiary care centers (January 2019 to January 2025). The development cohort included 1317 patients, and the validation cohort comprised 385 patients. During a median follow-up period of 2.8 years and 2.1 years, respectively, 243 and 72 patients in the development cohort and validation cohort reached the primary endpoint, respectively. Cox regression analysis showed that RA conduit strain was an independent predictor of the primary outcome (HR: 0.86 [0.82, 0.90]; P < .001). The full model integrating clinical variables, traditional imaging, and RA strain achieved the best predictive performance (C-index: 0.80 in development, 0.81 in validation cohorts). Conclusion RA conduit strain derived from CMR is an independent predictor of adverse outcomes in patients with HFmrEF, providing incremental prognostic value beyond traditional clinical and imaging-derived risk markers.​
