items.title: Perioperative Outcomes in Stage 1 Palliated Infants Undergoing Noncardiac Procedures: A Comparison by Shunt Type
items.abstract: Background Interstage infants with single‐ventricle (SV) physiology following Stage I palliation represent a high‐risk population for noncardiac procedures requiring anesthesia. Data comparing perioperative outcomes by shunt type remain limited. Aims Describe anesthetic management, perioperative complications, and postoperative outcomes in interstage SV infants undergoing noncardiac interventions and compare outcomes between right ventricle‐to‐pulmonary artery (Sano) and modified Blalock‐Taussig‐Thomas shunt (mBTTS) patients. Methods We performed a retrospective single‐center cohort study of interstage SV infants with Stage I palliation undergoing noncardiac surgery or nonsurgical procedures requiring anesthesia between 2015 and 2023. Outcomes were stratified by shunt type. Results A total of 208 noncardiac interventions in 120 interstage SV infants were analyzed; 136 (65.4%) encounters in 86 Sano patients and 72 (34.6%) encounters in 34 mBTTS patients. Compared with mBTTS infants, Sano patients underwent interventions at a younger age (57 [IQR 40–83] vs. 105 [59–278] days, p < 0.001) and lower weight (3.6 [3.0–4.1] vs. 4.8 [3.4–7.3] kg, p < 0.001). mBTTS procedures had higher rates of ventricular dysfunction (34.3% vs. 12.7%, p < 0.001), chromosomal abnormalities (63.9% vs. 19.1%, p < 0.001), gastrointestinal comorbidities (87.5% vs. 72.1%, p = 0.014), and hematologic comorbidities (41.7% vs. 22.8%, p = 0.006). Hemodynamic instability requiring vasoactive support was the most common perioperative complication and occurred similarly between groups (31.9% mBTTS vs. 31.6% Sano, p = 0.962). There were no perioperative cardiac arrests. Rates of postoperative escalation of care (2.9%), reintubation (3.0% vs. 2.9%, p = 0.999), readmission (16.2% vs. 16.9%, p = 0.999), and 30‐day mortality (2.3% vs. 2.9%, p = 0.999) were low and comparable between groups. Conclusions Despite the high‐risk physiology of interstage SV patients, perioperative outcomes were comparable between Sano and mBTTS cohorts. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and should not imply low procedural risk. Favorable outcomes likely reflect careful patient selection, multidisciplinary perioperative care, and specialized institutional expertise.

items.title: Comparative Efficacy of Sugammadex Versus Neostigmine for Neuromuscular Blockade Reversal in a Population of Neonatal Intensive Care Patients
Volume Guarantee Versus Manual Tidal Volume Monitoring During High‐Frequency Oscillatory Ventilation in Neonates: A Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial
items.abstract: Objective The present study compared the effects of high‐frequency oscillatory ventilation (HFOV) with automated volume guarantee (HFOV‐VG) versus careful manual high‐frequency tidal volume (VThf) monitoring (HFOV‐VM) on the incidences of hypo/hypercarbia in neonates. Methods In this open‐labeled, parallel‐group randomized controlled trial, 60 neonates failing conventional mechanical ventilation were allocated to receive HFOV‐VG ( n = 30) versus HFOV‐VM ( n = 30) as a rescue mode. The primary outcome was the incidence of hypo/hypercarbia at 1 h. Secondary outcomes were incidences of hypo/hypercarbia at 6/12/24/48 h and beyond, time‐specific trends for partial pressure of carbon dioxide (pCO 2 ), delivered VThf and mean airway pressure (MAP), cerebral blood flow (CBF) in the anterior cerebral artery (ACA) and regional cerebral oxygenation (CrSO 2 ), duration of respiratory support, and incidences of in‐hospital adverse events. Stata 18 was used for an intention‐to‐treat analysis. Results The incidence of hypo‐ or hypercarbia at 1 h of intervention was 15/30 (50%) in the HFOV‐VG and 13/30 (43%) in the HFOV‐VM groups ( p = 0.61). No differences were observed in the incidences of hypo‐ or hypercarbia anytime during HFOV. Time‐specific pCO 2 , VThf, and MAP were similar. On regression analysis, the only significant predictor for pCO 2 at 1 h was the baseline pCO 2 level in both the groups. No difference was observed in ACA‐CBF, CrSO 2 , duration of respiratory support, and in‐hospital adverse events including mortality. Conclusion There was no difference in the incidence of hypo/hypercarbia with HFOV‐VG versus HFOV‐VM at 1 h and throughout the duration of ventilation with a similar rate of complications when used as a rescue therapy. Trial Registration Clinical trial registry of India, Registration no: CTRI/2024/09/073455, Registered prospectively on 05/09/2024, https://ctri.icmr.org.in/

items.title: Risk Factors and Associated Severe Neonatal Morbidity and Mortality at Cesarean Delivery for the Second Twin
items.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between cesarean delivery for the second twin after vaginal delivery of the first twin and severe neonatal morbidity and mortality in comparison with vaginal delivery, and, secondarily, to identify risk factors for second twin cesarean delivery. METHODS: This was a planned secondary analysis of the JUMODA (JUmeaux MODe d'Accouchement) cohort, a national prospective population-based study of twin deliveries conducted from February 2014 to March 2015 in 176 French maternities. For this analysis, we included only second twins born after vaginal delivery of the first twin at a gestational of at least 32 weeks. The primary outcome was severe neonatal morbidity and mortality. The association of cesarean delivery for the second twin with severe neonatal morbidity and mortality in the total population was estimated from multivariate Poisson regression models. A sensitivity analysis limited to pregnancies that mirrored the Twin Birth Study low-risk population was conducted. Candidate risk factors were evaluated for cesarean delivery for the second twin. RESULTS: Among the 3,905 second twins included in analysis, 124 (3.2%) were delivered by cesarean and 3,781 (96.8%) were delivered vaginally. Cesarean delivery for the second twin was associated with severe neonatal morbidity and mortality compared with vaginal delivery (n=11/24 [8.9%] vs n=95/3,781 [2.5%]; adjusted relative risk [aRR] 3.17, 95% CI, 1.58–6.40). Findings were similar in the low-risk population (n=8/106 [7.5%] vs n=62/3,230 [1.9%]; aRR 4.03, 95% CI, 1.97–8.24). Absence of locoregional analgesia (aRR 2.13, 95% CI, 1.18–2.86), transverse second twin presentation (aRR 2.11, 95% CI, 1.44–3.08), and delivery in centers that performed fewer than 50 twin deliveries per year (aRR 1.58, 95% CI, 1.01–2.48) were associated with increased risk of cesarean delivery for the second twin. Conversely, breech second twin presentation was a protective factor (aRR 0.47, 95% CI, 0.27–0.82). CONCLUSION: In this secondary analysis of twin deliveries that involved vaginal delivery of the first twin, cesarean delivery for the second twin tripled the risk of severe neonatal morbidity and mortality when compared with vaginal delivery. Results should be interpreted with caution because of the small number of events and potential residual confounding.

items.title: Modeling the U.S. National Burden of Severe Hemolytic Disease of the Fetus and Newborn
items.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To estimate the national burden of severe hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn (HDFN) attributed to the three most clinically significant alloantibodies (anti-D, anti-K, and anti-c) using a large data set of prenatal antibody screens in U.S. pregnancies. METHODS: Prenatal red blood cell alloantibody results were extracted from a national laboratory firm from 2010 to 2021 and normalized to the U.S. population race, ethnicity, and regional distributions based on Census data. Prevalence of critical alloantibody titers, pregnancy continuation rates, distribution of paternal race and ethnicity, allele prevalence of antigen in paternal race and ethnicity, and rate of disease were used to estimate the burden of disease using Monte Carlo simulations. RESULTS: There were 8,809,993 pregnancies included in the cohort. Normalization of the cohort to U.S. births resulted in an estimated national prevalence of any high-risk antibodies of 686.5 per 100,000 pregnancies (27.9 per 100,000 for anti-c, 596.1 per 100,000 for anti-D, and 62.5 per 100,000 for anti-K), with 63.9 per 100,000 (1.9 for anti-c, 20.6 for anti-D, and 41.3 for anti-K) of those reaching critical levels. The estimated national burden of severe HDFN attributed to any high-risk antibody was 2.4 per 100,000 pregnancies (95% CI, 2.0–2.9). Among all pregnancies with critical titers, 3.8% (95% CI, 3.1–4.5) were estimated to result in severe HDFN. CONCLUSION: This study provides contemporary national estimates of severe HDFN in the United States, demonstrating that, although alloimmunization is relatively common, progression to severe HDFN remains rare.

items.title: Anti-Müllerian Hormone Trajectories Across the Menopause Transition
items.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To analyze the trajectory of anti-müllerian hormone (AMH) decline leading to the final menstrual period, identify distinct AMH patterns, and assess their association with unique participant characteristics. METHODS: SWAN (Study of Women's Health Across the Nation), a multisite, multiethnic perimenopausal cohort, was analyzed. Included participants had an observed final menstrual period and three or more measurements of AMH levels taken during perimenopause. Statistical modeling was used to identify AMH trajectory classes; participants were placed into predicted class based on best fit. Differences in baseline demographic and health characteristics were assessed by analysis of variance or χ 2 . Generalized estimating equation models were used to estimate the association between AMH trajectory class and outcomes, accounting for repeated measures. RESULTS: A total of 1,131 women had at least three AMH measurements and an observed final menstrual period. Two AMH trajectory classes were observed: 448 participants (39.6%) with lower initial AMH and slower decline (low/slow [LS] group) and 683 participants (60.4%) with higher AMH and steeper decline (high/fast [HF] group). Participants in the LS group had a median AMH decline of 1.2 pg/mL/month; those in the HF group had a decline of 6.7 pg/mL/month. The LS classification was associated with baseline older age, higher body mass index (BMI), and non-White race and ethnicity. Trajectory classes did not differ by history of oligomenorrhea, presumptive polycystic ovarian syndrome, or smoking status. Participants in the LS group had worse postmenopausal cardiovascular risk profiles and were less likely to report frequent vasomotor symptoms after the final menstrual period. CONCLUSION: Two different AMH trajectories to the final menstrual period were observed in a subsample of SWAN participants. Independent of a participant's premenopausal cardiovascular risk factors, lower starting AMH and slower decline were associated with higher postmenopausal cardiovascular risk.

items.title: Antidepressant Discontinuation During Pregnancy and Risk of Mental Health–Related Emergencies
items.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate contemporary patterns of antidepressant discontinuation during pregnancy and associated maternal mental health outcomes, including behavioral health–related emergency department (ED) visits, among patients with preexisting depression or anxiety. METHODS: This was a retrospective cohort study of a state-based private insurance claims database in Pennsylvania. Patients who delivered between January 1, 2023, and December 31, 2024, with a diagnosis of depression or anxiety before pregnancy and an active prescription for a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) or serotonin–norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor (SNRI) in the 3 months before pregnancy were included. The exposure was antidepressant continuation compared with discontinuation during pregnancy, defined as no prescription fills or a gap of more than 60 days. The primary outcome was behavioral health–related ED visits during pregnancy and the postpartum period. Behavioral health–related ED visit rates were compared between patients who continued and those who discontinued antidepressants with appropriate bivariate statistical tests. RESULTS: Among 3,983 patients with depression or anxiety, 1,462 (36.7%) entered pregnancy with an active SSRI or SNRI prescription. Of these, 260 (17.8%) had no medication fills during pregnancy, and 945 (64.6%) had a gap of more than 60 days. Among patients with a treatment gap of more than 60 days, discontinuation occurred most commonly in the first trimester (44.9%) followed by the third trimester (30.3%). Patients who continued and those who discontinued treatment had similar rates of outpatient and ED mental health visits before pregnancy. However, discontinuation was associated with a higher risk of mental health–related emergency visits during pregnancy, with peaks in the second month (58 vs 37/1,000, P =.027) and the ninth month (59 vs 29/1,000, P <.01) of pregnancy. This increased risk persisted postpartum, with higher rates of mental health–related ED visits within 8 months after delivery among those who discontinued treatment during pregnancy (32 vs 21/1,000, P =.02). CONCLUSION: In this cohort of privately insured patients with preexisting depression or anxiety, antidepressant discontinuation during pregnancy was common and was associated with increased risk of mental health–related ED visits. These findings underscore the need for clinical and policy strategies to support continuation of evidence-based treatment for perinatal mental health conditions and to address preventable contributors to maternal morbidity and mortality.

items.title: Hepatitis C Treatment Access With Implementation of an Antenatal Linkage-to-Care Bundle
items.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate a health system–wide quality-improvement bundle (HALT-C [hepatitis C antenatal linkage-to-care]) on its ability to integrate proactive patient identification, care coordination, and treatment timing options on direct-acting antiviral prescription by 6 months postpartum. METHODS: We implemented our quality-improvement initiative at a large midwestern health system and evaluated its effect by comparing outcomes among eligible pregnancies identified preimplementation (December 1, 2021–May 31, 2023) with those identified postimplementation (March 1, 2024–August 31, 2025). Eligible patients were aged at least 18 years, with detectable hepatitis C virus RNA and at least one encounter in the health system before 35 weeks of gestation. The primary outcome was the percentage of patients prescribed direct-acting antivirals by 6 months postpartum. Secondary outcomes included linkage to care, the treatment timing decision, treatment completion, sustained virologic response (SVR), infant screening, and perinatal transmission. Comparison of antenatal initiation of treatment and postpartum initiation of treatment was also performed. RESULTS: We identified 62 bundle-eligible pregnancies in the preimplementation period and identified 35 in the postimplementation period. Direct-acting antiviral prescription by 6 months postpartum increased from 48.4% to 77.1% ( P =.009); treatment completion improved from 21.0% to 54.3% ( P =.001). Treatment increases were greatest among patients who delivered regionally, rather than at the main hospital, with an increase in direct-acting antiviral prescription rates of 14.3% to 72.7% ( P <.001). Thirty of 35 individuals identified postimplementation were successfully linked to care, and 75.0% of clinic attendees preferred antenatal treatment over postpartum treatment. Known treatment completion and SVR increased from 21.0% to 54.3% ( P =.001). Those treated antenatally were twice as likely to complete treatment than those who deferred postpartum (92.3% vs 45.5%; P =.02). Infant screening and perinatal transmission rates did not change; however, no perinatal transmissions occurred among infants where treatment occurred antenatally. CONCLUSION: The HALT-C bundle was associated with significantly improved direct-acting antiviral receipt across a regional health system. Most patients preferred treatment during pregnancy. Patients treated antenatally were twice as likely to complete treatment, highlighting pregnancy as an important opportunity to initiate curative therapy.

items.title: Association Between Adverse Pregnancy Outcomes and Postpartum Contraceptive Method Selection and Use
items.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether adverse pregnancy outcomes are associated with self-reported postpartum contraceptive use and method selection. METHODS: We performed a secondary data analysis of data from the Pregnancy Risk Assessment Monitoring System (phase 8 cohort, 2016–2022). The exposures of interest were adverse pregnancy outcomes, including maternal hypertension, diabetes, preterm birth, prolonged infant hospitalization, and infant death. Contraceptive methods were grouped into four categories: permanent contraception, long-acting reversible contraception, prescription-start methods (patch, ring, pill, or injectable), and patient-start methods (condoms, natural family planning, withdrawal, or abstinence) based on the level of clinical engagement required. We employed multivariable logistic regression to examine the association between adverse pregnancy outcomes and postpartum contraceptive use. Among postpartum contraceptive users, we used multinomial logistic regression to analyze whether adverse pregnancy outcomes influenced method selection. RESULTS: In this analysis of 222,412 individuals, 32.7% of the study sample experienced at least one adverse pregnancy outcome and 77.4% of the sample reported using contraception. In weighted models, experiencing three or more adverse pregnancy outcomes was associated with lower odds of postpartum contraception usage (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 0.89; 95% CI, 0.82–0.97). Patients who experienced infant death had lower odds of using any postpartum contraception than those who did not (aOR 0.39; 95% CI, 0.33–0.46). We observed no association between experiencing preterm birth, prolonged infant hospitalization, gestational diabetes, or hypertension and postpartum contraceptive use. Among postpartum contraceptive users, experiencing at least one adverse pregnancy outcome was associated with a higher likelihood of using permanent contraception relative to patient-start methods. CONCLUSION: Experiencing an increasing number of adverse pregnancy outcomes was associated with lower odds of postpartum contraceptive use. Adverse pregnancy outcomes were associated with permanent contraception use. Patient-centered contraceptive counseling and shared decision making to support patients in identifying and actualizing their postpartum reproductive goals are necessary in the wake of adverse pregnancy outcomes.

items.title: Patient Report of Subsequent Uterine-Sparing Leiomyomata Procedures up to 10 Years
items.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To determine risk of subsequent treatment after uterine-sparing procedures for uterine leiomyomata. METHODS: Study participants from two uterine leiomyomata procedure studies were recontacted. The baseline procedures studied included myomectomy, endometrial ablation, laparoscopic ultrasound–guided radiofrequency ablation (RFA), and uterine artery embolization (UAE). Participants reported all uterine leiomyomata procedures after their baseline uterine-sparing leiomyomata procedure. The subsequent treatment options analyzed included the baseline uterine leiomyomata procedures plus hysterectomy and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)–guided focused ultrasonography. Kaplan-Meier curves and Cox proportional hazards models were used to evaluate differences in retreatment risk according to baseline procedure by means of hazard ratios (HRs) and corresponding 95% CIs. Fisher exact tests were used to examine the association between baseline procedure and retreatment procedure. RESULTS: The total number of participants in the study is 817. Median age at baseline procedure was 39.7 years; participant median age at recontact was 46.8 years. Follow-up after baseline procedure was 4.0–10.5 years. Baseline procedure types included myomectomy (n=469, 66.0%), endometrial ablation (n=90, 12.7%), RFA (n=96, 13.5%), and UAE (n=56, 7.9%). Of the 204 participants (28.7%) who had retreatment for uterine leiomyomata, the most common subsequent procedure was hysterectomy (n=94, 46.1%), followed by myomectomy (n=57, 27.9%), UAE (n=26, 12.7%), endometrial ablation (n=12, 5.9%), MRI-guided focused ultrasonography (n=9, 4.4%), and RFA (n=6, 2.9%). Within 5 years after the baseline procedure, 79.1% (95% CI, 76.2–82.1%) had no additional uterine procedures; 64.1% (95% CI, 57.7–71.2%) had none within 10 years. When endometrial ablation, RFA, and UAE were compared with myomectomy, RFA was found to have a higher retreatment rate (HR 1.61, 95% CI, 1.08–2.40). Those who had undergone myomectomy at baseline were the least likely (10.9%) and those who had undergone endometrial ablation were most likely (22.2%) to have a subsequent hysterectomy. CONCLUSION: The majority of women who have uterine-sparing uterine leiomyomata procedures can remain treatment free for 5–10 years. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06430320.

items.title: Improving Mental Health Support for Neonatal Intensive Care Unit Mothers Through a Universal Screening Quality-Improvement Initiative
items.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To improve early perinatal mood and anxiety disorder screening for neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) mothers and facilitate timely referral to mental health services through the integration of a dedicated mental health clinician at our level 3 NICU. METHODS: A multidisciplinary team convened to address barriers to universal maternal mental health screening in our NICU. Key drivers were identified, focusing on appropriate screening tools, availability of a mental health clinician, and a robust referral process should a mother screen positive. The primary outcome measure was percentage of referrals made for mothers who screened positive for perinatal mood and anxiety disorders. The process measure was percentage of mothers screened. Clinical characteristics were compared between mothers who screened positive and those who screened negative to ensure that any disparities identified were addressed in real time. RESULTS: Since implementation of our universal screening program, 95.0% of mothers in our NICU have been screened for perinatal mood and anxiety disorders (an increase from 29.5%). Of those, 59.9% required referral for additional psychosocial support (an increase from 25.3%). Mothers who screened positive were more likely to be Black non-Hispanic ( P <.001), and mothers who screened negative were more likely to be White non-Hispanic ( P =.021). No differences were identified in delivery mode or breastfeeding at discharge. CONCLUSION: A dedicated NICU mental health clinician, with multidisciplinary buy-in, may allow the successful implementation and maintenance of a universal perinatal mood and anxiety disorder screening and referral program.

items.title: Hospital-Level Variation in Antenatal Corticosteroid Use for Late Preterm Births
items.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To determine whether and to what extent hospitals across the United States vary in their use of late preterm steroids. METHODS: This was a retrospective cohort study of singleton births with known gestational ages identified in the Premier Healthcare Database from 2015 to 2022. The primary variable of interest was hospital-level adoption of antenatal corticosteroid use for late preterm singleton deliveries, calculated as the proportion of late preterm singleton births (34–36 completed weeks of gestation) with any betamethasone exposure during the same late preterm period. Hospital adoption was defined as the weighted average rate of steroid administration among late preterm births across the entire postperiod. Hospitals were ranked by their late preterm steroid adoption rates and categorized by quartile based on the empirical distribution. Temporal trends were assessed using annual hospital-level adoption rates and visualized using time series plots and distributional plots. A logistic regression model was constructed to identify hospital characteristics associated with being a highest-quartile adopter. RESULTS: The analysis cohort included 726 hospitals and 5,109,270 births, of which 309,837 (6.1%) were singleton late preterm births. Hospital steroid exposure rates ranged from 0% to 92% and were categorized into quartiles based on overall exposure rate, with cutoffs at 22.4%, 33.9%, and 45.1%. Median exposure rates increased progressively across quartiles, from 15.4% (IQR 10.0–18.9%) in the lowest-adopting hospitals (quartile 1) to 54.3% (IQR 49.1–61.0%) in the highest-adopting hospitals (quartile 4), with substantial within-quartile variation. In the multivariable model, urban location was a strong predictor of high adoption after adjustment (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 2.03; 95% CI, 1.04–4.02, P =.04). Compared with Midwestern hospitals, Southern hospitals had significantly lower odds of being high adopters (aOR 0.32; 95% CI, 0.17–0.61, P <.001). Among clinical case mix variables, a higher proportion of late preterm births at 34 weeks of gestation was strongly associated with high adoption (aOR 2.39; 95% CI, 1.73–3.36, P <.001). CONCLUSION: After the publication of the ALPS (Antenatal Late Preterm Steroids) trial, the adoption of late preterm steroid use was heterogeneous among U.S. hospitals. These findings highlight the need for a more in-depth exploration of local factors that drive the adoption of evidence-based practices outside of observable hospital characteristics.

IVF versus surgery for infertility in women with deep and ovarian endometriosis: a partially randomized patient preference trial
items.containerTitle: American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology
items.abstract: Study objective Endometriosis-associated infertility can be managed either surgically or through assisted reproductive technologies (ART). Given the recent substantial improvement in the accuracy of ultrasound diagnosis of ovarian endometriomas and deep infiltrating endometriosis, surgery is no longer required to detect these disease forms. Therefore, infertile women with ultrasound-diagnosed endometriosis face two alternatives; they can be either operated or straight embark in in vitro fertilization (IVF). In this study, we aimed to compare these two options, as no randomized clinical trial (RCT) has yet addressed this clinical scenario. Study design A multicenter, pragmatic, partially randomized patient preference trial (PRPT) was conducted at three Italian tertiary referral centers with expertise in both endometriosis surgery and IVF. The trial was designed to compare reproductive outcomes between IVF and surgery in infertile women with ultrasound-diagnosed ovarian and deep infiltrating endometriosis. Women with a history of previous surgery for endometriosis or prior IVF were excluded. Additional key eligibility criteria were age Results Recruitment began in March 2021 and was discontinued in September 2024 in accordance with the Ethics Committees after the enrollment of 130 women (55 in the randomized cohort and 75 in the preference cohort), owing to investigators' increasing awareness of a markedly higher likelihood of success in women allocated to IVF. In the randomized cohort, the number of live births observed in the surgical and IVF groups was 7 out of 27 (26%) and 16 out of 28 (57%), respectively (p=0.019). The RR of live birth in women assigned to IVF was 2.20 (95% CI, 1.08-4.50). In the preference cohort, the number of live births was 7 out of 25 (28%) and 32 out of 50 (64%), respectively (p=0.003). The relative risks (RR) of live birth for women assigned to IVF in the randomized and preference cohorts were 2.20 (95% CI: 1.08-4.50) and 2.29 (95% CI: 1.18-4.43), respectively. When data from the two cohorts were combined, the RR remained consistent at 2.29 (95% CI: 1.41-3.70). Per protocol and survival analyses further supported these findings. Conclusions In this pragmatic PRPT, IVF was more effective than surgery for the treatment of infertility in women with ultrasound-diagnosed ovarian or deep infiltrating endometriosis.

items.title: Assessing the Safety of Estro-Progestin and Progestin-only drugs: A Signal Detection Study of Meningioma Reports in EudraVigilance
items.containerTitle: American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Exogenous hormonal therapies are used for contraception and for several gynecologic and menopausal indications, frequently for prolonged periods. Previous epidemiological studies have reported an increased risk of meningioma with some progestins, particularly following prolonged exposure and high cumulative doses. It is a common intracranial tumor with marked female predominance, suggesting a potential role of hormones in its pathogenesis and growth. Most meningiomas are located in the anterior or middle skull base, where a higher prevalence of progesterone receptors has been observed. This evidence further underlines the relationship between hormonal factors and this type of intracranial tumor. Moreover, rapid and spontaneous tumor regression has been reported after cessation of treatment with exogenous hormones or when serum progestogen levels decrease due to physiological factors. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate the presence of a safety signal for meningioma among users of estro-progestin and progestin-only therapies using pharmacovigilance data. STUDY DESIGN: Data from the EudraVigilance database were analyzed using both descriptive and statistical approaches. Three complementary disproportionality methods were applied to strengthen signal detection: Reporting Odds Ratio (ROR), Information Component (IC), and Empirical Bayes Geometric Mean (EBGM). The study period covered the last ten years, from January 1, 2016, to December 31, 2025. The drugs analyzed included: drospirenone-ethinylestradiol combination, dienogest-ethinylestradiol combination, drospirenone-only, desogestrel and levonorgestrel. We included all reports in which these drugs were recorded as suspected, excluding those in which they were reported only as concomitant drugs. RESULTS: A total of 21,091 reports, corresponding to 70,476 drug-ADR pairs, were identified. As expected, most reports concerned female patients, consistent with both the indication of these therapies and the known higher prevalence of meningioma in women. Disproportionality signals were identified for drospirenone and desogestrel-only formulations, suggesting a potential association with meningioma: A disproportionality signal was identified for desogestrel-only pills (110 reports; ROR 11.11, 95% CI 8.79-14.06; IC025 2.64; EB05 5.79). A novel exploratory signal also emerged for drospirenone-only pills (8 reports; ROR 2.41, 95% CI 1.19-4.89; IC025 0.54; EB05 1.17). No disproportionality signal was detected for the two combined formulations or levonorgestrel; absence of a signal should not be interpreted as absence of risk or evidence of comparative safety. In addition to meningioma, other serious adverse drug reactions - including known cardiovascular events and previously unreported reactions - were identified, warranting further investigation. CONCLUSIONS: These findings highlight the importance of ongoing pharmacovigilance activities and careful benefit-risk evaluation of hormonal therapies, particularly given their widespread and long-term use and the potential for rare but serious outcomes such as meningioma. This analysis identified new but exploratory safety signals that warrant confirmation in studies with valid exposure denominators, longitudinal treatment histories, latency assessment, and control of confounding. The findings should not be used alone to infer causality or guide comparative clinical decisions.

items.title: Loop electrosurgical excision procedure with or without intraoperative iodine: A randomized controlled trial
items.containerTitle: American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Intraoperative Lugol's iodine staining of the cervix (IOS) during loop electrosurgical excision procedure (LEEP) is commonly used to better define surgical resection margins. No randomized head-to-head comparison of LEEP with vs without IOS is available to inform clinical practice. OBJECTIVE: To compare LEEP with versus without IOS regarding rates of involved resection margins, patient satisfaction and procedure-related outcomes. STUDY DESIGN: Consecutive women referred to a university colposcopy unit were recruited and randomized 1:1 to LEEP with intraoperative application of Lugol's iodine or LEEP without intraoperative Lugol's iodine (control). The primary endpoint was the histopathological rate of involved resection margins. Secondary endpoints included patient satisfaction assessed on the day of surgery and 14 days thereafter using numerical rating scales (0-10) and procedure-related complications, pain, blood loss, and surgeon preference. Results were compared using nonparametric, chi-square, and t tests. Multivariable logistic regression was used to assess the influence of covariates on the primary outcome. RESULTS: Between January 2022 and September 2025, we randomized 229 women, 114 in the IOS arm and 115 in the control arm. In an intention-to-treat analysis, rates of involved resection margins were 20/114 (17.5%) vs 8/115 (7.0%) (risk difference, 10.6 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.1-19.3; risk ratio, 2.52; 95% CI 1.16-5.49; P=.014). Post hoc analysis of 215 women showed lower main-cone depth after fixation with IOS (transformation-zone-adjusted mean difference, -1.47 mm; 95% CI, -2.61 to -0.34; P=.011). There were no differences in operative metrics including cone weight, cone fragmentation, procedure time, and time to complete hemostasis. Intraoperative complications were similar in both groups as were surgeons' ratings. Immediate postoperative pain and satisfaction did not differ significantly between groups. At 14-day follow-up, bleeding outcomes favored the iodine group. Bleeding intensity during the first 24 postoperative hours was lower (median 1 [interquartile range 0-3] vs 2 [1-4]; P=.008) and bleeding duration was shorter (median 3 [1-9] vs 5 [2-14] days; P=.047). There were no differences in pain intensity, pain duration, analgesic use, or overall satisfaction at follow-up. In multivariable logistic regression adjusting for age, body mass index, ever smoking, and transformation zone, randomization to IOS remained associated with higher odds of involved resection margins (adjusted odds ratio 3.46, 95% CI 1.38-8.70; P=.008). CONCLUSION: LEEP with IOS is associated with a higher rate of involved resection margins and should therefore not be used routinely in clinical practice.

items.title: Hysterectomy-corrected, age-specific incidence and survival of uterine sarcomas by histotype, race and ethnicity in the United States, 2000–2019
items.containerTitle: American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology
items.abstract: Background Uterine sarcomas are rare but aggressive mesenchymal malignancies of the uterus, characterized by diverse histotypes and poor survival. However, little is known about the epidemiology and clinical characteristics of uterine sarcoma histotypes at the population level. Objective To evaluate hysterectomy-corrected, age-specific incidence rates and five-year relative survival by histologic subtype, stage at diagnosis, and race/ethnicity among U.S. individuals aged ≥20 years diagnosed with uterine sarcoma in the SEER 22 registries from 2000-2019. Study design This retrospective population-based study included microscopically confirmed uterine sarcoma cases registered in the SEER 22 database. Hysterectomy-corrected, age-specific incidence rates were calculated by histotype, stage at diagnosis, and race/ethnicity. Five-year relative survival was estimated using the Ederer II method in SEER*Stat software (version 9.0.42). Results A total of 14,801 individuals aged ≥20 years diagnosed with uterine sarcoma were included. Leiomyosarcoma (LMS) were most common comprising 53.3% of the total cases (n=7883), endometrial stromal sarcoma (ESS) accounted for 26.7% of cases (n=3948), Adenosarcoma for 12.7% (n=1884), sarcoma not otherwise specified (NOS) for 5.7% (n=837), and undifferentiated sarcoma for 1.7% of cases (n=249). Incidence rates of uterine sarcomas increased until ages 50-54 and plateaued thereafter other than among Non-Hispanic Black (NHB) individuals, where incidence continued to increase until ages 65-69 years. LMS demonstrated the highest hysterectomy-corrected incidence (0.6 per 100,000), followed by ESS (0.3 per 100,000) and Adenosarcoma (0.1 per 100,000). NHB individuals had the highest incidence of uterine sarcomas across all histotypes. Overall, NHB individuals were more likely to be diagnosed with distant diseases compared with other groups. Among all individuals, five-year relative survival was 42.3% (95% CI: 41-43.5) for LMS, 70.2% (68.5-71.8) for ESS, and 78.3% (75.7-80.6) for Adenosarcoma. When categorized by stage at diagnosis, relative survival for localized disease ranged from 62% to 85% in all histotypes, vs. 13.5% to 34.7% for distant metastatic disease. Survival was lowest among NHB individuals, 41.9%, versus 55.4 % in Non-Hispanic White (NHW) individuals, across all histotypes and stage at diagnosis. Conclusion Uterine sarcomas exhibit pronounced heterogeneity, comprising distinct histotypes that demonstrate variable incidence patterns and survival trajectories. LMS had the highest incidence and worse survival compared with ESS and Adenosarcoma. NHB individuals had the highest incidence rates for all histotypes and were more likely to have advanced disease and worse survival compared with other groups. Future studies are required to evaluate underlying risk factors, early detection strategies, and response to therapy by histotype, with a particular focus on addressing disparities in NHB individuals.

items.title: Urgency urinary incontinence, one condition, or many? Cluster analysis of physiological variables in the Symptoms of Lower Urinary Tract Dysfunction Research Network (LURN) II cohort.
items.containerTitle: American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology
items.abstract: Background Our understanding of the pathophysiology of urgency urinary incontinence (UUI) remains incomplete, limiting treatment selection. Although UUI is considered to be multifactorial, evidence for which factors contribute is limited and there has tended to be a focus on bladder dysfunction, rather than taking a more multi-dimensional view. Objective To identify physiologically distinct phenotypes of UUI by cluster analysis of bladder and urethral motor and sensory function tests. Methods Secondary analysis of data from the Symptoms of Lower Urinary Tract Dysfunction Research Network (LURN) II Organ project which included 56 women with UUI and 31 asymptomatic controls was performed. Participants underwent urethral motor and sensory assessments, and rapid-fill cystometry before and after intravesical lidocaine instillation. Thirty-two physiological variables were analyzed using a validated, resampling-based consensus clustering pipeline. Cluster differences were assessed using ANOVA with false discovery rate correction ("P adj ") and logistic regression. Results Three distinct phenotypes were identified. Cluster A (n=15) showed detrusor overactivity during both saline and post-lidocaine fills, and reduced bladder sensation volumes (39-55% of controls) with normal urethral function. Cluster B (n=18) demonstrated significant lidocaine-related capacity increase of 138 mL (72%) (P adj ≤ 0.003 and P adj ≤ 0.0001, respectively) and a 30% decrease in maximum urethral closure pressure (P adj = 0.0076). Cluster C (n=23) exhibited minimal change in volumes post-lidocaine and a general lack of detrusor overactivity. Demographics and symptoms were similar across clusters. In regression analysis adjusting for age, BMI, and vaginal parity, primary predictors for A were detrusor overactivity (AUC = 0.95); for B, lidocaine-related capacity change (AUC = 0.92); and for C, low first desire to void (post-lidocaine) normalized by the functional (bladder diary) bladder capacity (AUC = 0.83). Conclusions In this exploratory analysis, clustering of physiological data identified three potential UUI phenotypes with differing bladder and urethral characteristics. If validated in larger cohorts, these phenotypes could guide trials testing whether phenotype-directed treatment improves outcomes.

items.abstract: Background Pelvic floor muscle dysfunction is a common contributor to chronic pelvic pain (CPP), yet targeted treatment options remain limited. Objective To determine whether baclofen vaginal suppositories in CPP is safe and effective when compared with placebo. Methods This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial compared 20mg baclofen vaginal suppositories to placebo suppositories nightly in women with CPP. Women older than18 years without allergy to baclofen or the suppository base were included if they had ≥40/100 mm pain on a visual analogue scale (VAS) with palpation of the obturator internus or levator ani on standardized pelvic exam. Improvement in this standardized pelvic exam 100mm VAS pain score represented the primary outcome. Participants completed Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS) pain interference, PROMIS global health, PROMIS sexual function at baseline, 4, and 8 weeks, with repeat pelvic examination at 8 weeks. The study was powered to detect the minimum clinically important difference (MCID) of 20mm on a 100mm VAS pain scale on a standardized pelvic floor muscle examination with a total sample size of 34, 17 in each group. Adverse events, pill count, and other treatments for CPP during the study period were collected. Differences between treatment groups were assessed using the Mann-Whitney test, and multiple imputation was used to account for missing data. Results A total of 39 women were enrolled in the study with 37 randomized.19 patients received baclofen vaginal suppositories and 18 received placebo suppositories. Demographic data was similar between groups, with similar mean age (42.5 ± 12.5 baclofen vs 46.3 ± 12.2 placebo) and body mass index (29.4 ± 6.7 vs 29.8 ± 7.6). There was a statistically and clinically significant improvement in the primary outcome of change in the 100mm VAS pain score on pelvic floor muscle examination at 8 weeks relative to baseline in the baclofen group as compared to placebo (median improvement of 33.5 mm [IQR: 30 to 46.230.0] baclofen vs 7.2 mm [0.0 to 10.0] placebo, p= Conclusions In this appropriately powered, randomized trial, patients experienced statistically and clinically significantly less pain with 8 weeks of nightly baclofen vaginal suppositories when compared to placebo. Baclofen suppositories were shown to be well tolerated with no adverse events.

items.title: Maternal Autoimmune Diseases During Pregnancy and Offspring Type 1 Diabetes
items.abstract: IMPORTANCE Maternal autoimmune diseases during pregnancy may influence the long-term risk of immune-mediated diseases in offspring, but the relative contributions of prenatal and familial factors to offspring type 1 diabetes (T1D) remain unclear. OBJECTIVE To investigate the association between a broad spectrum of maternal autoimmune diseases during pregnancy and offspring T1D, and to compare the associations of maternal and paternal autoimmune diseases with offspring T1D. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS This population-based cohort study included children identified from national health registers who were born in Sweden between 2001 and 2014, and were followed up from birth until T1D diagnosis, death, emigration, or December 31, 2023. These data were analyzed from November 2025 to June 2026. EXPOSURE Parental autoimmune diseases diagnosed before or during pregnancy, identified from national health registers. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES The primary outcome was incident T1D in offspring. Hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% CIs for offspring T1D were estimated using Cox proportional hazard regression models. Associations of maternal and paternal autoimmune diseases before childbirth with offspring T1D were directly compared, and cousin analyses were performed to assess the potential role of shared familial factors. RESULTS During a median follow-up of 15.3 years, 10 273 (0.71%) of the 1 455 645 included individuals (51.4% male and 48.6% female; median [IQR], age 15.3 [11.9-19.0] years) developed T1D. Maternal autoimmune disease during pregnancy was associated with an increased risk of offspring T1D (adjusted HR, 1.57; 95% CI, 1.46-1.68); paternal autoimmune disease before childbirth showed a similar association (adjusted HR, 1.51; 95% CI, 1.37-1.67). No overall difference was observed in maternal-paternal comparisons (ratio of HR, 1.04; 95% CI, 0.92-1.17), but heterogeneity was observed across specific disease categories. A clear gradient in T1D risk was observed according to parental T1D status, with the highest risk among offspring with both parents affected, followed by paternal T1D only and maternal T1D only. In cousin analyses, the association with maternal autoimmune disease was attenuated but persisted (HR, 1.27; 95% CI, 1.08-1.50). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE In this population-based cohort study, maternal autoimmune diseases during pregnancy were associated with an increased risk of offspring T1D. Comparable associations of maternal and paternal autoimmune diseases with offspring T1D suggest a role of shared familial susceptibility, while disease-specific differences indicate that some conditions could have parental-specific effects, suggesting contributions from shared familial susceptibility and potential intrauterine mechanisms.

items.title: Prenatal Exposure to Wildfire PM 2.5 and Risk of ASD and ADHD in Children Enrolled in Medicaid
items.abstract: Importance Wildfires are an increasing source of fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ), yet evidence on prenatal wildfire smoke exposure and long-term neurodevelopmental outcomes remains limited. Objective To examine whether prenatal exposure to wildfire-related PM 2.5 is associated with risk of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in children. Design, Setting, and Participants This was a population-based cohort study of the US nationwide Medicaid population using Medicaid Analytic Extract (MAX) data from 2007 to 2014 with follow-up through childhood. Included were mother-child pairs with continuous enrollment and stable residential zip code during pregnancy. Exposure Weekly wildfire smoke–attributable PM 2.5 at 1-km 2 resolution, aggregated to the zip code level across pregnancy. Main Outcomes and Measures Incident ASD and ADHD identified using validated claims-based algorithms. Associations were estimated using Cox proportional-hazards models with distributed lag nonlinear models. Results A total of 893 212 mother-child pairs (mother mean [SD] age, 24.7 [5.9] years) were included in this analysis. Children entered the cohort at birth (452 218 [50.6%] male). Mean (SD) observed follow-up was 6.3 (2.4) years for children diagnosed with ASD and 7.1 (1.9) years for children diagnosed with ADHD. Among 893 212 children, 8357 were diagnosed with ASD and 22 302 with ADHD. The cumulative incidence until age 8 years was 1.9% for ASD and 10.4% for ADHD. An IQR increase in cumulative wildfire PM 2.5 exposure (0.75 µg/m 3 ) during pregnancy was associated with increased risk of ASD (hazard ratio [HR], 1.30; 95% CI, 1.07-1.59) but not ADHD (HR, 1.03; 95% CI, 0.91-1.17). Associations for ASD were strongest during midpregnancy to late gestation compared with early gestation. Results were robust to sensitivity analyses. Conclusions and Relevance Results of this cohort study show that prenatal exposure to wildfire-related PM 2.5 may be associated with increased risk of ASD but not ADHD. These findings highlight the potential neurodevelopmental impacts of wildfire smoke and underscore the need for strategies to reduce exposure during pregnancy as wildfire activity intensifies.

items.title: SARS-CoV-2 mRNA Vaccination in Pregnancy and Child Neurodevelopment at 18 to 30 Months
items.abstract: Importance Little is known about neurodevelopmental outcomes of children exposed to SARS-CoV-2 messenger RNA (mRNA) vaccine during pregnancy. Evidence on long-term offspring outcomes after in utero exposure to SARS-CoV-2 mRNA vaccination is needed to inform vaccine recommendations in pregnancy. Objective To evaluate whether there is an association between SARS-CoV-2 vaccination during or shortly before pregnancy and offspring neurodevelopmental measures. Design, Setting, and Participants This multicenter, prospective, cohort study of 18- to 30-month-old children was conducted at 14 centers of the Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute of Child Health and Human Development Maternal-Fetal Medicine Units Network from 2024 through 2025. Women who received a SARS-CoV-2 mRNA vaccine during or within 30 days prior to pregnancy (exposed) were matched with women who did not (unexposed) by delivery site, delivery date, insurance status, and race and ethnicity. These data were analyzed from June 2025 to May 2026. Exposures Maternal receipt of at least 1 dose of an mRNA SARS-CoV-2 vaccine during, or within 30 days prior to, the index pregnancy vs no SARS-CoV-2 vaccination during pregnancy or within 30 days prior. Main Outcomes and Measures The primary outcome was Ages and Stages Questionnaire version 3 (ASQ-3) total score, which was deemed to be equivalent between the exposed and unexposed groups if the 90% CI of the median difference was between −10 and 10. Secondary outcomes included domain-specific ASQ-3 scores, the Child Behavior Checklist, Modified Checklist for Autism in Toddlers, and Early Childhood Behavior Questionnaire scores. Results Of 3956 screened, 271 exposed and 240 unexposed children were enrolled. Matching on all characteristics was possible in 217 pairs. Of the 434 children enrolled, 258 (59.4%) were Non-Hispanic White, 96 (22.1%) Non-Hispanic Black, 52 (12.0%) Hispanic, and 28 (6.5%) were not represented by any of the above racial or ethnic groups. Median age at assessment was 25.8 [24.6 to 28.3] months, 221 were female (50.9%), and 213 were male (49.1%). Exposed mothers were more likely to be nulliparous; their children were slightly younger at assessment and more likely to have been vaccinated against SARS-CoV-2. The primary outcome of ASQ-3 score was equivalent between the exposed and unexposed groups (255 vs 260, adjusted median difference, −3.4; 90% CI, −9.8 to 3.0). There were no significant differences in secondary outcomes. Conclusions and Relevance In this multicenter cohort study, ASQ-3 scores were equivalent between 18- to 30-month-old children whose mothers did or did not receive mRNA SARS-CoV-2 vaccination during or immediately prior to pregnancy. These findings support continued recommendations for SARS-CoV-2 mRNA vaccination during pregnancy.

items.title: Youth Exposure to Food and Beverage Marketing on Digital Media Platforms
items.abstract: Importance Youth are heavy users of digital devices, and digital media increasingly represents a source for unhealthy food marketing, which the World Health Organization highlights as a risk for poor diet and health. Objective To examine the extent and nature of youth exposure to food marketing on digital media across multiple platforms. Design, Setting, and Participants This cross-sectional study conducted from November 2024 to October 2025 used real-time screen capture data and surveyed screen use to estimate youth exposure to food marketing on digital media, including differences by sociodemographic characteristics. Content and nutritional analyses assessed marketed food categories, companies, and product healthfulness based on the Pan American Health Organization’s nutrient profile model (PAHO-NPM), as well as characteristics of marketing exposure. Participants included youth in the US aged 8 to 17 years. Exposure Food marketing on digital media. Main Outcomes and Measures Hours of smartphone and/or tablet device use per day and estimated median food marketing exposures per year among youth. Distribution of marketed food items by food category and company were analyzed, as was the percent exceeding the PAHO-NPM standard. Marketing exposures were reviewed by platform, source, and type. Results Participants included 1011 youth (median [IQR] age, 12 [10-15] years; 519 female [51.3%]; 511 aged 8-12 years; 500 aged 13-17 years). Participants reported spending a mean (SD) of 3.7 (1.9) hours per day using smartphones or tablets outside of school or homework activities. Estimated median number of food marketing exposures among youths was 3883 (IQR, 0-16 697) per year. Exposure was higher for adolescents vs children (10 107 [IQR, 0-26 205] per year vs 1427 [IQR, 0-7795] per year; P &lt; .001), female vs male youths (8017 [IQR, 0-25 999] per year vs 2139 [0-9027] per year; P &lt; .001), and youth with non–college-educated vs college-educated parents or guardians (5380 [IQR, 0-22 422] per year vs 3431 [IQR, 0-15 128] per year; P = .04). Exposure was higher but not significant for non-Hispanic Black vs White youth (6358 [IQR, 0-24 053] vs 3697 [IQR, 0-16 287]; P = .06). The largest food marketed categories were fast food (1983 of 6896 [28.8%]), sweets (1407 [20.4%]), and beverages (1384 [20.1%]). A total of 2437 of 2660 nonrestaurant food marketed items (91.6%) did not meet PAHO-NPM standards. A total of 4256 of 5154 food marketing exposures (82.6%) to youth were viewed on social media platforms (TikTok, 1565 of 5154 [30.4%] and YouTube, 1162 of 5154 [22.6%]). The majority of marketing exposures were paid (2703 of 5154 [52.4%]), 2261 (43.9%) were earned, and 190 (3.7%) were owned. Almost half (3231 of 6896 [46.9%]) of marketed food items were from Children’s Food and Beverage Advertising Initiative (CFBAI)–member companies. Conclusions and Relevance Results of this cross-sectional study suggest that youth exposure to unhealthy food marketing on digital media is high and differences exist across sociodemographic groups. Results that a substantial portion of exposure comes from nonpaid earned media and CFBAI-member companies highlights the complexities of and need for regulation.

Satisfaction, Regret, and Harm After Hormone Therapy in Youth From a Multidisciplinary Gender Clinic
items.abstract: Importance Concerns about regret and harm have led to restrictions on transgender and gender-diverse youths’ access to testosterone or estrogen therapy (ie, hormone therapy [HT]), while empirical data on decisional regret among those initiating HT as youth remain limited. Objectives To examine satisfaction, regret, and perceived harm among individuals who initiated HT as youth and to identify demographic and clinical characteristics associated with regret or harm and current HT status (receiving vs not). Design, Setting, and Participants This cohort study evaluates self-report surveys collected from October 2023 to October 2025 among former patients who initiated HT as youth at a single multidisciplinary gender clinic in the US. Data analysis was conducted from December 2025 to August 2026. Exposure Initiation of estrogen or testosterone. Main Outcomes and Measures Decision Regret Scale (DRS) total score (range, 0-100; higher scores indicate greater regret); item-level satisfaction, regret, and perceived harm; and current HT status. Associations with demographic and clinical characteristics were examined using nonparametric, Welch t , Fisher exact, or Pearson χ 2 tests as appropriate, with parametric sensitivity analyses for the DRS total score. Results Of the 376 participants who initiated HT as youth (112 [29.8%] initiating estrogen and 264 [70.2%] initiating testosterone; current age, 14-28 years; mean [SD] age, 20.9 [2.9] years; time since HT initiation: range, 1.2 months to 10.7 years; mean [SD], 4.9 [2.5] years), 4 were missing DRS scores, all of whom were currently receiving HT. Among the 372 respondents with DRS scores, overall decisional regret was very low (mean [SD] DRS score, 4.3 [14.7]; median [IQR], 0 [0-0]); 360 participants (96.8%) endorsed that receiving HT was the right decision, 10 (2.7%) reported regret, and 7 (1.9%) reported perceived harm. DRS scores were higher among participants not currently receiving HT vs currently receiving HT and among those identifying on the nonbinary vs binary spectrum; parametric sensitivity analyses estimated mean differences of 15.95 points (95% CI, 8.50-23.39) and 6.07 points (95% CI, 2.15-9.99), respectively. Participants not currently receiving HT (65 participants [17.3%]) were more likely than those currently receiving HT (311 [82.7%]) to have received testosterone (odds ratio, 3.58; 95% CI, 1.65-7.78; P = .001) and identify on the nonbinary spectrum (odds ratio, 8.88; 95% CI, 4.76-16.58; P &lt; .001), were older (mean difference, 1.04 years; 95% CI, 0.45-1.64 years; P = .001), and had longer time since initiating HT (mean difference, 1.00 year; 95% CI, 0.48-1.53 years; P &lt; .001). Neither regret or harm nor current HT status was associated with age at HT initiation or prepubertal gender diversity. Conclusions and Relevance The findings of this cohort study complement the literature documenting mental health benefits of HT, providing further support for existing standards of care for transgender and gender-diverse youth.
items.limitations: This study has several limitations. While the study assessed satisfaction with the decision to initiate HT, it did not examine satisfaction with the specific effects of HT. Although characteristics of participants no longer receiving HT were examined, reasons for discontinuation were not. Further, several participants reported ambivalent feelings toward HT (ie, neither agreeing nor disagreeing). Research has started to examine these treatment experiences and trajectories in greater depth among TGD adults; however, additional research specific to TGD youth is needed to support clinicians in providing developmentally informed and individualized care.

items.title: Air Pollution and Atopic Dermatitis in Children
items.abstract: Importance Atopic dermatitis is a common inflammatory skin condition that is heavily influenced by environmental factors, and while ambient air pollution has been linked to atopic dermatitis outcomes in adults, its effects in children remain more uncertain. Objective To synthesize the evidence examining the associations between ambient air pollutants and atopic dermatitis prevalence in children. Data Sources MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane databases were searched from inception to February 10, 2026. Study Selection Observational studies of children under 18 years of age that examined the association between at least 1 atopic dermatitis outcome of interest and a pollutant exposure were included. Data Extraction and Synthesis The PRISMA 2020 reporting guidelines were used; methodological quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist, and risk of bias was evaluated using the risk of bias in nonrandomized studies of exposure effects (ROBINS-E) tool. Data were synthesized using random-effects models, and certainty of evidence was assessed using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) framework. Main Outcomes and Measures The primary outcomes were health care utilization and prevalence, incidence, or severity of atopic dermatitis in relation to predefined ambient air pollutant exposures, including nitrogen dioxide (NO 2 ), sulfur dioxide (SO 2 ), particulate matter with a diameter of 10 µm or less (PM 10 ), particulate matter with a diameter of 2.5 µm or less (PM 2.5 ), ozone (O 3 ), carbon monoxide (CO), and traffic-related pollution. Results Of 2528 citations, 52 observational studies met the inclusion criteria and were included. It was found that every 10-µg/m 3 increase in NO 2 (odds ratio [OR], 3.46; 95% CI, 1.06-11.31; moderate certainty) and SO 2 (OR, 3.96; 95% CI, 1.00-15.65; moderate certainty) was probably associated with increased atopic dermatitis outpatient visits. It was also found that every 10-µg/m 3 increase in PM 2.5 (OR, 1.04; 95% CI, 1.00-1.08; moderate certainty) and PM 10 (OR, 1.19; 95% CI, 1.06-1.35; moderate certainty) was probably associated with higher atopic dermatitis prevalence. Findings were mixed or did not support associations between air pollutions exposure and incidence or severity of atopic dermatitis. Conclusions and Relevance This systematic review and meta-analysis found that increased levels of certain ambient air pollutants were probably associated with some increased population burden of atopic dermatitis in children.

items.title: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder Accommodations, Behavior Therapy, and Stimulant Medication
items.abstract: Importance Although widely deployed, little is known about the efficacy of academic accommodations for attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), alone or in combination of behavior therapy and stimulant medication. Objective To evaluate the efficacy of academic accommodations alone and in combination with behavioral interventions and stimulant medication. Design, Setting, and Participants This was a crossover randomized clinical trial with participants introduced to all conditions. Children with ADHD were enrolled in kindergarten through sixth grade. Academic accommodations were changed daily in a randomized order. Stimulant medication and placebo alternated weekly. The general classroom and enhanced behavior classroom intervention alternated every 2 weeks. The study was conducted in summer treatment program classrooms. For the present study, behavior was evaluated in (1) a classroom period where participants completed independent assignments and (2) a classroom period where participants were taught a lesson, completed small group cooperative tasks related to the lesson, and then took a quiz. Study data were analyzed from March to July 2026. Interventions The single and combined effects of academic accommodations, behavior therapy, and stimulant medication (methylphenidate, 0.3 mg/kg) were evaluated. Academic accommodations were extended time on tasks, frequent breaks during tasks, a low-distraction workspace, and the ability to stand at the desk, compared with a condition without an accommodation. A general classroom setting was compared with a classroom setting with enhanced behavior intervention. Main Outcomes and Measures Main outcomes were classroom rule violations during each of the two, 1-hour class periods, the number of seatwork items completed correctly (ie, academic productivity), and the quiz score. Results Of 306 children screened, 280 were enrolled in the study. A total of 255 children (mean [SD] age, 8.8 [1.6] months; 201 male [79%]) started the intervention, and 235 (84%) completed the study. Compared with placebo, stimulant medication increased effects related to seatwork productivity by 22% (ie, the rate ratio [RR] for this condition indicated that receiving medication compared with placebo multiplied the expected count of problems completed per minute by 1.22; 95% CI, 1.19-1.25), and quiz scores were significantly improved by 3.9 points (95% CI, 3.10-4.70 points). Medication and behavioral therapy significantly reduced classroom rule-breaking behavior by 37% (RR, 0.63; 95% CI, 0.60-0.67) and 61% (RR, 0.39; 95% CI, 0.37-0.42), respectively. There was no evidence that any of the academic accommodations significantly improved behavior or academic outcomes. No interactions were significant. Conclusions and Relevance Results of this crossover randomized clinical trial question whether school-based academic accommodations for children with ADHD should continue to be emphasized as accommodations were ineffective when used alone or in combination with other ADHD treatments. Results support the continued use of behavioral and pharmacological treatment for ADHD. Trial Registration ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05469386

items.title: Reasons for Nicotine Pouch Use Among US Youth: 2025
items.abstract: OBJECTIVE To document prevalence of reasons for nicotine pouch (NP) use and associations with use patterns among US youth. METHODS Data were from US youth reporting ever NP use in the nationally representative 2025 Monitoring the Future survey. We estimated (1) prevalence of 10 reasons for NP use (yes/no) and (2) association of each reason with past 30-day NP use (yes/no) and frequency (1–30 days). For comparison, we contrasted reasons for NP and e-cigarette use among youth reporting NP use (n = 57) or e-cigarette use (n = 397) on at least 10 of the past 30 days. RESULTS Among 484 respondents reporting ever NP use (6.1% of youth surveyed on NP use and reasons), the most common reasons were experimentation (32.3%), nicotine buzz (30.5%), relaxation (22.7%), appealing flavors (17.4%), convenience (16.5%), socializing (16.0%), boredom (11.7%), and ability to conceal use (11.0%). To quit smoking (6.2%) and feeling addicted (2.1%) were less common. Flavors, convenience, and feeling addicted were positively associated with both past 30-day NP use (prevalence ratios [PRs] range = 1.50–2.35) and frequency (incidence rate ratios [IRRs] range = 1.60–2.55). Nicotine buzz, relaxation, socializing, concealment, and to quit smoking were only associated with past 30-day use (PRs range = 1.57–1.85). Experimentation was inversely associated with frequency (IRR = 0.42). The prevalence of reasons overlapped between NPs and e-cigarettes, with relaxation, convenience, nicotine buzz, and flavors most prevalent among youth regularly using each product. CONCLUSIONS Prevention and regulatory strategies addressing NP use reasons, particularly flavors and convenience, are warranted. Existing effective strategies targeting youth nicotine vaping may be applicable to NP use.
items.limitations: Findings are subject to limitations inherent to self-report and potential sampling error. The cross-sectional design precludes causal inference. Participants selected reasons from a predefined list, which may not capture the full range or relative importance of reasons. It is also unclear how well adolescents differentiated reasons. For example, convenience could be interpreted as ease of use, ease of access, or concealability.

items.title: Children and Families Affected by Parental Substance Use: Clinical Report
items.abstract: Children and adolescents whose parents have an alcohol or substance use disorder are at increased risk of short- and long-term sequelae, ranging from medical conditions to psychosocial, safety, and behavioral challenges. In the course of providing health care services to children, pediatricians and other pediatric clinicians are likely to encounter families affected by parental substance use and are in a unique position to support the well-being of both the child and family. The purpose of this clinical report is to briefly discuss the epidemiology of substance use during pregnancy and while parenting in the United States; highlight the influence of bias, racism, and other structural inequities on families affected by substance use; describe the known risks associated with prenatal and postnatal parental substance use; discuss use and interpretation of toxicology testing as part of a substance exposure evaluation; review approaches to screening for prenatal and parental substance use; propose key topics for anticipatory guidance in the pediatric clinic; identify and address concerning parental and child presentations related to parental substance use leading to concern for child abuse or neglect; and provide recommendations for pediatric clinicians involved in the care of children from families affected by substance use.

items.title: Pediatric Hospital at Home: A Scoping Review
items.abstract: CONTEXT Hospital at Home (HaH) is an acute care model that delivers hospital-level services to the patient’s home as a substitute for conventional inpatient admission. Although pediatric HaH programs are well established internationally, the evidence base remains limited. OBJECTIVE To map the operational characteristics, outcomes, and evidence gaps of pediatric HaH programs. DATA SOURCES A comprehensive literature search was conducted for studies published between January 1, 2000, and July 25, 2025. STUDY SELECTION Eligible studies included programs with patients aged 18 years or younger and aligned with the World Hospital at Home Congress definition. DATA EXTRACTION Data were extracted on study characteristics; implementation, infrastructure, and program design; clinical safety and effectiveness; cost-effectiveness and economic impact; and patient, caregiver, and/or clinician perspectives and experiences. RESULTS Thirty-four studies met eligibility criteria. Most were observational, with few randomized or nonrandomized controlled studies. Programs varied substantially in admission pathways, staffing, eligibility criteria, monitoring, and clinical populations. Studies demonstrated low escalation and readmission rates, infrequent serious adverse events, high caregiver satisfaction, and generally comparable or lower health care costs relative to conventional inpatient care. Few studies directly evaluated clinical effectiveness, included rigorous economic analysis, or incorporated child and clinician perspectives. LIMITATIONS The literature was limited by heterogeneous study populations, program designs, outcome reporting, and variable definitions and descriptions of HaH models, introducing potential for misclassification. CONCLUSIONS Pediatric HaH shows promise as a safe and family-centered alternative to conventional hospitalization, though the existing evidence remains limited and heterogeneous, highlighting the need for more rigorous evaluation.

items.title: Developmental Trajectories of Executive Function From 2 to 13 Years in Children Born Very Preterm
items.abstract: OBJECTIVE Children born very preterm (VP; <32 weeks’ gestation) are at risk of executive function (EF) difficulties, yet limited longitudinal research has examined how these evolve from early childhood to adolescence for this population. This study described developmental trajectories of parent-reported EF from ages 2 to 13 years in children born VP and full term (FT). METHODS Participants were from the Victorian Infant Brain Study (VIBeS) longitudinal cohort comprising 224 children born VP (<30 weeks’ gestation) and 77 born FT (≥37 weeks’ gestation). EF difficulties were measured at 2, 5, 7, and 13 years using the parent-rated Behavior Rating Inventory of Executive Function (BRIEF) and its preschool version. Trajectories were estimated using multilevel mixed effects models. RESULTS EF difficulties were 0.3 to 0.7 SD higher in the VP than FT group across all BRIEF scales at each follow-up, and this difference tended to be greater in boys and those with higher socioeconomic risk. For both VP and FT groups, Global Executive Composite (GEC) and Shift T-scores increased from 2 to 13 years, Inhibit and Working Memory T-scores remained largely stable, and Emotional Control and Plan/Organize T-scores increased between 2 and 7 before stabilizing between 7 and 13 years. CONCLUSION Children born VP showed persistent EF difficulties from early childhood into adolescence, with little evidence of developmental catch-up to FT peers. These findings highlight the need for early and ongoing monitoring and intervention throughout development. Further research is needed to understand the role of sex and socioeconomic risk in the developmental course of behavioral EF difficulties.

items.title: Zika-Related Microcephaly in the First 5 Years After Birth
items.abstract: OBJECTIVE To characterize clinical manifestations and complications of children with Zika-related microcephaly in the first 5 years after birth. METHODS A cohort of children with Zika-related microcephaly were observed up to age 60 months as part of the Microcephaly Epidemic Research Group Pediatric Cohort. RESULTS Among the 181 children, 43.1% were male and 77.2% were born at term. The median birth weight was 2700 g, with 64.8% classified as small for gestational age. Notably, 22.3% were diagnosed with microcephaly after birth, and 48.8% had severe microcephaly. Most common phenotypic characteristics were craniofacial disproportion (54.1%), arthrogryposis (35.9%), and exacerbated occipital protuberance (35.5%). Approximately one-third (33.1%) presented with dysphagia (n = 151 evaluated at median age of 28.2 months), and 13.3% of children had gastrostomies (median age of 24 months). Hearing anomalies were detected in 9.7% (n = 93 evaluated at median age of 30 months). In ophthalmological evaluation, 30.4% showed changes in the retina and 28.5% in the optic nerve; strabismus was observed in 53.4%. During neurological assessment (median age at first assessment of 15.9 months), 73.8% presented with abnormalities. Imaging examinations showed ventriculomegaly and cortical atrophy in 75.3% and 64.4% of the children, respectively. Electroencephalography was performed based on clinical indication in 84 children, of whom 92.9% had pattern alterations. Over the 5 years, 62.4% were hospitalized, mainly for respiratory problems and seizures. CONCLUSIONS The study highlights the severity of Zika-related microcephaly. Future research should prioritize continued systematic monitoring of these children to understand the frequency and timing of late-onset manifestations and complications, including death.

items.title: Dual Remission of Atopic Dermatitis and Frequently Relapsing Nephrotic Syndrome With Dupilumab
items.abstract: Nephrotic syndrome in children and atopic dermatitis (AD) share a common type 2 inflammatory substrate driven by interleukin (IL)-4 and IL-13 dysregulation. We report the case of a 9-year-old girl with AD and frequently relapsing steroid-sensitive nephrotic syndrome. Given the broad atopic phenotype and increasing relapse frequency despite dual immunosuppressive therapy, dupilumab 300 mg every 2 weeks was introduced. The patient achieved rapid and complete clearance of cutaneous lesions alongside sustained complete remission of nephrotic syndrome, maintained over nearly 2 years. Both corticosteroids and tacrolimus were fully discontinued within 2 months of dupilumab initiation, with no subsequent relapse of either condition. This case supports the hypothesis that dupilumab may represent an effective steroid-sparing therapeutic option in children with nephrotic syndrome arising in an atopic context.

items.title: Correction to “A Resource to Understand and Prevent Sudden Unexpected Infant Deaths”
Erratum for “Health Outcomes in Young Children Following Pertussis Vaccination During Pregnancy”
Interpreting Safety and Immunogenicity Results From a Randomized Trial of Maternal RSV Vaccination, Infant Nirsevimab, or Both
Interpreting Interim Evidence on Sequential RSV Prevention in Infants
Literacy Promotion and Child Health: The Role of Reach Out and Read
items.abstract: This Special Article draws on a State of the Art Plenary, Literacy Promotion and Child Health: Reach Out and Read at 37, presented at the 2026 Pediatric Academic Societies meeting, which reviewed the evolution of Reach Out and Read (ROR) as a clinical intervention, a subject of research, and an increasingly incorporated component of pediatric primary care. The ROR model, supported by a national organization, now reaches 4.8 million children and families throughout the United States. Much of this growth has been driven by clinicians seeking to support family relationships, child development, and educational trajectories through primary care, especially for families at social risk. This article is based on 6 brief talks, each identified by theme and speaker, focusing on the original concept and rationale for early literacy promotion in pediatric primary care; ROR as an instrument for social justice in the context of brain development, toxic stress, and resilience; efforts to define critical elements of the intervention and strengthen them through training and engagement of both practicing clinicians and residents; a multistage collaborative research effort centering parent leaders across the ROR network in the design of the CONNECT Survey, a measure of the parent/caregiver-clinician relationship; and the crucial contribution of parent voice. Research on ROR has shown positive effects on parent reading and child vocabulary; more recent research, highlighting parent/caregiver voices, emphasizes the importance of modeling by clinicians and of the relationships between primary care clinicians and families.

items.title: Shared Clinical Decision-Making for Vaccines: Looking Backward and Ahead
Dupilumab in Pediatric Eosinophilic Esophagitis
items.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES Dupilumab is an approved biologic therapy for eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE); however, real-world pediatric data remain limited. The aim of this study is to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of dupilumab in children with EoE enrolled in the international European Society for Paediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology and Nutrition (ESPGHAN)-funded pEEr registry, with a focus on combined remission, treatment deescalation, and predictors of sustained response. METHODS DU-PED is a multicenter, retrospective cohort study including children with confirmed EoE treated with dupilumab in routine clinical practice. The primary outcome was combined remission at 6 and 12 months, defined as simultaneous clinical (≥75% Pediatric Eosinophilic Esophagitis Symptom Score [PEESS] v2.0 reduction or symptom resolution), endoscopic (EoE Endoscopic Reference Score [EREFS] ≤2), and histologic remission (<15 eos/high-power field [HPF]). Secondary outcomes included longitudinal changes in disease domains, treatment deescalation, predictors of remission, and safety. Multivariable logistic regression and ROC analysis were performed. RESULTS A total of 109 patients from 22 centers were included (median age 16 years; 75% male). Combined remission was achieved in 53% at 6 months and 86% at 12 months. PEESS v2.0, EREFS, and peak eosinophil counts significantly improved over time (P < 0.001). At 12 months, 81% of patients were receiving dupilumab monotherapy, and 94% reduced concomitant EoE-directed therapy. Higher baseline proximal eosinophil density was independently associated with a lower likelihood of sustained combined remission at 12 months (odds ratio 0.98, 95% CI 0.96–0.99). Dupilumab was well tolerated, with no treatment discontinuations. CONCLUSIONS In a large international registry-based pediatric cohort, dupilumab achieved high and durable rates of combined remission and enabled substantial treatment simplification, supporting its role as an effective long-term treatment strategy for pediatric EoE.

items.title: Racial and Ethnic Differences in Pediatric Perioperative Cardiac Arrest Survival
items.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE Perioperative cardiac arrest (POCA) is associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. Disparities in perioperative outcomes have been reported, but whether similar differences exist following pediatric POCA remains unclear.
