We evaluated racial and ethnic differences in 30-day mortality after pediatric POCA. METHOD Within the American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program for Pediatrics (NSQIP-P) registry, we identified 2646 children under 18 who underwent inpatient, noncardiac surgery (2012─2024) and experienced POCA. Race and ethnicity were categorized as Hispanic, non-Hispanic Asian, non-Hispanic Black or African American, non-Hispanic white, or other. Crude and adjusted risk ratios for 30-day mortality following POCA were estimated. RESULTS Among 2646 children with POCA, 47.9% (n = 1268) were non-Hispanic white, 28.2% (n = 745) non-Hispanic Black, 4.0% (n = 106) non-Hispanic Asian, 16.2% (n = 430) Hispanic and 3.7% (n = 97) Other race. Overall, 30-day mortality was 32.9% (871/2646). Mortality was similar across racial or ethnic groups (P = .72). In adjusted analyses, mortality risk did not differ significantly for non-Hispanic Black (adjusted relative risks [aRR] 1.02, P = .80), Hispanic children (aRR 1.06, P = .43), or children of other race (aRR 1.02, P = .88) compared with non-Hispanic white children. Emergent surgery (aRR 1.62, P < .001) and preoperative inotrope use (aRR 1.41, P < .001) were independently associated with increased mortality. CONCLUSION We found no significant racial or ethnic differences in mortality risk following POCA among children undergoing inpatient surgery. Mortality was associated with clinical and perioperative factors, including emergent surgery and preoperative inotrope use. This suggests that efforts to identify drivers of disparities in pediatric postsurgical mortality must look beyond POCA outcomes alone.

items.title: Complications in Pediatric Cancer Patients With Staphylococcus aureus Bloodstream Infection
items.abstract: BACKGROUND Staphylococcus aureus bloodstream infections (BSIs) can cause significant morbidity in children with cancer. Current guidelines recommend central venous catheter (CVC) removal, though the necessity remains uncertain. We assessed risk factors for complications among affected patients, focusing on impact of CVC removal vs salvage. METHODS This multicenter retrospective study includes pediatric oncology patients with S aureus BSIs from 2005 to 2022. The complication outcome period (72 hours to 6 months after initial positive culture) was divided into short-term (72 hours to 8 days) and late periods (8 days to 6 months). The composite primary outcome included occurrence of at least 1 major complication: recurrent BSIs, deep abscess/myositis, S aureus–related death, exit site infection, meningitis, endocarditis, or osteomyelitis. Multivariable logistic regression with propensity score weighting for CVC removal was performed. RESULTS Among 322 BSI episodes, 90.7% (n = 292/322) had a CVC at presentation; salvage was attempted in 55.5% (n = 162/292). The primary outcome was met in 21.2% (n = 62/292) of episodes with a CVC, more frequently in the CVC salvage (25.3%, n = 41/161) vs removal (16.2%, n = 21/130) group. CVC salvage was independently associated with the primary outcome (OR, 3.37; 95% CI, 2.08–5.61; P < .01) in short-term (OR, 21.8; 95% CI, 7.09–95.4) and late (OR, 1.83; 95% CI, 1.06–3.18) periods. Methicillin resistance, male sex, invasive infection at presentation, implanted ports, sepsis, and persistent blood culture positivity were also independently associated with the primary outcome. CONCLUSIONS CVC removal was associated with fewer short-term and late complications in pediatric cancer patients with S aureus BSIs, supporting recommendations for catheter removal in this population.

items.title: Middle Lobe Displacement Post Lobectomy in a Child With Congenital Pulmonary Airway Malformation
items.abstract: Congenital pulmonary airway malformations (CPAMs) are an important cause of structural lung disease in children and may remain undetected until later childhood. Although surgical resection is well established for symptomatic lesions, the long-term anatomical effects of lobectomy in pediatric patients remain incompletely understood. Postoperative changes in lung mechanics and lobar positioning can result in uncommon airway complications that are often under-recognized and diagnostically challenging. Obstruction of the right middle lobe (RML) bronchus due to postoperative lobar displacement is particularly rare, with reported cases originating from the adult surgical literature. We report a 9-year-old girl with mild persistent asthma who presented with an infected cystic lesion in the right upper lobe consistent with CPAM. She completed antimicrobial therapy and underwent right upper lobectomy, with pathology confirming type 1 CPAM. One month later, she developed a persistent cough refractory to optimized asthma treatment. Chest computed tomography (CT) demonstrated hyperinflation and poor visualization of the right upper and middle lobe bronchial orifices. Bronchoscopy identified RML bronchial obstruction, and fluoroscopy-guided bronchoscopy confirmed superior displacement of the RML with resultant bronchial kinking, likely related to postoperative lobar migration. Endobronchial stenting was unsuccessful, and further surgical intervention was not advised because of the anticipated risks of a second operation. Conservative management was pursued, resulting in modest symptomatic improvement, with the patient remaining clinically stable for 2 years. This case highlights a rare postoperative complication of CPAM resection in a child and emphasizes the need for heightened awareness, multidisciplinary evaluation, and pediatric-focused studies to guide management.

items.title: Penicillin Allergy Delabeling in Children
items.abstract: Nearly 10% of the global population has been labeled as having a penicillin allergy. Of those labeled, about 95% are not truly allergic, yet most do not receive any allergy evaluations. Patients with penicillin allergy labels are more likely to have worse clinical outcomes and incur higher health care costs, largely because they do not receive penicillin and other first-line β-lactam antibiotics for the treatment of infectious diseases. Consequently, the process of evaluating and removing inaccurate penicillin allergy labels—a process known as “delabeling”—has become increasingly supported by a growing body of evidence. Recently, penicillin allergy has garnered substantial public interest with the proposal of federal legislation to include evaluation of penicillin allergy during routine medical visits for Medicare patients. Although this moves delabeling into the generalist purview, most of the emphasis on penicillin allergies and delabeling has been on adult patients. Yet, penicillin allergy is a pressing issue for pediatrics, as most penicillin allergy labels are placed in childhood. Pediatric literature similarly demonstrates negative clinical and public health consequences of inaccurate penicillin allergy labels. Recent guidelines have strongly recommended a proactive effort to identify and delabel inaccurate penicillin allergies in children. To facilitate this process, simple delabeling procedures, such as direct oral challenge with amoxicillin, have been recommended for patients with low-risk allergy status, based on historical reaction verification, because of their safety and accuracy. These advancements are relevant to practicing pediatricians across specialties and practice locations.

items.title: Islamic Fatwa Guiding the Use of Pasteurized Donor Human Milk
items.abstract: Neonatologists noted hesitancy in Minnesota’s Muslim community to use pasteurized donor human milk, even when medically advised for premature and ill babies, due in part to religious concerns about milk kinship. To address these concerns and promote equitable health outcomes, we forged a coalition of partners including the Minnesota Islamic Council, Children’s Minnesota, M Health Fairview/University of Minnesota, Minnesota Milk Bank for Babies, Brighter Health Minnesota, and the Minnesota Breastfeeding Coalition. On Nov 16th, 2023, the Minnesota Islamic Council issued a fatwa, or a religious clarification, encouraging the use of pasteurized donor human milk for babies when a mother’s own milk is not available. The fatwa provides information on the health benefits of human milk for newborns, clarifies Islamic teachings, and encourages the use of donor human milk when indicated. This is believed to be the first fatwa regarding donor milk use in the United States, although there are precedents in other countries. We believe that this landmark decision, along with collaboratively developed patient and family education materials, will help clinicians across the country navigate conversations with Muslim families about pasteurized donor human milk in an empathetic and culturally sensitive manner, while simultaneously improving outcomes for babies and decreasing disparities. This effort also serves as an example to pediatricians interested in addressing specific religious or cultural concerns about an aspect of pediatric care in a community-centered manner.

items.title: Low-Level Pyuria and Antibiotic Prescribing for Suspected Urinary Tract Infection in Children
items.abstract: OBJECTIVE Our objective was to understand the impact of urinalysis results on clinician antibiotic prescribing for pediatric patients evaluated at ambulatory visits. We hypothesized that responses to low pyuria levels contribute disproportionately to overtreatment. METHODS This cross-sectional study combined electronic health record and abstracted symptom data from emergency department and urgent care visits to 4 Northern California settings. We sampled ambulatory visits by patients aged between 2 months and 17 years who underwent urinalysis between January 1, 2022, and December 31, 2023. We used multivariable logistic regression to assess relationships between urinalysis results, clinical covariates including age, and empiric antibiotic initiation. We estimated attributable impact of these relationships on overtreatment for patients in whom urinary tract infection (UTI) was excluded by culture criteria. We similarly estimated impact on treatment for those with culture-confirmed UTI. RESULTS Among 1150 patients with median age 6.3 years, 191 (16.6%) received antibiotics. Low pyuria levels (trace leukocyte esterase, 10-69 white blood cells [WBC]/mm,3 5-10 WBC/high-power field) were associated with antibiotic initiation with adjusted odds ratio 6.62 (95% CI 3.72–11.79) compared with no pyuria. The adjusted attributable fraction (aAF) for overtreatment at this level was 17.0% (95% CI 10.3%-23.2%), with aAF 1.8% (95% CI 1.1%-2.4%) for UTI treatment. Differential impacts on overtreatment and UTI treatment were consistent in age-stratified analyses. CONCLUSIONS To promote selective UTI treatment, clinicians should consider degree of pyuria in context with age, risk factors, symptoms, and other urinalysis results. Health system interventions should be designed to mitigate excess influence of low pyuria levels and promote integrated diagnostic assessments.

items.title: Facial Dysmorphism in Infants Following Combined Prenatal Exposure to Alcohol and Tobacco
items.abstract: OBJECTIVES Alcohol and smoking have well-established teratogenic effects; however, despite their frequent co-use during pregnancy, the combined impact on fetal development remains less understood. Facial dysmorphism is a sensitive marker of embryonic disruption. This study investigated whether concomitant prenatal exposure to alcohol and tobacco exerts synergistic effects on infant facial dysmorphism, facial size, and growth trajectories. METHODS This longitudinal study included 634 infants from a high-risk population in South Africa. Prenatal alcohol and smoking behaviors were assessed using a modified timeline follow-back interview at each visit, capturing frequency and quantity. Three-dimensional facial images were obtained at 1 month and 1 year postnatally. Infants were categorized into 5 exposure groups: control, continuous alcohol only, continuous smoking only, continuous coexposure, and continuous smoking with any alcohol. Group differences were evaluated using anthropometric measurements and dense surface modeling to assess facial dysmorphism, size, and growth trajectories. RESULTS Continuous prenatal coexposure to smoking and alcohol was associated with the greatest facial dysmorphism and reduced facial size compared to controls and single-exposure groups. Effects were largely sex specific, with stronger alterations in girls. Coexposure was also associated with ocular changes, including reduced palpebral fissure length and increased canthal index. Single exposures showed more limited effects, and facial growth trajectories were not significantly influenced by exposure. CONCLUSIONS Combined prenatal exposure to alcohol and tobacco is associated with greater facial dysmorphism than single exposures. These findings highlight the importance of interventions targeting alcohol and smoking cessation during pregnancy to reduce teratogenic risk.

items.title: Increasing Chlamydia/Gonorrhea Screening in Adolescents Across a Multisite Primary Care Network
items.abstract: OBJECTIVE To increase chlamydia and gonorrhea (CT/GC) screening among sexually active female adolescents in a large pediatric primary care network using a multifaceted quality improvement (QI) intervention, with secondary aims to increase male screening and case detection. METHODS From 2021 to 2025, we implemented a sequential QI intervention including Adolescent Health Questionnaire implementation, financial incentives, electronic health record (EHR) best practice advisories, and universal screening protocols across 33 practices. The primary outcome was CT/GC screening rates for sexually active female patients aged at least 15 years at well visits. Secondary outcomes included male screening rates and case detection rates. We evaluated outcomes using statistical process control and run charts. RESULTS During the study period, 136 241 adolescents aged 15–19 years received care across the network, with monthly well care visits increasing over time (average 1472-1681 visits/month). CT/GC screening rates for sexually active female patients increased from approximately 25% to 75%, with the most substantial improvements following universal opt-out protocols. Male testing rates similarly increased from approximately 20% to 75%. Monthly chlamydia case counts for female patients increased from approximately 8 cases/month to a peak of approximately 25 cases/month during the highest-volume testing period. For male patients, cases increased from approximately 4 to 16 monthly. Improvements occurred across demographic groups regardless of insurance type, race, or ethnicity. CONCLUSIONS A systematic, EHR-enabled QI intervention significantly improved adolescent CT/GC screening rates while increasing case detection. Universal opt-out screening protocols proved most effective in achieving comprehensive screening and identifying previously undiagnosed infections, demonstrating the clinical value of systematic CT/GC screening in pediatric primary care.

items.title: Parent Perceptions of Australia’s Social Media Minimum Age Law
Human in the Loop Might Not Be Enough: Large Language Model Oversight in Pediatrics
Father-Inclusive Perinatal Obesity Prevention: A Randomized Clinical Trial
items.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES Although fathers influence early child feeding, growth, and health behaviors, they are rarely included in early life obesity prevention interventions. We hypothesized that the father-inclusive First Heroes program would reduce rapid infant weight gain and improve parental weight-related and health behavior outcomes. METHODS We conducted a randomized controlled trial (2020-2023) in a Massachusetts health care system, enrolling 227 English- or Spanish-speaking mother-father dyads during the second trimester. Dyads were randomized to the First Heroes intervention—three virtual health coaching sessions plus multimedia content from pregnancy through 12 months postpartum—vs safety education control group. Primary outcomes were odds of rapid infant weight gain from birth to 6 and 12 months and infant overweight at 12 months. Secondary outcomes included maternal postpartum weight retention, paternal body mass index (BMI) change, and parent health care and infant-care behaviors. RESULTS Among 194 infants, intervention participants had lower odds of rapid infant weight gain vs control participants at 6 months (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.42; 95% CI, 0.19–0.93) and 12 months (aOR, 0.49; 95% CI, 0.25–0.99); however, there was no difference in odds of infant overweight between groups. Fathers in the intervention vs control group had greater BMI reduction at 6 months postpartum (adjusted difference, −1.08; 95% CI, −2.06 to −0.11). Maternal weight outcomes were not significantly different by randomization group. CONCLUSIONS The First Heroes trial was associated with improvements in rapid infant weight gain, although other primary infant growth outcomes were not significantly different between groups. Future studies should examine strategies to sustain family-based obesity prevention across infancy.

items.title: Engaging Fathers and Mothers to Promote Responsive Feeding and Healthy Infant Growth
Supporting the Health and Well-Being of Youth Aging Out of Foster Care: Policy Statement
items.abstract: This policy statement examines disparities and structural barriers affecting youth aging out of foster care and evaluates existing policy efforts, such as extended foster care and Medicaid expansion, that have expanded access to care but remain constrained by administrative complexity, workforce shortages, and fragmented systems of care. This statement provides policy recommendations to improve outcomes for this population, including centering lived experience in policy development, strengthening collaboration between pediatricians and child welfare systems, expanding access to extended foster care, and enhancing transition planning for health care. Pediatricians play a key role in advocacy and trauma-informed care to support successful transitions to adulthood.

items.title: Advancing Pediatric Workforce Diversity and Culturally Effective Health Care for a Changing US Child Population: Policy Recommendations for Change: Policy Statement
items.abstract: This policy statement provides recommendations on enhancing pediatrician workforce diversity and providing culturally effective health care (CEHC). It highlights the barriers that racism and other biases create in providing culturally effective pediatric care and achieving child health equity. There are 3 interconnected areas needing greater attention: 1) expanding the underrepresented in medicine (URiM) candidate pool through fostering health career aspirations among diverse youth; 2) enhancing recruitment, retention, and leadership development of URiM pediatricians through facilitating health care system change; and 3) advancing CEHC delivery through synergistic efforts addressing care during clinical encounters, ability to access care, and ongoing improvement processes.

items.title: A Community-Engaged Research Partnership to Address Behavioral Health Inequities in ADHD Care
Weight Estimation and Dose Calculation in Resuscitation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
items.abstract: CONTEXT The accuracy of instruments to estimate weight and calculate drug doses in children requiring medications during resuscitation is a critical patient safety issue. OBJECTIVE To determine if length-based tapes were superior to other instruments for drug dose calculation or improved the accuracy of weight estimation, time to drug administration, drug dose accuracy, or clinical outcomes during resuscitation. METHODS We systematically reviewed Embase, PubMed, and the Cochrane Library from inception to December 19, 2025. Systematic reviews, randomized controlled trials, nonrandomized studies were included. Country, sample size, study design, and results were extracted. RESULTS In the 250 included studies, 9 enrolled children requiring resuscitation. Compared with the Broselow tape, the PAWPER tape (a length-based tape with habitus correction) was superior for time to drug administration, drug dose accuracy, and weight estimation accuracy in all analyses. In direct paired meta-comparison for the proportions of estimates within 10% (P10), the PAWPER tape was superior to the Broselow tape (odds ratio, 2.48; 95% CI, 2.04–3.02]). All age-based formulas were consistently inaccurate (P10 < 50%). Findings were consistent across countries classified by income levels. There were no patient outcomes data. Children exceeding the length of the tape and children with skeletal deformities and growth restrictions were excluded from many source studies. CONCLUSIONS There were no studies of patient outcomes for instruments calculating drug dosing during resuscitation. Time to drug administration, drug dose, and weight estimation accuracy were superior with a length-based tape with body habitus correction compared with tapes without habitus correction in all populations.

items.title: Adolescent Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy Can Be the First Clue to Multisystem Mitochondrial Disease
items.abstract: Up to 40% of children with mitochondrial disease develop hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) during their disease course, but HCM is almost never the first presenting manifestation. When it is, the underlying mitochondrial disorder is easily missed: the cardiomyopathy is managed in isolation, and extracardiac findings that emerge later may be dismissed as unrelated. We describe an adolescent whose severe HCM was the first major manifestation of clinicopathologically confirmed multisystem mitochondrial disease with a phenotype consistent with Leber hereditary optic neuropathy. Her cardiomyopathy was managed in isolation for over a year before optic atrophy, primary ovarian insufficiency, osteopenia, and exercise intolerance were ultimately recognized as part of a single mitochondrial process. Endomyocardial and skeletal muscle biopsy confirmed mitochondrial pathology. The diagnosis directly changed management: cofactor supplementation was initiated, her visual acuity stabilized on idebenone, and perioperative planning for transplantation was adapted to prevent catabolic decompensation. Her cardiac disease progressed to heart failure requiring transplantation at age 16 years, but she remains clinically stable with preserved graft function more than 15 years later. This case challenges the assumption that mitochondrial disease should enter the differential only after neurologic dysfunction appears. General pediatricians, who see the whole child longitudinally, are uniquely positioned to recognize when dysfunction in other high-energy tissues points toward a unifying mitochondrial diagnosis in a child with cardiomyopathy.

items.title: To Test or Not to Test? A Dilemma in Prenatal Testing for an Adult-Onset Genetic Condition
items.abstract: Pediatric genetic testing for adult-onset genetic conditions is controversial and generally not recommended because of concerns about protecting a future child’s autonomy to decide as an adult whether to know their genetic status. Yet, preimplantation genetic testing of embryos and prenatal diagnosis of fetuses for adult-onset genetic conditions are routinely offered to at-risk prospective parents when parents intend to select unaffected embryos or terminate an affected pregnancy to avoid having a child with the condition. These commentaries consider a case in which expecting parents (1 of whom is at risk) request prenatal testing for Huntington disease (HD), a genetic, progressive, adult-onset neurological condition, but do not intend to terminate the pregnancy if affected. Such situations highlight the tension between protecting a potential child’s interest in an open future and honoring prospective parents’ reproductive autonomy and ability to make decisions that they determine to be in the best interests of their family and future child. The first commentary highlights ethical distinctions in the case from obstetric and pediatric perspectives. The second commentary considers the role of parental reason-giving in shifting ethical reasoning and deliberation between prenatal and pediatric frames of reference. The third commentary, from the perspective of an HD community member, offers reflections on the breadth of personal and family experiences of HD that may inform choices about prenatal testing. The fourth commentary considers clinicians’ process-related obligations while counseling families about prenatal testing for adult-onset conditions to argue for a shared decision-making model.

items.title: Primary Care Spending as a Proportion of Total Spending for Children vs Adults
items.abstract: BACKGROUND A crisis in primary care access for adults has led to calls to increase primary care spending to specific targets. It is unknown whether the same targets for primary care spending should be used in pediatrics since total and primary care spending patterns differ between adults and children. METHODS We determined percent of total spending devoted to primary care and average expenditures, along with trends over 20 years, by payer type (commercial vs. Medicaid) and age group, using the Medical Expenditure Panel Survey. RESULTS Primary care share averaged 8% during this period across all ages without significant change over time. Pediatrics (0-18 years) averaged 17.0%, partly reflecting lower total spending in pediatrics (fewer hospitalizations, expensive surgeries, and medications). Average expenditures ranged from $2,767 for 0-18 y.o. to $14,429 for elder adults. Primary care share was lower for children insured by Medicaid (11.7%), likely reflecting higher rates of chronic and complex conditions. Among all children, per capita primary care spend was $470, but varied from $276 for those on Medicaid to $494 for commercially-insured children. CONCLUSIONS Lower total pediatric expenditures partly reflect less high-cost need, but also high rates of Medicaid coverage with low payment. Pediatric primary care will benefit from increasing primary care percent spend and improvements in financing pediatric care. As percent expenditure on primary care for children is already higher than for older populations, simply raising it to a specific target (e.g., 15%) will benefit pediatrics less than other strategies (e.g., doubling primary care spend).

items.title: Bringing Children Into the Primary Care Investment Debate
items.abstract: The work of pediatrician Barbara Starfield established that primary care is unique. Defined by first-contact access, continuity, comprehensiveness, and coordination—and delivered through enduring relationships with patients and families—primary care provides the essential foundation for any high-performing health care system. Yet the United States has persistently underinvested in that foundation, leaving primary care practices chronically under resourced.1 Recognizing this crisis for the overall population, states and national organizations are measuring primary care spending, setting explicit investment targets, and pressing to rebalance the health care dollar toward primary care. Although these approaches differ in payer scope, definitions, and enforcement, they share a central premise: within a constrained health care budget, greater investment in primary care must be intentional rather than left to market forces. One recent expression of this movement, the Triple Double campaign, calls for doubling primary care investment from 5% to 10% of health care spending, while also doubling its reach and the proportion of the next generation choosing primary care.2 In this issue of Pediatrics, Perrin et al ask an essential question that this movement has largely left unanswered: What should primary care investment policy mean for children?3

items.title: Are They Flourishing? Enhancing Learner Well-Being in the Clinical Learning Environment
Gestational Age–Associated Pathogen Distributions in Very Preterm Infants With Sepsis
Beyond Croup: A Phenotype-Based Perspective on Parainfluenza Virus Types in Children
items.abstract: Human parainfluenza viruses (PIVs) caused an estimated 18.8 million acute lower respiratory infection episodes, 725 000 hospitalizations, and 34 400 deaths among children under 5 in 2018, ranking second only to respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). Despite this burden, clinical attention has historically focused on croup, leading to the common perception that parainfluenza is a single disease entity. However, the 4 types differ substantially in taxonomy, tropism, clinical syndrome, and severity. PIV-1, the most common cause of croup, drives biennial epidemics in toddlers, whereas PIV-2 is less frequent but can cause severe disease, particularly in children with underlying conditions. PIV-3 predominates in young infants, causing bronchiolitis and pneumonia clinically like RSV infection, reflecting its early postnatal susceptibility, which may relate to earlier and more frequent viral exposure. PIV-4, historically underrecognized due to culture limitations, usually does not cause croup but is linked to lower respiratory tract disease, hypoxemia, and occasional neurologic complications. PIV infections are most severe in infants, immunocompromised children, and those in low-resource settings. Seasonal patterns vary by type and geography. Advances in multiplex molecular diagnostics now allow rapid type-specific detection, improving clinical interpretation and management. No vaccine or antiviral is licensed. Emerging therapeutics include sialidase-based antivirals with Food and Drug Administration Breakthrough designation; monoclonal antibodies capable of cross-neutralizing PIV-1, PIV-3, RSV, and human metapneumovirus; and messenger RNA vaccines showing early immunogenicity in children. Recognizing the distinct epidemiology, clinical features, and immune responses of each type is critical for informed pediatric care and the development of targeted preventive and therapeutic strategies.

items.title: Mental Health Diagnoses Among Children With and Without Complex and Chronic Conditions
items.abstract: OBJECTIVES Mental health (MH) diagnoses can complicate outcomes of underlying medical conditions. However, prevalence of MH diagnoses across the spectrum of complex and/or chronic conditions is poorly understood. We aimed to (1) compare prevalence of MH diagnoses across categories of complex and chronic conditions and (2) identify factors associated with MH diagnoses among children with noncomplex chronic conditions (NCCCs) and complex chronic conditions (CCCs). METHODS Retrospective cross-sectional study of 2.9 million children aged 5 to 17 years from MarketScan Medicaid Database representing 12 US states in 2022. The primary exposure was mutually exclusive categories of complex and chronic conditions: noncomplex nonchronic (NCNC) conditions, NCCCs, and CCCs. The outcome was presence of a mood or anxiety MH diagnosis (anxiety, depression, bipolar disorder, obsessive-compulsive disorders, trauma-related disorders, and suicide/self-injury) coded at 1 inpatient/emergency department or 2 outpatient encounters. RESULTS Prevalence of MH diagnoses increased with increasing medical complexity and chronicity: 7.6% in NCNC, 16.0% in NCCCs, and 20.0% in CCCs (P < .001). Among children with a CCC, categories with the greatest adjusted odds of MH diagnoses were cardiac (odds ratio [OR] 1.49; 95% CI, 1.44–1.54), neurologic (OR 1.18; 95% CI, 1.14–1.23), and renal (OR 1.13; 95% CI, 1.06–1.21). Among youth with NCCCs or CCCs, Black and Hispanic children had lower odds of MH diagnoses compared to non-Hispanic white children. CONCLUSIONS MH prevalence increased significantly with increasing medical complexity and chronicity. Differences in MH diagnoses were identified across individual NCCC and CCC categories and sociodemographic characteristics. These results may inform future screening, intervention, and health equity efforts among medically vulnerable populations.

items.title: Timing of the Adrenaline Administration in Witnessed Pediatric Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: Retrospective, National Cohort Study in Japan, Using a 2014–2020 Dataset
items.abstract: Objectives: We evaluated the association between the timing of initial adrenaline administration and outcomes in witnessed pediatric out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA). Design: A multicenter, retrospective cohort study addressing resuscitation time bias by performing a risk-set matching analysis using time-dependent propensity scores. Setting: Analysis of data from the Japanese Association for Acute Medicine OHCA (JAAM-OHCA) registry, which is a nationwide, multicenter, prospective collection of prehospital and in-hospital data involving Japanese patients with OHCA. Patients: Pediatric patients (< 18 yr) with witnessed OHCA who received adrenaline, during the period June 2014 to December 2020. Interventions: None. Measurements and Main Results: We compared patients who received adrenaline in specific time intervals (1–10, 11–15, 16–20, 21–25, or 26–30 min) after first contact with emergency medical services with those who still had not received adrenaline during the same time. The primary and secondary outcomes were survival and favorable neurologic outcome at one month, defined as a Pediatric Cerebral Performance Category score of 1–3. We identified a total of 259 OHCA patients who had received adrenaline at 1–10, 11–15, 16–20, 21–25, 26–30, and 31 minutes or later; at each respective time point, there were 15, 39, 62, 55, 37, and 51 patients. Risk ratios (RRs) with 95% CIs for 1-month survival at each time group compared with patients at risk were: 1–10 minutes, RR, 2.94 (95% CI, 0.38–22.81); 11–15 minutes, RR, 0.97 (95% CI, 0.30–3.12); 16–20 minutes, RR, 1.00 (95% CI, 0.29–3.48); 21–25 minutes, RR, 1.35 (95% CI, 0.54–3.40); and 26–30 minutes, RR, 1.71 (95% CI, 0.27–10.78). We failed to identify an association between time interval and greater or lesser probability of survival or neurologic outcome. Conclusions: In the JAAM-OHCA registry, with pediatric data from 2014 to 2020, we failed to identify an association between earlier adrenaline administration and greater probability of 1-month survival or favorable neurologic outcomes.

items.title: Extubation Failure and Duration of Respiratory Support Postextubation in Children: Australian and New Zealand Multicenter, ICU Registry Data, 2014–2021
items.abstract: Objectives: To compare postextubation failure and duration of noninvasive respiratory support postextubation in children receiving continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) or high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC). Design: Retrospective cohort using the Australian and New Zealand Pediatric Intensive Care (ANZPIC) registry. Setting: Ten PICUs and 24 mixed adult/pediatric units. Patients: All children extubated between 2014 and 2021 who required noninvasive respiratory support. Interventions: None. Measurements: Postextubation failure rate requiring reintubation and duration of noninvasive respiratory support. Secondary outcomes were length of stay (LOS) in the PICU, time from extubation to discharge from the PICU, hospital LOS, and prevalence of death during hospital admission. Results: Of 31,910 extubation episodes in 23,930 children, 7,156 children received noninvasive respiratory support. Propensity matching yielded 1418 pairs for CPAP and HFNC. We failed to identify an association between postextubation failure and the use of CPAP vs. HFNC (107/1418 [7.6%] vs. 115/1418 [8.1%]; rate ratio, 0.93 [95% CI, 0.72–1.25]). There was an associated difference in median (interquartile range [IQR]) duration of postextubation respiratory support when CPAP was compared with HFNC, 72.0 hours (IQR, 30.5–72.0 hr) vs. 30.5 hours (IQR, 17.2–72.0 hr); median difference, 41.5 hours (95% CI, 37.7–45.2 hr). Median PICU LOS on CPAP vs. HFNC was 10.2 days (IQR, 5.1–20.9 d) vs. 7.1 days (IQR, 3.9–14.3 d); median difference, 2.2 days (95% CI, 1.6–2.8 d). Use of HFNC as opposed to CPAP was associated with shorter PICU LOS postextubation and hospital LOS. Last, we failed to identify an association between postextubation support and in-hospital mortality. Conclusions: In the ANZPIC registry, 2014–2021 dataset, we failed to identify an association between type of postextubation form of respiratory support and postextubation failure rate. However, being supported with CPAP as opposed to HFNC was associated with longer duration of postextubation respiratory support in the PICU.

items.title: Prevalence and Outcomes of Refeeding Syndrome in Critically Ill Children: A Retrospective Study in a Tertiary Care Setting
items.abstract: Objectives: To determine the prevalence and outcome of refeeding syndrome in critically ill children admitted to the PICU. Design: Retrospective cohort study. Setting: Single PICU in a tertiary care university-affiliated hospital. Patients: Children of age 1 month to 18 years hospitalized in the PICU between January 2018 and December 2022 were included in this study. Intervention: None. Measurement and Main Results: We identified children with refeeding syndrome based on the 2020 guidelines established by the American Society for Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition. The outcomes measured included length of hospitalization, complications, and mortality rates. During the study period, a total of 404 children were admitted to the PICU, with 94 children (23.3%) classified as undernourished. Refeeding syndrome was diagnosed in 53 children (13.1%). Comorbidity with chronic neurologic conditions was prominently associated with greater adjusted odds of refeeding syndrome. An increase in BMI was associated with lower odds of developing refeeding syndrome. The median duration of hospital stay was significantly longer for children with refeeding syndrome compared with those without it. Conclusions: This study suggests that children at greater risk of developing refeeding syndrome were those with comorbid chronic neurologic conditions. Close monitoring of metabolic disturbances is crucial in the care of these patients.

items.title: Peripheral IV Catheter Longevity With Ultrasound Guidance in the PICU: Single-Center Retrospective Cohort, 2016–2018
items.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To compare associated outcomes between ultrasound-guided peripheral IV catheter (USGPIV) insertion and device longevity in critically ill children. DESIGN: Retrospective observational cohort study. SETTING: Tertiary medical-surgical pediatric PICU with cardiac patients. PATIENTS: Patients admitted to the PICU requiring peripheral vascular access between January 1, 2016, and October 1, 2018. INTERVENTIONS: None. MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: We identified patients who underwent USGPIV and landmark-guided peripheral IV catheters (LMGPIV) placed within 2 weeks of a USGPIV, and made comparisons between the procedures. There were 507 USGPIV and 292 LMGPIV placements. Of these, 334 USGPIV and 278 LMGPIV had longevity data. Log-rank analysis with median (interquartile range, IQR) data showed an associated greater catheter longevity in USGPIVs vs. LMGPIVs, respectively: 5 days (IQR, 2–9 d) vs. 3 days (IQR, 1–4 d), p value of less than 0.001. When restricted to either patients admitted with cardiac disease or those with known difficult vascular access, the association between USGPIVs and LMGPIVs and greater longevity remained, respectively: cardiac cases, 5 days (IQR, 2–9 d) vs. 3 days (IQR, 2–6 d); p = 0.038 and difficult access, 5 days (IQR, 2–9 d) vs. 2 days (IQR, 1–4 d), p value of less than 0.001. CONCLUSIONS: In this single-center experience of using USGPIV placement over 28 months (2016–2018), USGPIV placement was associated with greater catheter longevity. These findings suggest that USGPIV placement is potentially a means for improving PIV insertion and maintenance.

items.title: Lung Morphology Assessed by Ultrasound and Positive End-Expiratory Pressure During Mechanical Ventilation for Acute Hypoxemic Respiratory Failure: Secondary Analysis of a Multicenter PICU Cohort From Spain and Portugal, 2020–2021
items.abstract: Objectives: In pediatric patients with acute hypoxemic respiratory failure (AHRF), we aimed to determine whether positive end-expiratory pressure alignment with lung ultrasound (LUS) morphology was associated with shortened duration of mechanical ventilation. Design: Exploratory, secondary analysis of a prospective, multicenter cohort study carried out in 2020–2021. Setting: Twenty-five PICUs in Spain and Portugal. Patients: Children from 1 month to 18 years with AHRF undergoing invasive mechanical ventilation. Interventions: None. Measurements and Main Results: Data from lung morphology using a 12-zone LUS score between 12 and 48–72 hours after PICU admission were classified as focal or nonfocal. PEEP was considered “aligned with morphology” when greater than or equal to 10 cmH 2 O in cases with nonfocal lung morphology, and less than 10 cmH 2 O in cases with focal morphology. The primary outcome was ventilator-free days (VFDs) at 28 days, analyzed using competing-risk regression and reported as the subdistribution hazard ratio (SHR) with 95% CI. Among 160 children, 101 children (63.1%) had nonfocal morphology. PEEP was aligned with morphology in 84 of 160 children (52.5%). Aligned vs. nonaligned PEEP was associated with lower median (interquartile range [IQR]) driving pressure (13 cmH 2 O [IQR, 12–15 cmH 2 O] vs. 16 cmH 2 O [IQR, 15–18 cmH 2 O]; p < 0.001) and higher median VFDs (22 [IQR, 19–24] vs. 17 [IQR, 12–19]; p < 0.001). In adjusted competing-risk models, PEEP alignment with lung morphology was associated with greater cumulative probability of extubation at 28 days (SHR, 1.87 [95% CI, 1.30–2.69]). Stratified analyses confirmed the associated greater probability for both focal (SHR, 1.96 [95% CI, 1.20–3.21]) and nonfocal morphology cases (SHR, 2.23 [95% CI, 1.30–3.82]). Conclusions: In pediatric cases of AHRF, lung ultrasound-defined morphology identifies clinical and physiologic heterogeneity. PEEP aligned with LUS morphology was associated with greater cumulative probability of extubation at 28 days. These multicenter data from Spain and Portugal (2020–2021) suggest that LUS may be a potentially useful bedside tool for personalized mechanical ventilation in children.

items.title: Flow-to-Compliance Ratio as a Bedside Marker of Strain Rate in Pediatric Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome: Analysis of Observational Cohort Data From 2022
items.abstract: Objectives: To determine the relationship between the ratio of peak inspiratory flow and respiratory system compliance (Flow/C RS ) and strain rate in cases of pediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome (PARDS). Design: Secondary analysis of observational cohort data collected in 2022. Setting: Single-center tertiary PICU in Chile. Patients: Thirty-one mechanically ventilated patients with early PARDS, 15 years or younger. Interventions: None. Measurements and Main Results: All patients were supported with volume-controlled ventilation during measurement of pulmonary mechanics, including tidal volume (V t ), inspiratory time (Ti), inspiratory flow, and respiratory system compliance (C RS ). End-expiratory lung volume (EELV) was assessed using the nitrogen multiple-breath wash-in/washout method. Lung strain (V t /EELV), strain rate (lung strain/Ti, s –1 ), and the Flow/C RS ratio ([L·min –1 ]/[mL·cm H 2 O –1 ]) were calculated. The median (interquartile range [IQR]) strain rate was 0.56 s –1 (IQR, 0.40–0.73 s –1 ) and the median Flow/C RS ratio was 0.94 (IQR, 0.77–1.20). In the complete dataset, Flow/C RS ratio demonstrated a moderate positive correlation with measured strain rate (Spearman, ρ = 0.42; 95% CI, 0.08–0.67; p = 0.009). Linear regression confirmed a proportional relationship ( R 2 = 0.17; p = 0.022), but the Bland-Altman analysis showed systematic bias (mean difference, −0.43 ± 0.29 s −1 ) with 95% limits of agreement from −0.99 to 0.14 s −1 . Sensitivity analysis excluding three outliers (leaving data from 28 patients) demonstrated a stronger association (ρ = 0.63; p = 0.0018) and improved model fit ( R 2 = 0.41; p < 0.001), with the following equation: strain rate = 0.61·(Flow/C RS ) + 0.01. Conclusions: In PARDS, the Flow/C RS ratio is associated with measured strain rate but exhibits systematic bias, precluding direct interchangeability. Flow/C RS may serve as a pragmatic bedside marker reflecting deformation-velocity behavior. Prospective validation in larger and more heterogeneous cohorts is required.

items.title: Platelet Transfusion Practices in the PICUs: Multicenter, Observational Study, in Türkiye and Northern Cyprus, 2024
items.abstract: Objectives: We aimed to describe the use of platelet transfusions among critically ill children managed in Türkiye in late 2024. Secondarily, we sought to determine these practices in relation to the 2022 Transfusion and Anemia Expertise Initiative-Control/Avoidance of Bleeding (TAXI-CAB) recommendations for critically ill pediatric patients. Design: Prospective study (October–December 2024). Setting: 22 PICUs in Türkiye and Northern Cyprus. Patients: Patients of 1 month to 18 years who received at least one platelet transfusion in the PICU. Interventions: None Measurement and Main Results: Out of 2693 PICU admissions, 200 patients (7.4%) received 577 platelet transfusions. Of the transfusions, 383 of 577 transfusions (66.4%) were for prophylaxis, most frequently for isolated thrombocytopenia (194/383, 50.7%). Regarding the transfusion threshold for prophylaxis, in the 194 cases of isolated thrombocytopenia, the median (interquartile range [IQR]) pretransfusion platelet count was 24 (IQR, 16–38) × 10 9 /L, which differed from the TAXI-CAB consensus statement guidance of less than 10 × 10 9 /L. Platelet transfusion, as opposed to not, was associated with 20-fold greater odds of 28-day mortality ( p < 0.001), and among the 200 patients receiving platelets, multivariable analysis showed that lower pretransfusion platelet count, support with invasive mechanical ventilation, and hospital-acquired infections collectively accounted for 34% of the variance in model performance for classifying 28-day mortality. Conclusions: Our 2024 national, multicenter PICU study across Türkiye and Northern Cyprus shows that around two-thirds of transfusion episodes were for prophylaxis, and multivariable logistic regression modeling identified patient factors associated with greater odds of 28-day mortality. The median pretransfusion threshold for isolated thrombocytopenia was around 20 × 10 9 /L, which is double the less than 10 × 10 9 /L in the 2022 TAXI-CAB consensus statement. Given the heterogeneity of critically ill patients and practice environments, understanding the reasons behind these practices may help inform future research and consensus recommendations.

items.title: Online Abstract Translations
Pediatric Resident ICU Exposure Before and After the 2025 Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education Requirement Revision
Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation for Pediatric Lung Transplantation: An Extracorporeal Life Support Organization Registry Study, 2000–2022
items.abstract: OBJECTIVES: We aimed to identify factors associated with greater odds of survival, as well as odds of successful lung transplantation (LTx) in pediatric patients undergoing extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) as a bridge-to-LTx (BTT) or supported with ECMO after LTx. DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study using the Extracorporeal Life Support Organization (ELSO) registry. SETTING: International ECMO centers submitting data to the ELSO registry. PATIENTS: Pediatric patients younger than 19 years old who were supported with ECMO before or after LTx between 2000 and 2022. INTERVENTIONS: None. MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: We identified 194 pediatric patients who used ECMO as a bridge to LTx, and 63% survived to hospital discharge. We failed to identify an association between ECMO modality (i.e., venovenous vs. venoarterial) and odds of survival. Central venoarterial ECMO cannulation was associated with greater odds of receiving a LTx compared with not receiving a LTx (30/85 [35%] vs. 15/109 [14%]; odds ratio [OR], 3.42; 95% CI, 1.69–6.91). In the 109 patients who did not receive a LTx, ECMO cannulation delayed after hospital day 7 was associated with lower odds of survival (OR, 0.34; 95% CI, 0.15–0.75). ECMO post-LTx occurred in 95 patients, 62% received venoarterial or veno-venoarterial ECMO, and 48 of 95 (51%) survived to hospital discharge. In patients requiring ECMO post-LTx, cystic fibrosis was associated with lower odds of survival (OR, 0.31; 95% CI, 0.12–0.79) and pulmonary hypertension was associated with greater odds of survival (OR, 5.04; 95% CI, 1.68–15.1). CONCLUSIONS: Our data show that ECMO was used to support children as a BTT and for stabilization of postoperative LTx recipients. Early initiation of ECMO was associated with greater odds of survival in patients undergoing BTT who did not receive LTx. Further studies, including additional patients and focused LTx-related data, are needed to better characterize and delineate treatment options in this population.

items.title: Writing for Pediatric Critical Care Medicine: The Expanded Article from a Conference Abstract or Research Letter
The Short and Long View of Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation as a Bridge to Lung Transplant in Children
Fluid-Refractory Septic Shock in Children and Milrinone: Outcomes in a Two-Center, Retrospective Cohort in France, 2011–2021
items.abstract: Objectives: We have examined the associated outcomes of milrinone treatment for fluid-refractory septic shock. Design: Two-center, retrospective cohort from France. Setting: Two PICUs, both within tertiary care teaching hospitals. Patients: Children of 1 month to 18 years hospitalized between May 2011 and April 2021 with an episode of fluid-refractory septic shock treated with at least one vasoactive or inotropic agent. Intervention: None. Measurements and Main Results: We compared survival and PICU outcomes (organ support, length of stay) between patients who received milrinone and those who did not. We compared adverse events in the two groups, and we described the frequency and dosing of milrinone. We identified 290 patients with fluid-refractory septic shock with a median (interquartile range [IQR]) age of 48 months (IQR, 13–148 mo), of whom 46 of 290 (16%) received milrinone, with a median dose of 0.5 µg kg –1 min –1 (IQR, 0.5–0.8 µg kg –1 min –1 ). Overall mortality was 55 of 290 (19%). Use of milrinone was associated with a greater hazard (hazard ratio [HR], and 95% CI) of 30-day mortality (HR, 2.57 [95% CI, 1.15–5.75]; p = 0.021). Receiving milrinone, as opposed to not, was associated with greater volume of fluid boluses per case (16.8 [IQR, 0–50] vs. 10 [IQR, 0–29] mL kg –1 ; p = 0.04) and greater proportion undergoing mechanical ventilation (41/46 vs. 174/244; mean percentage difference, 17.8% [95% CI, 4.5–26.4%]; p = 0.011). Milrinone grouping, as opposed to not, was associated with greater proportion having cardiac arrests in the PICU (22/46 vs. 28/244; mean percentage difference, 36.3% [95% CI, 21.8–50.7%]; p < 0.001) and greater proportion with adverse events (17/46 vs. 24/244; mean percentage difference, 27.1% [95% CI, 13.9–41.9%]; p < 0.001). Conclusions: In our 2011–2021 cohort of children, milrinone was used in around one-in-six cases with fluid-refractory septic shock. Patients treated with milrinone had an associated greater hazard of mortality; and, proportionately, worse PICU outcomes, and greater adverse events.

items.title: Outcomes of Acute Kidney Injury in Pediatric Liver Transplant: Retrospective Cohort Study, 2013–2023
items.abstract: OBJECTIVES: We aimed to determine the prevalence of acute kidney injury (AKI) after pediatric liver transplantation (LT) and the associated preoperative and intraoperative factors. DESIGN: Single-center retrospective cohort study. SETTING: Sixteen-bed PICU in a university-affiliated tertiary care hospital. PATIENTS: PICU admissions with liver disease who underwent LT between January 2013 and December 2023. INTERVENTIONS: None. MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: We analyzed data from the first week, 90 days, and at 1-year follow-up. Patients with stage 2–3 AKI according to the Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) definitions or those receiving continuous renal replacement therapy for renal or mixed hepatorenal indications were defined as having severe AKI. There were 283 children with liver disease who underwent LT. Over the first postoperative week, 64.7% (183/283) developed AKI, including 30.4% (86/283) with severe AKI. Peak AKI occurred within the first 24 hours after surgery in 50.2% of LT patients (142/283). In a multivariable logistic regression model, pretransplant bilirubin levels, baseline renal function, and longer operative duration were associated with severe AKI. Severe AKI was associated with prolonged mechanical ventilation, longer PICU and hospital stays, and greater mortality in posttransplant patients. At 90-day follow-up, 1.9% of patients (5/260) had an estimated glomerular filtration rate less than 60 mL/min/1.73 m 2 . CONCLUSIONS: In our 2013–2023 retrospective cohort, a high proportion of children developed severe AKI within 1 week of LT. Preoperative factors such as bilirubin level, renal function, and intraoperative factors like procedure duration were associated with severe AKI. Severe AKI was associated with prolonged mechanical ventilation, length of PICU and hospital stay, and greater mortality. Further studies are needed to explore risk models.

items.title: Extubation Failure in Pediatric Critical Care: A Secondary Analysis of the 2018–2019 Sedation and Weaning in Children (SandWiCh) Trial
items.abstract: Objectives: Extubation failure is defined as requirement for emergency reintubation within 48 hours of extubation. We aimed to examine the rate of extubation failure in a large U.K. dataset, including an examination of the prevalence of postextubation stridor, and to determine which patient factors were associated with failure. Design: A post hoc, non–prespecified secondary analysis of the 2018–2019 Sedation and Weaning in Children clinical (SandWiCh) cluster-randomized trial (ISRCTN16998143) dataset. Setting: The SandWiCh trial recruited patients from 18 U.K. PICUs. Patients: All patients with data for a planned extubation were included and patients who had an unplanned extubation, or who died following their first extubation without being reintubated were excluded. Interventions: None. Measurements and Main Results: Data for 9215 patients in the trial with at least one planned extubation attempt were available for analysis. The factors associated with for extubation failure being examined included age, diagnostic group, severity of illness at PICU admission, and duration of mechanical ventilation before extubation. Extubation failure occurred following first planned extubation in 618 of 9215 (6.7%). On multivariable analysis, Pediatric Index of Mortality (PIM-3) score and duration of ventilation before extubation attempt were associated with greater odds of extubation failure. Of the entire cohort, 874 children (9.4%) had postextubation stridor, but this figure rose to 173 of 618 patients (28%) who had extubation failure. Conclusions: In the 2018–2019 SandWiCh dataset from the United Kingdom, failed extubation rate was comparable to other published cohorts. Greater odds of failed extubation was associated with increased PIM-3 score and duration of mechanical ventilation before attempted extubation. Stridor was present in a quarter of patients with extubation failure.

items.title: A Retrospective Study on the Evolution of Complex Chronic Conditions Over a Decade in a Large Swiss Tertiary PICU
items.abstract: Objectives: To examine, over a 10-year period, changes in the prevalence of complex chronic conditions (CCCs) and in the distribution of underlying chronic health categories within a large Swiss PICU, and to compare patient characteristics and PICU mortality between children with CCCs and those without. Design: Single-center retrospective observational study of two cohorts (2007 vs. 2017). Setting: Large academic tertiary referral PICU. Patients: Overall, 1867 children were included (0–16 years old): 981 admitted between January 1, 2007, and December 31, 2007, and 886 admitted between January 1, 2017, and December 31, 2017. Interventions: None. Measurements and Main Results: The prevalence of children with CCCs increased from 61% in 2007 to 70% in 2017. The most common conditions were cardiovascular (55% in 2007 vs. 52% in 2017), congenital/genetic defects (36% vs. 38%), and neurologic/neuromuscular (25% vs. 34%). The proportion of children with 3 or more chronic conditions rose from 16% to 25%. Children with CCCs had longer PICU stays than children without, with length of stay increasing significantly with the number of CCCs. Most children who died during the two study periods had a chronic condition (2007: 61%; 2017: 66%), with a significant increase in the proportion of deaths following intensive care treatment withdrawal (8% in 2007 vs. 48% in 2017). Conclusions: Over a decade, the proportion of children with CCCs needing PICU care has grown, with trends toward increasing prevalence in the clinically dominant categories of respiratory and hematology, immunodeficiency, and immunology, and the subcategories respiratory malformations , hereditary hemostasis anomalies, and home ventilation , and trends toward higher mortality rates following treatment withdrawal.

items.title: Neutrophil Extracellular Traps and Acute Kidney Injury in Pediatric Patients Receiving Cardiopulmonary Bypass
items.abstract: Objectives: To assess whether preoperative plasma neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) are associated with acute kidney injury (AKI), CICU length of stay, duration of hospital length of stay, chylothorax, thrombus, necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC), and vasoactive-ventilator-renal (VVR) score in pediatric patients undergoing cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB). Design: Single-center, prospective observational cohort study. Setting: Tertiary academic pediatric hospital. Patients: A total of 118 pediatric patients (birth to < 18 yr) undergoing CPB between June 2022 and June 2024. Intervention: None. Measurements and Main Results: Preoperative plasma NET levels were quantified by measuring myeloperoxidase-DNA complex levels via enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. AKI was defined using the Kidney Disease Improving Global Outcomes serum creatinine or urine output criteria. Creatinine was corrected for fluid balance on each postoperative day. AKI occurred in 31% of patients. Higher preoperative NET levels occurred more frequently among patients with postoperative AKI and lower Society of Thoracic Surgeons-European Association for Cardio-Thoracic Surgery score 1–3 patients. A 1 sd increase in NET levels was also significantly associated with a 2.61-fold increase in odds of NEC in unadjusted logistic regression (OR, 2.61 [95% CI, 1.29–5.31]). No associations were observed with CICU length of stay, hospital length of stay, chylothorax, thrombosis, or VVR score. Conclusions: Elevated preoperative plasma NET levels may serve as a biomarker of early postoperative complications, including AKI and NEC, in pediatric CPB. Further studies are needed to validate these findings and explore targeted therapies.

items.title: Propofol Infusion in a Mixed PICU: Prevalence of Propofol-Related Infusion Syndrome in a Retrospective Cohort, 2019–2022
items.abstract: Objectives: To describe usage and complications of propofol as a sedative agent in patients younger than 16 years old admitted to a PICU and to identify evidence of propofol-related infusion syndrome (PRIS). Design: Retrospective analysis of routinely collected data with comparison between patients receiving propofol for less than 48 hours compared with greater than or equal to 48 hours. Setting: Single-center mixed PICU in London, United Kingdom. Patients: All patients admitted to the PICU, from November 2019 to November 2022, younger than 16 years old, in whom an infusion of propofol was administered. Interventions: None. Measurements and Main Results: Propofol infusion was used in 1595 patients, 337 of whom had infusions of greater than or equal to 48 hours with a maximum dose of 5 mg/kg/hr and for a maximum duration of 45 days. The cohort age ranged from 1 day to 16 years and included patients with cardiac diagnoses. Patients were administered propofol for a median 76% of their ventilation time, and 26% of patients who were treated with propofol were also treated with noradrenaline. Physiologic variables, blood gases, laboratory values, and discharge summaries were reviewed, and no patients were clinically suspected of having PRIS. Variables previously reported in PRIS were analyzed across each patient’s admission, and we failed to identify an association between abnormal physiologic values and receipt of a propofol infusion or whether duration of propofol infusion was greater than or equal to 48 hours. Hence, the upper limit of the 95% CI for 0 of 1595 gives a PRIS prevalence in our population up to 0.19%. Conclusions: In our single-center, mixed PICU experience during 2019–2022, we have used propofol infusion in children younger than 16 years old. This practice included neonates and children with cardiac pathology. We failed to identify any episodes of clinically suspected PRIS in 1595 patients, including in the group treated for greater than or equal to 48 hours, which gives an upper limit for PRIS prevalence of ~0.19%.

items.title: Handheld Ultrasound Confirmation of Pediatric Endotracheal Intubation in a Resource-Limited Country
items.abstract: Objectives: Chest radiograph (CXR) and colorimetric capnography for confirmation of endotracheal tube (ETT) placement may be costly and inaccessible in resource-limited countries. Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) is considered a low-cost, fast alternative. We sought to study the accuracy of bedside POCUS as compared with CXR, using a pocket-sized handheld device, for confirmation of ETT placement in the neonatal ICU and PICU. Design: Prospective, observational study. Setting: PICU and neonatal ICU in a tertiary care center in Nepal between October 1, 2023, and April 30, 2024. Patients: Newborns to 14-year-old children. Interventions: POCUS using a handheld device at the bedside. Measurements and Main Results: POCUS was performed on 59 intubated children; 37 (62%) were males. Median age was 3 hours (interquartile range [IQR], 1–5 hr) in newborns ( n = 27) and 24 months (IQR, 12–84 mo) in children ( n = 32). POCUS demonstrated tracheal-confirmed ETT placement in 53 children (89.8%), suspected endobronchial in four, and indeterminate in two. CXR agreed with all 53 POCUS tracheal-confirmed intubations. There were three additional tracheal-confirmed cases on CXR and three endobronchial intubations. Sensitivity and specificity of POCUS for detection of ETT placement in the trachea, compared with CXR, were 94.6% (95% CI, 85.1–98.9%) and 100% (95% CI, 29.2–100%), respectively. Based on this, accuracy was calculated at 94.9%. Conclusions: Our study demonstrated good accuracy of POCUS using a handheld device to confirm ETT placement in neonates and children. It could be a reliable and effective method in a resource-limited country like Nepal.

items.title: Between the Dings
Postoperative Infection Mediates and Modifies the Effect of Risk Adjustment for Congenital Heart Surgery-1 Category on Hospital Stay in Pediatric Cardiac Surgery: A Retrospective Cohort Study
items.abstract: Objectives: To investigate whether postoperative infection mediates and/or modifies the effect of surgical complexity, as defined by the Risk Adjustment for Congenital Heart Surgery (RACHS-1) category, on hospital length of stay (LOS) in pediatric cardiac surgery patients. Design: Retrospective cohort study. Setting: Tertiary pediatric cardiac center at Xinhua Hospital, Shanghai Jiao Tong University. Patients: A total of 1244 children who underwent congenital heart surgery between October 2020 and July 2024. Interventions: None. Measurements and Main Results: Multivariable regression and causal-mediation analyses were performed to estimate the direct and infection-mediated effects of surgical complexity on LOS. Higher-RACHS-1 categories and postoperative infection were independently associated with prolonged LOS (all p < 0.001). In negative binomial mediation analysis, infection mediated 17.4% of the total RACHS–LOS association for RACHS-1 category greater than or equal to 5 vs. 1, corresponding to an infection-mediated increase of 3.87 expected LOS days (95% CI, 1.70–6.42). Infection also modified the association between surgical complexity and LOS, with infection-associated excess LOS increasing to +16.73 days in RACHS-1 category greater than or equal to 5 vs. 1. Mediation was strongest among infants less than or equal to 1 year (28% for RACHS-1 category 3 vs. 1). Conclusions: Postoperative infection both mediates and amplifies the impact of surgical complexity on hospital LOS, particularly in high-risk infants. Targeted infection-prevention strategies are essential to reduce postoperative morbidity in this population.

items.title: The Serum Proteomic Signatures Associated With Organ Dysfunction Based on Phoenix Criteria in Pediatric Sepsis: A Pilot Study
items.abstract: Objectives: To investigate the serum proteomic characteristics linked to sepsis-induced organ dysfunction, as defined by the Phoenix Pediatric Sepsis (PPS) criteria. Design and Setting: We conducted a serum proteomic study using data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry in pediatric patients with sepsis, admitted to the PICU at a tertiary, university-affiliated children’s hospital in China. Patients: Thirty-eight patients with sepsis and 19 healthy controls were included from November 2020 to June 2022. Interventions: None. Measurements and Main Results: A total of 403 differentially expressed proteins (DEPs) were identified in the serum of pediatric sepsis patients compared with healthy controls. Gene Set Enrichment Analysis revealed that DEPs across the four PPS-defined organ dysfunction were enriched in the antimicrobial humoral response, negative regulation of inflammation, plasminogen activation, and cytokine-mediated signaling pathways. Weighted Gene Co-Expression Network Analysis (WGCNA) showed that the MEgreen module was highly associated with the PPS score and was enriched in neutrophils. Further analysis identified seven hub proteins (tissue inhibitor of metalloproteinase-1 [TIMP1], cathepsin L peptidase 1, β-1,4-galactosyltransferase 1, carbonic anhydrase 3, interleukin 1 receptor like 1, olfactomedin 4, and cathepsin G [CATG]) as candidate serum proteomic markers of organ dysfunction risk. We used the expression of these seven hub proteins in a least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression model to predict organ system dysfunction. It achieved an area under the curve of 0.857 for the coagulation system and 0.769 for the cardiovascular system. All seven hub proteins were significantly correlated with lactic acid and the international normalized ratio (all p < 0.05); CATG was positively correlated with mean arterial pressure ( p = 0.005), TIMP1 displayed a positive correlation with d- dimer ( p = 0.021) and a negative correlation with platelet ( p = 0.005). Conclusions: We identified seven hub proteins that constitute a novel proteomic signature for predicting sepsis-associated organ dysfunction based on the Phoenix criteria. It is particularly relevant to the coagulation and cardiovascular systems.

items.title: The Quiet Struggle: Parental Perspectives on Sibling Well-Being During PICU Admission
items.abstract: Objective: To identify the impact of PICU admission on parental perceptions of the well-being of patients’ child-aged siblings and understand how families use hospital resources to support siblings. Design: Qualitative study using semi-structured interviews of parents of PICU patients with siblings to characterize sibling socioemotional changes during PICU admission and how the sibling interacted with hospital resources. Interviews were transcribed and thematically analyzed. Setting: Quaternary-care PICU at a level 1 trauma center in St. Louis, MO. Subjects: Parents of a child admitted to the PICU with at least one additional child living at home between the ages of 5 and 19 years. Interventions: None. Measurements and Main Results: Fourteen biological parents and one legal guardian representing 15 households and 17 siblings of PICU patients were interviewed. Four themes were identified describing parental perspective on sibling psychosocial well-being: 1) routine is important, 2) parents consider multiple factors when evaluating the impact of sibling visits on child well-being, 3) hospitalizations impacts sibling well-being in many ways, and 4) few siblings’ physical well-being changed following hospitalization. Two themes were identified regarding parental perspective of hospital resources: 5) parents believed that hospital support was designed to cultivate a sense of normalcy, and 6) the provision and utilization of child life services was not uniform. Conclusions: It is critical to prioritize the emotional and social well-being of siblings of critically ill and injured children through the maintenance of routine, balancing the needs of both patient and sibling when considering visitation policies, and providing hospital supports tailored to sibling’s age and cognitive level.

items.title: Who Counts in Pediatric Sepsis? Lessons From Ibero-Latin America
Sepsis Point Prevalence Across Ibero-Latin America PICUs: The 2024 Sepsis Prevalence Assessment Database in Pediatrics (SPREAD PED IBERO-LATAM)
items.abstract: Objectives: To determine the prevalence and outcome of sepsis in PICUs across Ibero-Latin America; to identify patient- and institution-level factors associated with mortality; and to explore the prognostic performance of pediatric sepsis definitions. Design: Multinational, multicenter, prospective point prevalence study with follow-up to hospital discharge. Setting: One hundred sixty-eight PICUs in 21 countries across Latin America, Spain, and Portugal. Patients: Children of 28 days to 18 years with a clinical diagnosis of sepsis or septic shock admitted to participating PICUs between September 9 and September 13, 2024. Interventions: None Measurements and Main Results: Among 1318 screened PICU patients, 340 met criteria for clinical sepsis, yielding a point prevalence of 25.8% (95% CI, 23.5–28.2%). Complete outcome data were available for 324 patients. PICU mortality was 42 of 324 (13.0% [95% CI, 9.5–17.1%), and total in-hospital mortality was 49 of 324 (15.1% [95% CI, 11.4–19.4%]). Cardiovascular and respiratory dysfunction were most frequent, whereas multivariable logistic regression identified greater odds of PICU mortality associated with renal dysfunction (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 3.2 [95% CI, 1.5–7.5]) and immunologic dysfunction (aOR, 12.7 [95% CI, 4.6–37.5]).In multivariable analysis, abnormal nutritional status, lack of vaccination, renal dysfunction, and admission to PICUs with intermediate or low resource availability were associated with greater odds of PICU mortality. In exploratory analyses, the Phoenix sepsis criteria identified 95.2% of PICU deaths, but the positive predictive value of the score for mortality was no different from the 2005 International Pediatric Sepsis Consensus Conference criteria. Conclusions: In 2024, in Ibero-Latin American PICUs, sepsis affected approximately one in four admissions, and the diagnosis was associated with mortality. Both patient vulnerability and institutional resource availability were associated with greater odds of mortality, underscoring the potential influence of health system capacity on pediatric sepsis outcomes in the region.

items.title: Electronic Children’s Hospital Early Warning Score: Development and Validation of a Novel Machine Learning Algorithm Predicting Critical Deterioration Events in a Retrospective, Single-Center Cohort
items.abstract: Objective: To develop and validate a novel, machine learning prediction model for critical deterioration events. Design: Retrospective cohort study. Setting: Single quaternary care freestanding pediatric hospital. Patients: All patients up to 21 years old admitted to acute care wards (excluding cardiac and psychiatry units) between January 2012 and June 2023. Interventions: None. Measurements and Main Results: The primary outcome was a critical deterioration, defined as utilization of advanced respiratory support or continuous IV medication infusions not administered on acute care units. Secondary outcome was ICU transfer. Each outcome was evaluated between 6 and 30 hours after each prediction score. Among 179,074 unique hospitalizations with 2,803,017 windows of scoring data, 10,656 (0.4%) had a subsequent critical deterioration event. Compared with the legacy Children’s Hospital Early Warning Score (CHEWS), the model, which we call electronic CHEWS (eCHEWS), had a higher area under the precision-recall curve (0.157; 95% CI [0.150–0.164]) vs. 0.017; 95% CI [0.013–0.027]). At sensitivity approximately 44%, CHEWS had positive predictive value (PPV) 1.8% (number needed to alert [NNA] 55), whereas eCHEWS had PPV 11.4% (NNA 9). Conclusions: eCHEWS outperforms traditional early warning scores for predicting critical deterioration among acute care inpatients and can detect critical deterioration at least 6 hours before occurrence. If prospectively validated, eCHEWS could serve as an early warning trigger integrated into the electronic health record to support proactive rounding, escalation decisions, and timely transfer to ICUs.

items.title: Associations between air pollution and pediatric pneumonia incidence in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia: age and sex susceptibility
items.abstract: Background: Childhood pneumonia is a major public health issue in Mongolia and other low- and middle-income countries (LMIC). Identifying modifiable environmental risk factors and vulnerable populations is essential for developing effective prevention strategies. We investigated whether short-term exposure to ambient air pollutants was associated with daily outpatient visits for pneumonia among children under 5 years of age in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia, and assessed whether age and sex modified these associations. Methods: )in Ulaanbaatar. Associations between ambient air pollutants and daily pneumonia outpatient visits were estimated using generalized additive models (GAMs) with a quasi-Poisson distribution. The models estimated relative risks (RRs) per interquartile range (IQR) increase in pollutant concentrations while adjusting for long-term trends, seasonality, temperature, humidity, day of the week (DOW), holidays, and raw coal ban policy. We examined pollutant effects across different lag periods, assessed effect modification by age and sex, and evaluated the robustness of associations using multi-pollutant models. Results: were attenuated. Conclusions: associations in multi-pollutant models suggests that these pollutants may represent important independent contributors to childhood pneumonia risk. Boys and infants appeared to be more susceptible, highlighting vulnerable populations that may benefit from targeted air pollution mitigation strategies.

items.title: Hemodynamic and biomechanical impact of proximal aortic surgery on the cardiovascular system: a systematic review and meta-analysis
items.abstract: Background: The consequences of proximal aortic (PA) replacement with a stiff vascular prosthesis remain insufficiently understood. This systematic review and meta-analysis aims to consolidate evidence regarding the hemodynamic and biomechanical effects of PA surgery on the cardiovascular system. Methods: Four databases were searched on April 16th, 2025. Clinical and experimental studies reporting hemodynamic or biomechanical outcomes after PA compliance alterations were included. Exclusion criteria comprised non-original work, computational models, acute procedures, interventions beyond the PA, and PA constriction surgeries. Primary outcomes reflected cardiac functioning, hemodynamics, and aortic biomechanics. Results: 1.11 Pa, P=0.04). Meta-analysis (four studies) found increased distensibility [standardized mean change score (SMCC) 0.50, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.24-0.76, k=3] and circumferential strain (SMCC 0.55, 95% CI: 0.00-1.10, k=3) of the descending aorta. Ejection fraction (SMCC 0.08, 95% CI: -0.29-0.45, k=3) and pulse pressure (SMCC 0.47, 95% CI: -0.36-1.31, k=3) remained unchanged. Certainty of evidence was very low, and risk of bias was moderate. Conclusions: PA stiffening due to a vascular prosthesis appears to have limited systemic hemodynamic effects, likely due to compensatory mechanisms (e.g. increased left ventricular mass and distal aortic adaptation). Local distensibility, WSS and flow dynamics are adversely affected.
items.limitations: This finding may be explained by limitations of these studies. The study by Sieren et al., compared intervention data to a small cohort of healthy volunteers, instead of before- and after measurement. In the study of Palumbo et al., multiple testing was done on outcomes within the same domain risking type I statistical error with a barely statistical significant P value of 0.04 for the SV. Upstream compensatory mechanisms (i.e., cardiac adaptation) may explain why no consistent effects on cardiac indices are observed. One cohort observed an increase of LVMI after PA surgery (47 patients after 9–12 months), suggesting chronic afterload and adverse remodeling, which could be due to a stiff PA conduit. Due to the small number of studies, heterogeneity (e.g., pre- and postoperative comparison vs. healthy controls, short-term experimental data vs. longer-term clinical data), small sample size per study, and individual study limitations, interpretation of results is difficult and conclusions on impact of PA surgery on the cardiovascular system could only be drawn with caution. However, this review serves as a strong exploratory basis, providing mechanistic insights from both clinical and experimental literature. While more studies exist on the impact of aortic stiffening, only 13 studies were included using strict inclusion and exclusion criteria (e.g., related to valve pathology, connective tissue disease, and only focussing on the PA). However, these criteria are believed to be a distinct strength of the current study, as the impact of relevant confounders is reduced. Some studies were reported by overlapping research groups, which may also have overlapping patient cohorts.

items.title: Prognostic value of the apelin-12-to-white blood cell ratio for long-term major adverse cardiovascular events in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention: a retrospective cohort study
items.abstract: Background: Despite advances in primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), patients remain at risk for long-term major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs).
