The apelin-12/white blood cell ratio (AWR), a ratio has never been studied before, may reflect the balance between cardioprotective apelin signaling and systemic inflammation. We examined the prognostic value of admission AWR for long-term MACEs in STEMI patients after primary PCI. Methods: This secondary analysis included 464 consecutive STEMI patients who underwent primary PCI at The First People's Hospital of Taizhou (Zhejiang, China) between January 2010 and October 2014. Blood samples were collected on admission, immediately before primary PCI, for apelin-12 measurement. Patients were followed for 30 months. MACE was defined as the composite of cardiac death, cardiogenic shock, congestive heart failure, recurrent target-vessel myocardial infarction, or clinically driven target-lesion revascularization. AWR was analyzed as a continuous variable and by pre-specified tertiles (cut-points 6.48 and 10.49). Cox proportional-hazards (PH) regression with a directed acyclic graph (DAG)-derived minimal adjustment set (age, sex, diabetes mellitus, hypertension, serum creatinine, and Killip class) was used to estimate associations. Predictive performance was evaluated using time-dependent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), C-index, bootstrap optimism correction, integrated discrimination improvement (IDI), and net reclassification improvement (NRI). Results: lowest tertile: HR 0.40, 95% CI: 0.24-0.65, P<0.001]. The protective association strengthened after the first month. Adding AWR to the Global Registry of Acute Coronary Events (GRACE) 2.0 and Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction (TIMI) scores significantly improved reclassification (IDI and NRI both P<0.01). Conclusions: A lower admission AWR is associated with an increased risk of long-term MACEs in STEMI patients undergoing primary PCI, supporting its potential as a prognostic biomarker.

items.title: Lean dual-portal versus conventional multi-portal robotic-assisted thoracic surgery for anatomical lung resection: a retrospective comparative cohort study of a sustainable approach harmonizing clinical efficiency, environmental protection, and next-generation education
items.abstract: Background: Conventional robotic-assisted thoracic surgery (RATS) is increasingly scrutinized for its high procedural costs, excessive medical plastic waste, and the passive role it often assigns to surgical trainees. To address these systemic inefficiencies, we introduced the 'lean' dual-portal RATS (DRATS) strategy. This study evaluates the clinical feasibility and multi-dimensional benefits of this approach, which prioritizes resource stewardship and educational autonomy. Methods: insufflation and specialized cannula seals, and the proactive 'Bedside Surgeon' model. Allocation to the DRATS group was determined by the daily availability of a designated fixed surgical team, minimizing selection bias. Primary outcomes included operative efficiency and safety, with complications recorded via the Clavien-Dindo classification. Patients were followed through outpatient clinic visits to monitor for late complications and confirm the absence of readmissions. Results: 6 (4-66) days, P<0.001]. No patients in either group required readmission after discharge. The "lean" strategy achieved a cost reduction of approximately 118,000 JPY ($762 USD) per case by eliminating specialized seals and utilizing resident-operated manual endoscopic stapling executed synchronously during active console time. Conclusions: This small, single-center study suggests that the 'lean' DRATS approach is feasible for anatomical lung resection in a selected group of patients. While the strategy significantly reduced procedural costs and shortened hospital stay without compromising immediate safety, its equivalence to conventional robotic surgery requires further validation through larger prospective trials.

items.title: First-line systemic treatment patterns and outcomes in lung cancer patients with malignant pleural effusion: a retrospective multicenter study
items.abstract: Background: Malignant pleural effusion (MPE) is a frequent complication of advanced lung cancer with poor prognosis. The optimal first-line systemic treatment for these patients remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate first-line systemic treatment patterns and outcomes in lung cancer patients with MPE. Methods: This multicenter retrospective study across 27 centers in China evaluated the efficacy and safety of first-line systemic therapy in lung cancer patients with MPE from 2013 to 2024. The primary endpoints were progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS). Results: 21.4 months; P=0.04) and was an independent predictor of favorable OS [HR, 0.59; 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.38-0.90; P=0.02], despite no significant PFS improvement (HR, 0.72; 95% CI: 0.51-1.01; P=0.055), with a manageable safety profile [grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs): 14.8%]. Conclusions: First-line systemic therapy was associated with improved survival in lung cancer patients with MPE, though outcomes differed according to histologic and molecular subtypes. The addition of bevacizumab to chemotherapy was independently associated with longer OS among patients with driver gene-negative NSCLC with MPE.

items.title: Development and validation of an interpretable clinical-radiomics model for predicting 3-year postoperative recurrence in clinical stage I lung adenocarcinoma: a multicentre study
items.abstract: Background: Although surgical resection is the standard curative treatment for clinical stage I lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), a clinically meaningful proportion of patients still experience postoperative recurrence. Conventional clinical and computed tomography (CT) imaging features have limited ability to provide individualized preoperative risk stratification. This study aimed to develop and externally validate an interpretable CT-based clinical-radiomics model for predicting recurrence within 3 years after surgery in patients with clinical stage I LUAD. Methods: This multicentre retrospective prediction model development and validation study included 333 patients with pathologically confirmed clinical stage I LUAD who underwent surgical resection between January 2020 and December 2021. Patients from Center 1 (The Affiliated Hospital of Qingdao University) (n=199) constituted the training cohort, and those from Center 2 (The Fourth Affiliated Hospital of Zhejiang University School of Medicine) (n=134) served as the validation cohort. The outcome was recurrence within 3 years after surgery (determined by imaging findings, clinical follow-up records, and pathological confirmation when available). Patients without recurrence were required to have at least 3 years of follow-up. Radiomics features were extracted from preoperative CT images and selected using analysis of variance (ANOVA) and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, while clinical predictors were identified using univariable and multivariable logistic regression. Radiomics, clinical, and combined models were evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve, calibration, and decision curve analysis (DCA). SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis was used to interpret the optimal model. Results: Overall, 63 of 333 patients (18.9%) experienced recurrence within 3 years after surgery. In the validation cohort, the clinical, radiomics, and combined models achieved the areas under the curve (AUCs) of 0.674 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.550-0.799], 0.781 (95% CI: 0.668-0.893), and 0.850 (95% CI: 0.752-0.948), respectively, with corresponding sensitivities/specificities of 0.880/0.385, 0.920/0.532, and 0.840/0.798. The combined model showed significantly better discrimination than the clinical model (DeLong P=0.02). The combined model showed acceptable calibration in the validation cohort, with the calibration intercept, calibration slope, and Brier score were -0.157, 0.763, and 0.114, respectively. DCA suggested a potential net benefit of the combined model across a range of threshold probabilities in both cohorts, while SHAP analysis provided individualized interpretation of model predictions. Conclusions: The combined clinical-radiomics model based on preoperative CT and clinical characteristics showed potential for stratifying the risk of recurrence within 3 years after surgery in patients with clinical stage I LUAD. Further validation in larger, prospective cohorts is warranted before clinical implementation.

items.title: Current state of management of post-pneumonectomy empyema: a narrative review
items.abstract: Background and Objective: Pneumonectomy operations have been performed for around 100 years with post-pneumonectomy empyema (PPE) as a feared complication. Unlike an isolated empyema, these cases are most often associated with a bronchopleural fistula (BPF) that causes ongoing contamination of the surgical space and contralateral lung with subsequent respiratory failure and severe sepsis. The objective of this narrative review is to outline the wide range of treatment options that range from conservative management to more extensive surgical procedures, while also proposing a treatment algorithm. Methods: Two reviewers (A.P.K. and A.A.) queried PubMed, MEDLINE, and the Cochrane Library since inception for meta-analyses, retrospective, cohort studies, case series, and case reports. Disagreements between the two reviewers were resolved through discussion and consensus. Exclusion criteria included non-English articles. Key Content and Findings: First reports of BPF were managed with open window thoracostomy (OWT), which eventually evolved into the two-stage "Modified Clagett Procedure". Alternative surgical approaches described included trans-sternal and contralateral intra-thoracic approach for left-sided fistulas with short stumps to avoid repair in an infected field. More recently, endoscopic approaches have been described with variable success rates but are worth exploring for small fistulas to avoid the morbid surgical approach and poor surgical candidates as a salvage technique. Conclusions: Although there is limited data given the scarcity of this disease, current evidence shows that PPE with associated BPF located in a small (<6-8 mm) healthy stump can be successfully managed endoscopically, whereas surgical approach may be the better strategy for larger fistulas. Further evaluation of specific endoscopic techniques is necessary to further refine the treatment algorithm.

items.title: Revealing the complex association between environmental toxicants and preserved ratio impaired spirometry: an exploratory study
items.abstract: Background: Preserved ratio impaired spirometry (PRISm), as a novel heterogeneous pulmonary function pattern, is associated with the early stage of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). However, whether human exposure to environmental toxicants is associated with PRISm has not been comprehensively studied, particularly with respect to combined exposure to multiple toxicants. The objective of the study was to investigate the effects of single and combined environmental toxicants on PRISm. Methods: We analyzed data from 1,754 adult participants in an American population study. We employed multivariable logistic regression, weighted quantile sum (WQS) regression, quantile g-computation (Qgcomp), Bayesian kernel machine regression (BKMR), and machine learning models to examine associations between 21 environmental toxicants and PRISm. We additionally conducted subgroup analyses stratified by smoking status. We also explored the potential mediating roles of the lipid indicator non-high-density lipoprotein to high-density lipoprotein ratio (NHHR) and lipid-related inflammatory markers. Results: In the single-exposure model, eight environmental toxicants were found to be positively associated with PRISm, with lead (Pb) exhibiting the strongest association estimate. The results of WQS regression, Qgcomp, and BKMR consistently indicated that mixtures of environmental toxicants showed a stable positive association with PRISm in both the overall population and smokers. Pb and cadmium (Cd) were identified as the most contributory environmental toxicants, respectively. The mediation analysis indicated that NHHR statistically accounted for 12.5% of this relationship, while the mediation proportion of lipid-related inflammatory markers ranged from 8.51% to 11.1%. Gradient boosting decision tree (GBDT) emerged as the top-performing machine-learning model, with the highest area under the curve (AUC) of 0.865. Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) interpretability analysis further revealed that Pb was the most influential environmental toxicant. Conclusions: Our findings provide exploratory evidence of individual and combined associations between environmental toxicant exposure and PRISm in the selected National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) analytic sample.

items.title: Prognostic value of changes in skeletal muscle index on serial computed tomography scans for overall survival in patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer: a single-center retrospective study
items.abstract: Background: Survival rates in advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) vary substantially, and changes in host body composition may affect prognosis. Serial computed tomography (CT) can repeatedly quantify skeletal muscle index (SMI) at the L3 level, but its dynamic predictive value and clinically usable thresholds have not been systematically validated. This study systematically evaluates the predictive value of longitudinal SMI changes based on serial CT for overall survival (OS), validate early treatment thresholds, and test its incremental effect over clinical models and Response Evaluation Criteria In Solid Tumors (RECIST). Methods: A single-center retrospective cohort was established, including 451 patients with stage IIIB-IV NSCLC who received systemic therapy from 2018 to 2023. L3 SMI was extracted at baseline and follow-up CT; segmentation consistency intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) ≥0.97. ΔSMI% was modeled as a time-dependent exposure (per 5% decrease) in multivariable Cox, and a 12-week landmark analysis was used to evaluate early ΔSMI% ≤-5%. Baseline missing data were handled with MICE (m=20). Combined with RECIST, we compared the C-index, Uno time-dependent area under the curve (AUC), and 12-month net reclassification improvement (NRI), and conducted decision curve analysis and 1,000 bootstrap calibration. Results: HR =0.87, P=0.006); the association between ΔSMI% and death risk was approximately linear (overall P=0.001). At the 12-week landmark analysis, early ΔSMI% ≤-5% was associated with worse survival (log-rank P=0.003), with an adjusted HR =1.68 (P=0.001). The correlation between early ΔSMI% and RECIST was weak (r=-0.18, P=0.001). On top of clinical covariates, adding baseline SMI and time-dependent ΔSMI% increased the corrected C-index from 0.67 to 0.71; 12-month NRI =0.19; AUC at 6/12 months was 0.71/0.70. Decision curves showed higher net benefit than treat all/none within threshold ranges 0.23-0.47 and 0.34-0.58; calibration was good. Conclusions: SMI dynamic metrics derived from serial CT constitute an independent and actionable prognostic signal in advanced NSCLC, enable early identification of high-risk patients within routine follow-up windows, and provide incremental gains in discrimination and net benefit over clinical models.

items.title: Explainable machine-learning prediction of prolonged postoperative hospitalization after esophagectomy using clinical and CT-derived body-composition features
items.abstract: Background: Prolonged postoperative hospitalization after esophagectomy reflects delayed recovery, postoperative morbidity, nutritional difficulty, discharge readiness, and healthcare resource utilization. Computed tomography (CT)-derived body-composition features may provide additional information about physiologic reserve, but their incremental value for predicting prolonged length of stay (LOS) after esophagectomy remains uncertain. This study aimed to develop and internally validate machine-learning models for predicting prolonged postoperative hospitalization after esophagectomy using routine clinical variables and CT-derived body-composition features. Methods: This retrospective prediction-model development and internal-validation study included 299 patients who underwent esophagectomy between December 2020 and June 2025. The primary outcome was prolonged postoperative LOS, defined as LOS >15 days. Three prespecified feature sets were evaluated: Clinical-only, CT-only, and Clinical + CT. CT-derived variables included average thoracic muscle, average thoracic fat, average lumbar muscle, and average lumbar fat. Logistic regression, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) logistic regression, random forest, and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) models were developed. Internal validation was performed using 1,000 bootstrap resampling iterations with out-of-bag evaluation. Model performance was assessed using discrimination, calibration, decision-curve analysis, and supplemental performance metrics. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis was performed using the XGBoost Clinical + CT model to explain individual-level predictions. Results: Among 299 patients, 70 patients experienced prolonged postoperative LOS. The Clinical + CT LASSO model achieved the highest internally validated discrimination among the LASSO models, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.6288, accuracy of 0.6121, sensitivity of 0.5207, specificity of 0.6408, and Brier score of 0.2422. The Clinical-only LASSO model showed similar performance, with an AUC of 0.6194, whereas the CT-only LASSO model showed limited discrimination, with an AUC of 0.5439. The incremental improvement in AUC after adding CT-derived features to clinical variables was small and statistically non-significant [AUC difference +0.0094; 95% confidence interval (CI): -0.1393 to 0.1403; P=0.44]. SHAP analysis identified average lumbar fat, white blood cell count, age, albumin, and average thoracic muscle as the most influential features in the XGBoost Clinical + CT model. Conclusions: Machine-learning models using routine clinical variables and CT-derived body-composition features demonstrated modest ability to predict prolonged postoperative hospitalization after esophagectomy. CT-derived features alone showed limited discrimination and provided only limited incremental value beyond clinical variables in the primary LASSO comparison. However, SHAP analysis of the tree-based model suggested that selected CT-derived features may contribute to nonlinear, individual-level risk estimation. Given the moderate discrimination and relatively high negative predictive value observed, these models should be considered supportive risk-stratification tools rather than replacements for clinical judgment. Their potential role may be in identifying patients less likely to experience prolonged hospitalization and supporting perioperative planning, although external validation and prospective evaluation are required before clinical implementation.
items.limitations: Several limitations should also be acknowledged. First, this was a single-center retrospective study, and only internal validation was performed. External validation in independent multicenter cohorts is required before clinical implementation. In addition, patients requiring perioperative ICU admission or experiencing early postoperative mortality were excluded because these patients represent a distinct subgroup with severe postoperative deterioration, in whom hospitalization duration is primarily driven by critical illness rather than delayed recovery within the conventional postoperative pathway. Therefore, the current model should be interpreted as a tool for risk stratification among patients undergoing expected postoperative recovery rather than the entire spectrum of postoperative trajectories.

items.title: Association of triglyceride-glucose and triglyceride-glucose body mass indexes with risk and prognosis of lung cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis
items.abstract: Background: The relationship of triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index and triglyceride-glucose body mass index (TyG-BMI) with the risk of lung cancer and survival of patients with lung cancer remains unclear. This meta-analysis aimed to clarify the association of TyG index and TyG-BMI with the risk of lung cancer and survival of lung cancer patients. Methods: Several databases were searched up to July 2, 2026. Odds ratios (ORs) and hazard ratios (HRs) were combined to assess the association of TyG index and TyG-BMI with risk and prognosis of lung cancer, respectively. Subgroup analyses based on study design, tumor type, treatment and combination of diabetes mellitus (DM) were performed. Results: Thirteen studies were included. Pooled analyses demonstrated that higher TyG index [OR =2.42, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.54-3.81, P<0.001] and TyG-BMI (OR =1.01, 95% CI: 1.01-1.02, P<0.001) were significantly related to increased risk of lung cancer. Subgroup analyses based on the study design and tumor type manifested similar results. However, subgroup analysis based on the combination of DM indicated that the significant association of TyG index and TyG-BMI with lung cancer risk was only observed among the population without DM. Besides, a higher TyG index was associated with poorer overall survival (OS) (HR =2.24, 95% CI: 1.49-3.37, P<0.001) and progression-free survival (PFS) (HR =3.09, 95% CI: 1.78-5.37, P<0.001). TyG-BMI was also related to OS (HR =1.86, 95% CI: 1.36-2.56, P<0.001) and PFS (HR =2.34, 95% CI: 1.20-4.56, P=0.01). Subgroup analyses stratified by treatment and tumor type indicated consistent findings, but association of TyG-BMI with OS was only observed in non-diabetic patients. Conclusions: Elevated TyG index and TyG-BMI are significantly associated with increased risk of lung cancer and poorer survival outcomes, particularly among non-diabetic individuals.

items.title: Fully implantable subcutaneous pleural port for patient-centered management of recurrent non-malignant pleural effusions
items.abstract: Background: Non-malignant pleural effusions (NMPEs) significantly impact patients' quality of life and represent a growing healthcare burden. We describe an alternative, patient-centered approach for managing recurrent NMPEs: the subcutaneous pleural port catheter (SPPC) technique. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients with NMPEs managed with SPPC between December 2023 and February 2026. Demographic details, clinical presentation, fluid volume management, and patient-tolerability were recorded. The procedure involved placement of a pleural catheter with subcutaneous tunneling, followed by routine outpatient drainage. Results: . Conclusions: SPPC appears to be a safe and feasible outpatient option for selected patients requiring chronic pleural drainage, demonstrating favorable early procedural outcomes and patient tolerability in this study. It may be particularly suitable for patients with low protein, transudative pleural effusions who require intermittent drainage every 2-8 weeks and wish to avoid an external device, irrespective of anticoagulation status. Larger randomized controlled trials are needed to assess long-term efficacy, safety, and patient reported quality of life outcomes, and to define its role in the management of nonmalignant pleural effusions.

items.title: Burden, trends and predictions of esophageal cancer in the top five GDP countries: a systematic analysis based on the Global Burden of Disease 2023 study
items.abstract: Background: Esophageal cancer remains a major global health burden, but comparative analyses across leading economies are limited. This study aimed to comprehensively evaluate and compare the esophageal cancer burden from 1990 to 2023 and project trends to 2050 in the top five gross domestic product (GDP) countries-China, Germany, India, Japan, and the United States-using data from the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2023 study. Methods: We extracted age-, sex-, and risk factor-specific data on esophageal cancer incidence, mortality, and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) for the five countries from the GBD 2023 database. Age-standardized rates (ASRs) were calculated, and temporal trends were assessed using Joinpoint regression. Age-period-cohort (APC) modeling was employed to disentangle the independent effects of age, period, and cohort. Decomposition analysis quantified the contributions of population aging, population growth, and epidemiological changes. Bayesian age-period-cohort (BAPC) models were applied to project disease burden through 2050. Results: China had the highest absolute burden but achieved the steepest declines. India's age-standardized incidence rates (ASIRs) more than doubled. Japan, Germany, and the USA maintained lower, stable rates. APC analysis showed an "inverted-U" age peak in China versus older peaks elsewhere. Decomposition identified epidemiological changes as the main alleviating factor in China, whereas aging and unfavorable trends drove India's rise. Smoking dominated in four countries; India was co-driven by chewing tobacco and low vegetable intake. BAPC projections foresee continued declines in China, Germany, and Japan, a surge in India, and a rebound in the USA. Conclusions: The esophageal cancer burden exhibits marked heterogeneity across the top five GDP countries, driven by distinct demographic transitions, risk factor profiles, and public health responses. These findings emphasize the urgent need for tailored, context-specific cancer control strategies, including strengthened tobacco and alcohol regulation, dietary improvements, and expanded screening in high-risk populations.
items.limitations: Our study has several limitations. First, as with all analyses based on the GBD study, our findings depend on the quality and completeness of the original data sources. However, epidemiological surveys in many middle and low income countries are incomplete, which may introduce bias and reduce the accuracy of burden estimates. Second, the GBD database only includes risk factors such as low vegetable intake, smoking, alcohol use, and chewing tobacco; other potential factors, such as nitrosamine intake, consumption of overheated beverages, and genetic mutations, were not incorporated in the current analysis. Third, the BAPC projections of disease burden are based on extrapolations of historical trends, but future breakthroughs in prevention, screening technologies, or treatment, as well as unforeseeable public health emergencies or policy shifts, may affect the accuracy of the predictions.

items.title: MYL9 silencing inhibits proliferation and migration of lung adenocarcinoma cells: a potential therapeutic target
items.abstract: Background: Myosin light chain 9 (MYL9), a regulatory light chain of myosin II, plays a crucial role in cytoskeletal dynamics and has been associated with tumor progression in multiple malignancies. However, its role in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains poorly characterized. Despite recent advances in treatment, the prognosis of LUAD patients remains poor, underscoring the need for novel therapeutic targets.Methods: Here, we systematically assessed MYL9 expression and its clinical relevance in LUAD by integrating transcriptomic data from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and protein-level validation from the Human Protein Atlas (HPA) via immunohistochemistry. Functional investigations in H1299 cells indicated that silencing MYL9 significantly impeded cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, as corroborated by colony formation and Transwell assays. In vivo xenograft models further verified that MYL9 knockdown inhibited tumor growth and triggered apoptosis. Bioinformatic analyses, including the ESTIMATE algorithm, single-sample gene set enrichment analysis (ssGSEA), and drug sensitivity profiling, were also performed.Results: In addition to its oncogenic impacts, bioinformatic analyses demonstrated that elevated MYL9 expression is correlated with distinct immune infiltration patterns and diminished chemosensitivity, possibly through the modulation of the tumor microenvironment. These findings suggest that MYL9 may link cytoskeletal regulation with tumor progression, immune remodeling, and treatment response in LUAD.Conclusions: Collectively, these findings recognize MYL9 as a novel prognostic biomarker and therapeutic target in LUAD, providing insights into its multifaceted role in tumor biology and treatment response. Further studies are warranted to validate these findings in larger clinical cohorts and to elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms.

items.title: Clinical and prognostic characteristics of concurrent small cell lung cancer in patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis: a retrospective study
items.abstract: Background: Lung cancer (LC) is a comorbidity that seriously affects the prognosis of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) patients. Small cell LC (SCLC) accounts for the highest proportion of hospitalized LC patients with concurrent IPF at Peking Union Medical College Hospital (PUMCH). To enable effective and standardized management of patients with IPF and SCLC, this study aims to summarize the clinical and prognostic characteristics of IPF-SCLC patients to improve their prognosis. Methods: We retrospectively enrolled patients with IPF (diagnosed by 2022 ATS/ERS/JRS/ALAT criteria)-SCLC (pathologically confirmed) admitted to PUMCH from January 2014 to December 2023. Clinical manifestation, chest computed tomography (CT) imaging, laboratory test, treatment and outcome data of patients with IPF-SCLC were collected and reviewed in detail with final follow-up on June 30, 2024. Results: Forty patients with IPF-SCLC were included with the average age of 68.2±6.3 years (range, 54 to 82 years). And there were 37 (92.5%) males. Median follow-up time was 12.0 months. Additionally, 35 (87.5%) patients had a smoking history. Twenty-eight (70.0%) IPF-SCLC patients were concurrent with one or more other underlying diseases. Emphysema was detected in 26 (65%) patients via chest CT. IPF and SCLC were diagnosed during the same period in 23 (57.5%) patients, whereas SCLC was diagnosed during the follow-up of IPF in the remaining 17 patients. However, pirfenidone and nintedanib were only prescribed to two patients, respectively. Most patients were diagnosed with late-stage SCLC: 17 (42.5%) patients had stage IV SCLC, and 15 (37.5%) patients had stage III SCLC. Furthermore, with respect to anticancer therapy, one (2.5%) patient received no chemotherapy, 2 (5%) patients received oral etoposide, 37 (92.5%) patients received intravenous chemotherapy, and 11 (27.5%) patients received pulmonary radiotherapy. Finally, 29 (72.5%) patients died during follow-up. The main causes of death were acute exacerbation of IPF (AE-IPF) (13 patients, 44.8%) and progression of SCLC (12 patients, 41.4%). Conclusions: The patients with IPF-SCLC included in our studies were mainly elderly males with a heavy smoking index, most of whom were diagnosed with late-stage SCLC. Antifibrotic medications for IPF were uncommon, and chemotherapy was the main cancer treatment. The progression of uncontrolled SCLC and AE-IPF were the main causes of death. Clinicians should consider early initiation of antifibrotic therapy alongside chemotherapy, monitor for the occurrence of AE-IPF, and adopt multidisciplinary management.

items.title: Development and internal validation of a prediction model for severe postoperative complications (Thoracic Morbidity and Mortality Grade ≥ III) after radical esophagectomy
items.abstract: Background: Severe complications after radical esophagectomy remain a major clinical concern, highlighting the need for early postoperative risk stratification. Existing prediction models rely largely on preoperative factors, and models incorporating early postoperative inflammatory biomarkers to predict severe complications remain limited. This study aimed to develop and internally validate a nomogram integrating baseline characteristics and postoperative day (POD) 1 inflammatory biomarkers to predict severe postoperative complications after radical esophagectomy. Methods: Clinical data from 606 consecutive patients (2019-2025) were analyzed. Severe complications were defined as Thoracic Morbidity and Mortality (TM&M) grade ≥ III within 30 days after surgery. Candidate predictors, measured at baseline and from venous blood collected at 06:00 AM on POD 1, included demographics, surgical variables, and inflammatory biomarkers. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression with 10-fold cross-validation was embedded within a 1,000-bootstrap internal validation framework to avoid data leakage, followed by multivariable logistic regression. Results: Severe complications occurred in 178 patients (29.4%). Age [adjusted odds ratio (OR) =1.04], operative time (OR =1.04 per 10-min increase), and non-middle tumor location (OR =1.58) were independent predictors (all P<0.05). Female sex (OR =0.60), neoadjuvant therapy (OR =0.52), and POD 1 lymphocyte-to-monocyte ratio (D1-LMR, OR =0.76) were protective factors. The nomogram yielded an apparent AUC of 0.685 (95% confidence interval: 0.635-0.735) and a bootstrap optimism-corrected AUC of 0.672. At the optimal cutoff of 0.28 determined by the Youden index, sensitivity was 68.5%, specificity 63.4%, positive predictive value 45.2%, and negative predictive value 82.1%. Calibration was excellent (calibration slope =0.942, intercept =0.018, Brier score =0.184). Adding D1-LMR significantly improved predictive performance over baseline clinical models (ΔAUC =0.034, net reclassification improvement =0.158, P=0.008). Decision curve analysis confirmed positive net clinical benefits across threshold probabilities of 2-45%. Conclusions: Integrating baseline features and D1-LMR, this nomogram provides an exploratory early risk-stratification tool on POD 1 to optimize perioperative management and intensive care unit resource allocation.
items.limitations: Several limitations should also be acknowledged. First, the single-center retrospective design may introduce selection and information biases. Second, although outcome assessors were blinded to biomarker data, retrospective TM&M grading may still be influenced by documentation quality. Third, external validation was not performed, and the generalizability of the model across institutions with different surgical techniques and perioperative protocols remains uncertain. Finally, the moderate AUC suggests that additional predictors, such as intraoperative hemodynamic parameters, pulmonary function, and surgeon-related factors, may further improve predictive performance.

items.title: Association between early vein graft failure and long-term major adverse cardiovascular events following off-pump coronary artery bypass grafting: an exploratory retrospective cohort study
items.abstract: Background: Early vein graft failure (VGF) following coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) is far from rare and often clinically silent. While mid-to-late graft failure is established to predict adverse clinical events, the long-term prognostic impact of predischarge early VGF remains poorly defined. This study aimed to evaluate the association between early VGF and 10-year clinical outcomes following off-pump CABG.Methods: In this exploratory retrospective cohort study, adult patients undergoing elective isolated off-pump CABG using vein grafts with early postoperative coronary computed tomography angiography between July 2014 and December 2015 were consecutively included. Baseline, intraoperative, and postoperative data were collected from electronic medical records. VGF was defined as Fitzgibbon grade B (≥50% stenosis) or O (occlusion). Patients were stratified into the early VGF group (with at least one failed vein graft) and non-early VGF group (without failed vein grafts). Clinical follow-up was conducted through routine outpatient visits or standardized telephone interviews in accordance with institutional protocol. Primary outcomes included 10-year major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE, composite of all-cause death, myocardial infarction, stroke, or revascularization) and its individual components. Secondary outcomes included perioperative myocardial injury and perioperative myocardial infarction (PMI). Propensity score overlap weighting was applied to adjust for baseline confounders. Exploratory post-hoc landmark and piecewise Cox analyses were performed to address non-proportional hazards.Results: A total of 233 patients were included in the analyses (mean age 64.3±7.5 years; 18.4% female). Among them, early VGF was identified in 33 (14.2%) patients and 41 (5.9%) vein grafts. Early VGF numerically increased the risk of perioperative myocardial injury [45.5% vs. 30.5%, odds ratio (OR) 1.90, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.89–4.01; P=0.09] and PMI (12.1% vs. 6.0%, OR 2.16, 95% CI: 0.57–6.69; P=0.21), though without statistical significance. Over a median follow-up of 9.6 years, there was no statistically significant difference in 10-year MACE between the two groups [early VGF 51.5% vs. non-early VGF 48.2%; adjusted hazard ratio (aHR) 1.31, 95% CI: 0.76–2.24; P=0.33]. In exploratory landmark analyses addressing non-proportional hazards (P=0.03), early VGF was associated with a higher risk of MACE within the first 2 years post-surgery (aHR 2.18, 95% CI: 1.14–4.17; P=0.02), which attenuated beyond the 2-year landmark (aHR 0.56, 95% CI: 0.22–1.46; P=0.24). Additionally, early VGF was associated with a higher risk of repeat revascularization (18.2% vs. 7.7%; aHR 3.06, 95% CI: 1.13–8.31; P=0.03).Conclusions: Predischarge early VGF was not significantly associated with the overall 10-year risk of MACE following off-pump CABG. Exploratory findings regarding early risk clustering within 2 years and an increased risk of repeat revascularization remain hypothesis-generating. Further prospective studies are warranted to validate these observations.
items.limitations: This study has several limitations. First, given its retrospective, single-center design with a modest sample size and relatively sparse event counts, the statistical power was limited, highlighting the exploratory nature of our study and restricting the generalizability of our findings. Second, although propensity score OW was applied to adjust for key confounding variables, potential unmeasured residual confounding cannot be completely ruled out; thus, our findings should be interpreted with caution and cannot be used for causal inferences or establishing independent prognostic causality. Third, all landmark analyses, time-varying risk evaluations, individual components, and secondary outcomes were exploratory and post-hoc in nature. Specifically, the 2-year landmark breakpoint was chosen post hoc based on non-proportional hazards testing and curve inspection rather than a pre-specified clinical hypothesis.

items.title: Development and internal validation of a chest CT radiomics model for identifying pneumoconiosis
items.abstract: Background: Pneumoconiosis is a major occupational lung disease with an insidious onset, making early diagnosis challenging. We aimed to develop and internally validate a chest computed tomography (CT)-based radiomics model for objective identification of pneumoconiosis and to support subjective visual diagnosis in dust-exposed individuals. Methods: This retrospective study consecutively enrolled 474 patients with documented occupational dust exposure who underwent pneumoconiosis evaluation at The Third People's Hospital of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region between January 2020 and December 2024. Eligible participants had high-resolution chest CT images and no history of pulmonary surgery or trauma; those with coexisting respiratory disease, severe systemic dysfunction, or poor image quality were excluded. The reference standard was expert-panel consensus according to GBZ 70-2015 criteria. Lung parenchyma was semi-automatically segmented using a region-growing algorithm in three-dimensional (3D) Slicer, and radiomics features were extracted with the Deepwise Multimodal Research Platform. From 2,153 features, Pearson correlation filtering (r≥0.9 excluded) and analysis of variance (ANOVA) F-test (P<0.05) selected the 10 most discriminative features. Data were randomly divided into training and test sets. A logistic regression model was constructed and evaluated using area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve (AUC), sensitivity, specificity, calibration, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Results: Of 474 patients, 293 had pneumoconiosis (all stage I) and 181 were dust-exposed controls. The model achieved AUCs of 0.804 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.754-0.853] in the training set (n=331) and 0.759 (95% CI: 0.680-0.838) in the test set (n=143). At the optimal threshold, sensitivity and specificity were 76.2% and 68.3% in the training set and 61.8% and 67.1% in the test set, respectively. Calibration curves showed good agreement between predicted and observed outcomes, and DCA confirmed net clinical benefit across a range of threshold probabilities. Conclusions: This CT-based whole-lung radiomics model, without manual lesion delineation, shows promise for early pneumoconiosis identification in dust-exposed populations, with favorable diagnostic accuracy and clinical utility. However, the findings are preliminary and require external validation in independent multicenter cohorts before clinical implementation.

items.title: A matter of size: 20-Fr vs. 24-Fr chest drainage after uniportal video-assisted thoracoscopic lobectomy for non-small cell lung cancer—a randomized trial
items.abstract: Background: Chest drains are routinely used after pulmonary lobectomy to evacuate air and pleural fluid and promote lung re-expansion. However, the optimal chest tube caliber remains controversial, particularly in the context of minimally invasive surgery. Smaller-bore drains may reduce discomfort, whereas larger drains may provide more effective evacuation of air and fluid. The aim of this study was to compare 20-Fr and 24-Fr chest tubes after uniportal video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (uVATS) lobectomy for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), with particular focus on postoperative pain, pleural drainage-related outcomes, and recovery.Methods: This single-center prospective randomized study included 80 patients undergoing uVATS lobectomy for NSCLC, who were allocated 1:1 to receive either a 20-Fr or 24-Fr chest tube (n=40 per group). The primary outcome was postoperative pain at 24 hours, assessed using the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS). Secondary outcomes included NRS pain at 12 and 48 hours, prolonged air leak (PAL), chest tube duration, subcutaneous emphysema, analgesic requirements, respiratory physiokinesitherapy outcomes, and length of stay (LOS). Pneumothorax (PNX) and pleural effusion (PE) were evaluated as exploratory radiographic outcomes.Results: The 24-Fr group showed significantly lower rates of PNX on postoperative day (POD) 3 (27.5% vs. 60.0%, P=0.003) and PE on POD2 (50.0% vs. 77.5%, P=0.01). Conversely, patients with 24-Fr drains reported significantly higher NRS pain scores at 12 hours [4.0 (3.0–5.0) vs. 2.0 (2.0–4.0), P=0.001], 24 hours [5.0 (4.0–6.0) vs. 4.0 (3.0–5.0), P=0.002], and 48 hours [5.5 (4.8–6.2) vs. 4.5 (3.0–6.0), P=0.02]. No significant differences were observed in PAL (27.5% vs. 47.5%, P=0.07), chest tube duration, subcutaneous emphysema, analgesic requirements, or LOS.Conclusions: After uVATS lobectomy, 24-Fr chest tubes were associated with better early radiographic pleural control but greater postoperative pain. These findings highlight a trade-off between drainage efficiency and patient comfort and support an individualized approach to chest tube selection.Trial Registration: The trial was registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT07827885).

items.title: Factors associated with postoperative sleep disturbance in patients undergoing thoracoscopic radical resection for lung cancer: a retrospective cohort study
items.abstract: Background: Postoperative sleep disturbance (PSD) is common in patients following surgery, resulting in severe cognitive and mood disturbances, and even increase mortality risk. This study aimed to identify factors associated with PSD in patients undergoing thoracoscopic radical resection for lung cancer.Methods: We retrospectively identified sixty-two patients who underwent thoracoscopic radical resection of lung cancer at Tangdu Hospital, a tertiary teaching hospital in Xi’an, China, from June 2023 through October 2024. PSD was defined as a Richards-Campbell Sleep Questionnaire (RCSQ) score <60 on postoperative day 2 (POD2). Preoperative sleep quality was assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Pain was measured using the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS) at rest and during coughing on POD1 and POD2. intraoperative fluid volume, and POD2 cough-induced pain, selected a priori based on clinical relevance and prior evidence. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors independently associated with PSD.Results: Of 62 patients (mean age 67.5 years; 45.2% female), 36 (58.1%) met the RCSQ-defined criteria for PSD on POD2. Three factors were independently associated with PSD: preoperative PSQI score [odds ratio (OR) =1.58, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.19–2.10, P=0.001], intraoperative fluid volume (OR =1.004 per mL, 95% CI: 1.001–1.007, P=0.02), and POD2 cough-induced pain (OR =2.23 per point, 95% CI: 1.36–3.66, P=0.001). The model demonstrated good calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow P=0.10) and discrimination (Nagelkerke R2=0.652).Conclusions: Preoperative sleep quality, intraoperative fluid volume, and POD2 cough-induced pain were independently associated with PSD in this cohort. These exploratory findings highlight the importance of closer assessment of potentially high-risk patients, but require validation in larger prospective studies before being translated into definitive preventive strategies.

items.title: Simplified synchronous division of pulmonary vessels and the horizontal fissure during thoracoscopic right upper lobectomy for lung cancer with incomplete fissure: a propensity score-matched study
items.abstract: Background: Incomplete horizontal fissure increases the technical difficulty of thoracoscopic right upper lobectomy and may increase parenchymal injury and stapler use. We evaluated a simplified synchronous disconnection of pulmonary vessels and the horizontal fissure (SSDPVH) for right upper lobe non-small cell lung cancer with incomplete fissure. Methods: This single-center retrospective cohort included 140 consecutive patients who underwent thoracoscopic right upper lobectomy, including 60 treated with SSDPVH and 80 treated with conventional video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (cVATS). Patients with incomplete or absent horizontal fissure were identified on preoperative high-resolution computed tomography (CT), with final intraoperative confirmation of anatomical suitability. Propensity score matching generated 50 well-balanced pairs. The primary endpoints were operative time, stapler cartridge use, postoperative air leak, and hospitalization cost, reported in Chinese yuan (CNY). Secondary endpoints included blood loss, postoperative stay, nodal yield, perioperative complications, and 18-month follow-up. Results: 36,145±945 CNY; mean difference -3,658 CNY, 95% CI: -4,022 to -3,294; P<0.001). Prolonged air leak occurred in 2 patients (4.0%) after SSDPVH and 6 patients (12.0%) after cVATS (risk ratio 0.33, 95% CI: 0.07-1.58; P=0.27). Blood loss, postoperative stay, and lymph node harvest were similar between groups. No postoperative bleeding, conversion to open thoracotomy, recurrence, or death was observed in either matched cohort during 18 months of follow-up. Conclusions: In this matched retrospective cohort, SSDPVH was associated with shorter operations, fewer stapler reloads, and lower hospitalization cost during thoracoscopic right upper lobectomy for lung cancer with incomplete fissure. The study was not powered to determine differences in postoperative complications or long-term oncologic outcomes.

items.title: Global burden of respiratory infections and tuberculosis and risk factors, 1990–2021: a systematic analysis of the Global Burden of Disease Study 2021
items.abstract: Background: Respiratory infections and tuberculosis (RIT) remain major contributors to global morbidity and mortality, with pronounced geographic and socioeconomic disparities. The emergence of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) has further disrupted existing control efforts, highlighting the need to reassess temporal trends, socioeconomic disparities, and risk-factor changes. This study aimed to quantify temporal trends, characterize geographic and socioeconomic disparities, and assess changes in risk-factor-attributable burden of RIT from 1990 to 2021. Methods: Using Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2021 data, we quantified incidence, prevalence, deaths, and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) of RIT across 204 countries/regions from 1990 to 2021. Temporal trends were assessed using average annual percentage change (AAPC) and joinpoint regression. Associations with the Socio-demographic Index (SDI) were examined using Pearson correlation and generalized additive models (GAMs). Risk factor-attributable burdens were estimated using comparative risk assessment (CRA) methodology. Results: In 2021, RIT caused 11.25 million deaths and 349.68 million DALYs worldwide, accounting for 16.59% of total deaths and 12.15% of total DALYs. COVID-19 became the leading cause of RIT mortality (7.89 million deaths), followed by lower RIT. We identified four distinct regional burden trajectories, which reflected differences in health-system capacity and pandemic impact. SDI showed strong negative associations with age-standardized DALYs, deaths, and prevalence, but showed no significant association with incidence. From 1990 to 2021, environmental and behavioral risk factor burdens declined substantially, whereas metabolic risks rose, particularly in high-SDI regions. Conclusions: Despite declining age-standardized rates (ASRs), the absolute global burden of RIT continues to rise due to demographic transitions and the COVID-19 pandemic. Persistent socioeconomic disparities call for integrated strategies that combine vaccination, tuberculosis control, risk-factor reduction, and health-system strengthening to improve respiratory health equity.
items.limitations: There are limitations in this analysis. GBD estimates depend on data sources that vary in quality and completeness, especially in low-SDI regions. Incomplete vital registration, limited laboratory testing, weak surveillance systems, and underreporting may lead to underestimation of RIT burden, whereas changes in diagnostic intensity, coding practices, or cause-of-death attribution during COVID-19 may cause overestimation or misclassification, particularly for non-COVID respiratory infections. SDI captures broad socioeconomic conditions but does not fully reflect health-system governance, cultural practices, or environmental exposures. CRA estimates also require cautious interpretation because they depend on modeled exposure distributions, relative risks, and TMRELs, and may not fully account for interactions between multiple risks or regional differences in exposure measurement.

items.title: Lymph node metastasis patterns and survival in patients with esophageal squamous cell carcinoma undergoing McKeown esophagectomy: a retrospective cohort study
items.abstract: Background: The distribution of lymph node metastases in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) varies with tumor location. We examined nodal metastasis patterns and factors associated with overall survival in patients undergoing McKeown esophagectomy. Methods: This single-center retrospective study analyzed hospital records of 909 patients with ESCC who underwent McKeown esophagectomy between December 2011 and July 2019, including total minimally invasive and hybrid procedures. Nodal involvement was summarized using node-based metastatic percentages and patient-level positivity among patients with evaluable regional records. Survival was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier methods and separate univariable Cox models for nodal status and recorded tumor length. Exploratory ABO analyses used Firth logistic regression for nodal positivity and a multivariable Cox model stratified by tumor location for overall survival. Analysis-specific exclusions were applied to missing or unresolved data. Results: The cohort included 535 men (58.9%), and the mean age was 64.2±7.2 years among 904 patients with recorded age. Tumors were located in the upper, middle, and lower thoracic esophagus in 200, 603, and 106 patients, respectively; 407 patients had pT3 disease. Nodal positivity was identified in 326 of 878 patients with evaluable nodal status (37.1%). Regional nodal involvement varied by tumor location. Reliable survival data were available for 895 patients, with 347 deaths and a median follow-up of 51 months. The nodal-status analysis included 864 patients and 320 deaths within 60 months; nodal positivity was associated with poorer survival [unadjusted hazard ratio (HR), 3.054; 95% confidence interval (CI): 2.446-3.821]. Recorded tumor length >3.79 cm was also associated with poorer survival (unadjusted HR, 2.693; 95% CI: 2.162-3.372). Both P values were <0.001. In exploratory adjusted analyses, the overall ABO association was significant for survival (P=0.01), but not for nodal positivity (P=0.21). Conclusions: Nodal involvement varied by tumor location. Nodal positivity and greater recorded tumor length were associated with poorer survival in univariable analyses. These findings do not establish the benefit of changing the extent of lymphadenectomy.

items.title: Ethical considerations in the management of complications after lung resection: a narrative review
items.abstract: Background and Objective: Complications following lung resection present complex clinical, ethical and interpersonal challenges that extend beyond technical management. Although substantial literature addresses the prevention and treatment of complications after lung resection, there is limited guidance regarding the ethical principles that should shape clinical decision-making as complications evolve. This review proposes a practical ethical framework for the management of complications following lung resection. Methods: Recommendations were developed based on clinical expertise and relevant published sources. A narrative literature search was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE and Embase, supplemented by targeted searches of relevant clinical resources and reference lists. English-language literature published within the last fifteen years was considered, with more recent evidence prioritized alongside foundational literature. Where lung resection-specific evidence was limited, related thoracic surgery, critical care, perioperative medicine, and surgical ethics literature was incorporated. Key Content and Findings: The developed framework is focused on six foundational ethical principles spanning patient-centered and provider-/systems-centered domains. Patient-centered principles include autonomy, shared decision-making and proportionate goal-concordant care, which help define patient values and integrate those values with clinical expertise to align treatment strategies with meaningful outcomes. Provider-/systems-centered principles include beneficence, nonmaleficence, justice, transparency and accountability, all of which guide professional responsibility, equitable care, honest communication and collaboration throughout recovery. The application of these principles is examined across the preoperative, intraoperative and postoperative phases of care. Conclusions: This framework emphasizes aligning treatment decisions with patient-defined goals, while balancing the potential benefits and burdens of intervention. Overall, these six ethical principles provide a structured and durable framework for navigating complications following lung resection.

items.title: Correlation between chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and comorbidities—a systematic analysis integrating global burden of disease and mendelian randomization study
items.abstract: Background: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) frequently coexists with multiple comorbidities. However, the long-term trends, regional disparities, and potential causal relationships in the global burden of these comorbidities remain to be systematically elucidated. This study aimed to characterize the disease burden of common comorbidities in patients with COPD and to assess the potential causal relationships between these comorbidities and COPD. Methods: This study integrated data from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 (GBD 2023) and conducted two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) analyses. Based on GBD data from 1990 to 2023, we performed descriptive burden assessment, Das Gupta decomposition, Bayesian age-period-cohort modelling, exploratory correlation analysis, and formal age-interaction regression. Using summary statistics from the FinnGen consortium, we evaluated bidirectional genetic associations between COPD and various comorbidities primarily via the inverse variance weighted (IVW) method with false discovery rate (FDR) correction for multiple comparisons. The comorbidities of focus included asthma, anxiety disorders, major depressive disorder, pulmonary hypertension, hypertensive heart disease, ischemic heart disease, musculoskeletal disorders, osteoporosis, and respiratory tract cancers. Results: The absolute burden of comorbidities in COPD continued to increase, albeit driven by distinct factors. Population aging and growth were identified as the primary drivers for the rising burden of several COPD comorbidities, such as ischemic heart disease and musculoskeletal disorders. Significant regional inequalities were observed in disease distribution: high Socio-demographic Index (SDI) regions bore a heavier burden of musculoskeletal and mental disorders, whereas middle and low SDI regions exhibited more pronounced mortality and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) attributable to ischemic heart disease. Formal interaction models demonstrated significant age heterogeneity in the ecological associations between COPD prevalence and all eight comorbidities after Benjamini-Hochberg correction (all q ≤0.028). MR analyses provided evidence supporting bidirectional genetic associations between COPD and specific comorbidities. Genetically predicted COPD was significantly associated with an increased risk of asthma and depression (FDR <0.05), and conversely, genetic susceptibility to asthma and depression was associated with a higher risk of developing COPD (FDR <0.05). Conclusions: The comorbidity patterns between COPD and its key concomitant conditions are influenced by multiple factors, including demographic structure, regional development levels, and shared biological mechanisms. Our findings underscore the necessity of shifting from a single-disease management model towards integrated care strategies that emphasize comorbidity screening and holistic patient management.

items.title: Speckle perfusion dynamics as an objective marker of sympathetic interruption and its association with compensatory sweating after thoracic sympathectomy
items.abstract: Background: Thoracic sympathectomy is an effective treatment for primary palmar hyperhidrosis; however, postoperative compensatory sweating remains a common and unpredictable complication. Objective physiologic markers for assessing sympathetic interruption and predicting the risk of compensatory sweating remain insufficiently established. This study aimed to evaluate perioperative speckle perfusion dynamics as an objective marker of sympathetic interruption and to assess its association with compensatory sweating after thoracic sympathectomy. Methods: A retrospective cohort of 117 patients undergoing thoracic sympathectomy with perioperative speckle perfusion assessment was analyzed. Perfusion was measured at preoperative, pre-trigger, and postoperative time points. Percent changes from baseline were calculated. Associations with compensatory sweating and cold sensation were evaluated using logistic regression. Results: Perfusion increased from 120.9±30.7 preoperatively to 128.1±29.8 at the pre-trigger state and decreased to 102.7±23.3 postoperatively (all P<0.001). Percent pre-trigger change was associated with compensatory sweating (odds ratio 1.03, 95% confidence interval: 1.00-1.05; P=0.02). Heart rate correlated with pre-trigger response (r=0.21, P=0.02) but was not independently predictive. Cold sensation was related to body mass index. Conclusions: Speckle perfusion demonstrates measurable perioperative changes in cutaneous microvascular perfusion associated with thoracic sympathetic interruption, supporting its potential as an objective physiologic marker of the vascular response to sympathectomy. Greater pre-trigger perfusion response was associated with clinically significant compensatory sweating in univariable analysis, although this association was attenuated after multivariable adjustment and remains exploratory. These findings suggest that preoperative vascular reactivity may reflect an autonomic phenotype relevant to compensatory sweating and warrant prospective physiologic validation.

items.title: Clinical and prognostic analysis of unicentric mediastinal Castleman’s disease: a 10-year retrospective series study
items.abstract: Background: Castleman disease (CD) is a rare lymphoproliferative disorder, and unicentric mediastinal CD (UMCD) represents an uncommon thoracic manifestation for which surgical resection remains the mainstay of treatment.This study aims to: (I) characterize the anatomical distribution of UMCD in a single-center cohort; (II) evaluate the efficacy of video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) for UMCD resection and identify preoperative predictors of thoracotomy; (III) analyze prognostic outcomes in surgically managed UMCD patients. Methods: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 49 consecutive UMCD patients (26 males, 23 females; mean age 37.27±15.27 years) undergoing surgical resection at the department of thoracic surgery (Tangdu Hospital, Fourth Military Medical University) between May 2014 and October 2024. Demographic characteristics, anatomical distributions, and perioperative outcomes were systematically analyzed. Comparative analysis between VATS and thoracotomy groups was performed using independent samples t-tests. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression identified predictors of thoracotomy, with diagnostic performance evaluated via receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Survival outcomes were assessed using Kaplan-Meier methodology. Results: 5.52±3.54 days, P<0.05). Multivariate analysis identified tumor diameter >6.6 cm (P<0.05) and arterial-phase contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) attenuation >102 Hounsfield units (HU) (P<0.05) as independent predictors of thoracotomy. ROC analysis revealed an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.875 for the combined diagnostic model. With a median follow-up duration of 52 months, the VATS group maintained 100% recurrence-free survival. In the thoracotomy group, three patients succumbed to disease (two from local recurrence refractory to conservative therapy, one from postoperative pneumonia with respiratory failure following pneumonectomy). The overall survival (OS) rate for the cohort was 91.83%. Conclusions: Station 3A lymph nodes represent the predominant anatomical site of UMCD involvement. VATS resection confers significant advantages over thoracotomy, including reduced operative time, blood loss, and postoperative recovery duration. The diameter >6.6 cm and arterial-phase CT attenuation >102 HU of tumors serve as reliable preoperative indicators for thoracotomy. Early surgical intervention correlates with favorable prognosis, while postoperative complications and local recurrence demonstrate significant association with mortality.

items.title: Development and internal validation of a nomogram for predicting high-risk postoperative status after thoracoscopic pulmonary wedge resection: a single-center retrospective cohort study
items.abstract: Background: Routine placement of a chest tube after thoracoscopic pulmonary wedge resection may cause postoperative pain and delay recovery, yet safe implementation requires accurate identification of patients at low risk for significant drainage, air leak, and pneumothorax. This study aimed to identify independent risk factors for failure to meet early chest tube removal criteria after video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) pulmonary wedge resection, and to establish a validated nomogram for individualized risk stratification to inform postoperative chest tube management decisions. Methods: This retrospective single-center study included 680 patients who underwent VATS wedge resection between January 2023 and December 2025. Low-risk status was defined as chest tube drainage ≤200 mL within 24 hours, absence of air leak on coughing, and no significant pneumothorax on chest radiography. The cohort was randomly divided into a training set (70%) and an internal validation set (30%). Univariate and multivariate logistic regression were used to identify independent predictors of high-risk status. A nomogram was developed and internally validated using bootstrap resampling (500 replicates). Model performance was assessed by discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, AUC), calibration, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Results: Six independent predictors were identified: age [odds ratio (OR) =1.042, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.019-1.066, P<0.001], lower forced expiratory volume in 1 second percentage (FEV1%) predicted (OR =0.907, 95% CI: 0.883-0.928, P<0.001), neoadjuvant chemotherapy (OR =2.794, 95% CI: 1.244-6.340, P=0.013), operative duration (OR =1.033, 95% CI: 1.018-1.049, P<0.001), number of stapler cartridges used (OR =1.173, 95% CI: 1.106-1.258, P=0.041), and pleural adhesion degree (OR =3.649, 95% CI: 1.340-13.351, P=0.023). The nomogram showed good discrimination (training AUC =0.865; validation AUC =0.835) and excellent calibration (bootstrap-corrected calibration curve; Hosmer-Lemeshow P=0.62). DCA confirmed its clinical utility across threshold probabilities of 10-40%. No significant difference was observed between training and validation AUCs (ΔAUC =0.030, P=0.433). Conclusions: A six-variable nomogram incorporating age, FEV1% predicted, neoadjuvant chemotherapy, operative duration, number of stapler cartridges used, and pleural adhesion degree was developed to predict failure to meet early chest tube removal criteria after VATS wedge resection. This tool may assist in individualized risk stratification to inform clinical decision-making regarding chest tube management.

items.title: Clinical efficacy of minimally invasive cardiac valve surgery concomitant with radiofrequency ablation for atrial fibrillation: a single-center retrospective study
items.abstract: Background: Concomitant atrial fibrillation (AF) and valvular heart disease (VHD) present complex clinical challenges. Standard radiofrequency ablation (RFA) combined with valve surgery via median sternotomy offers robust rhythm correction but causes significant surgical trauma. Minimally invasive cardiac valve surgery with concomitant RFA (MICVS-RFA) is a promising strategy, but clinical data regarding its comprehensive safety, efficacy, and predictive risk factors for AF recurrence remain scarce. Thus, we aimed to evaluate the safety and clinical efficacy of MICVS-RFA and to develop an exploratory prognostic model for risk stratification. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 146 patients with concomitant VHD and AF who underwent MICVS-RFA between April 1, 2020, and August 1, 2025. Surgical cohorts included mitral valve replacement (MVR; n=34), mitral valve repair (MVr; n=19), MVR combined with tricuspid valve repair (MVR + TVr; n=57), and MVr combined with tricuspid valve repair (MVr + TVr; n=36). Pre-operative predictors for post-operative AF recurrence were identified using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) and elastic net regularization integrated within a multiple imputation framework to develop an exploratory model. Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) improvements were assessed dynamically. Results: Procedural success was achieved in all 146 patients, with an overall 30-day freedom from recurrent AF (FFAF) rate of 89.7% and no observed major adverse events (stroke, bleeding, or thromboembolism) within the first post-operative month. Length of stay (LOS) showed no statistical differences among surgical cohorts (P=0.71). Logistic regression modeling identified pre-operative metoprolol usage as associated with lower odds of AF recurrence [odds ratio (OR) =0.17; 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.04–0.62], while pre-operative pulmonary hypertension (PH) showed a non-significant association with higher odds of AF recurrence (OR =3.07; 95% CI: 0.67–14.10). The predictive model showed moderate discrimination [bootstrap-corrected area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) =0.773] and apparent calibration. Patients with baseline LVEF <55% experienced superior functional recovery compared to those with LVEF ≥55% (ΔLVEF: 13.07%±2.56% vs. 0.18%±0.80%, P<0.001). Conclusions: MICVS-RFA was a feasible “dual minimally invasive” strategy that permits concomitant treatment of valvular pathology and AF through a minimally invasive approach, minimizing perioperative trauma. Comparative and long-term effects require further study.
items.limitations: Regularization and bootstrap resampling may reduce optimism but cannot overcome the limitations imposed by only 15 recurrence events. Furthermore, while confirming promising short-term outcomes, our data are limited by follow-up duration. External validation using MIMIC-IV was not feasible because of the limited number of comparable cases, insufficient procedural detail, and restricted longitudinal follow-up. Future studies using larger, multicenter cohorts with standardized procedural information and long-term rhythm follow-up are warranted to externally validate the predictive model and to further determine the durability of the observed clinical benefits, particularly with respect to long-term rhythm maintenance, survival, and stroke reduction. MICVS-RFA is an integrated, feasible procedure for patients requiring concurrent valvular intervention and rhythm control.

items.title: An explainable machine learning model combining intratumoral and peritumoral computed tomography radiomics with maximum standard uptake value for predicting International Association for the Study of Lung Cancer grading and prognosis in stage I pure-solid lung adenocarcinoma
items.abstract: Background: The novel International Association for the Study of Lung Cancer (IASLC) grading system provides important prognostic information for lung adenocarcinoma; however, preoperative noninvasive prediction of this grading remains challenging. This study aimed to evaluate the predictive value of a combined intratumoral and peritumoral radiomics model based on computed tomography (CT) and maximum standard uptake value (SUV max ) for preoperative prediction of the novel IASLC grading and prognosis in stage I pure-solid invasive lung adenocarcinoma (LADC). Methods: Patients with stage I pure-solid LADC from The First Affiliated Hospital of Wenzhou Medical University were retrospectively included and randomly assigned to a training set (n=207) and a testing set (n=89) in a 7:3 ratio. There were 851 radiomics features extracted from the gross tumor volume (GTV) and the GTV incorporating peritumoral 3, 6, and 9 mm regions (GPTV3, GPTV6, GPTV9). A combined model based on an individual radiomics signature, SUV max , and clinical independent predictors was constructed. Recurrence-free survival (RFS) was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier survival method, while independent prognostic factors were identified through Cox proportional hazards models. Results: The GPTV3 model demonstrated a higher area under the curve (AUC) compared to other individual radiomics models, with AUCs of 0.804 and 0.715 in the training and testing sets. Tumor size was identified as an independent predictor of high-grade IASLC grading in the clinical model. The combined model showed AUCs of 0.837 and 0.767 for the training and testing sets, respectively, which were higher than those of the individual GPTV3 and SUV max models. The high-risk group was associated with poorer RFS (P<0.05). Pathological and predictive IASLC grade, smoking history, and tumor size were independent prognostic factors. Conclusions: The interpretable machine learning model can predict the novel IASLC grading and prognosis in stage I pure-solid LADC.

items.title: Multidimensional patient-reported recovery and early pain trajectories within 90 days after the Nuss procedure: a retrospective cohort study
items.abstract: Background: Postoperative assessment after the Nuss procedure often emphasizes pain intensity, although recovery also includes functional and procedure-specific symptoms. We characterized multidimensional patient-reported recovery during the first 90 postoperative days. Methods: This retrospective single-center cohort included 93 patients with at least three valid assessments on a 10-item Nuss-specific symptom and function scale. Records were summarized in five postoperative windows. Longitudinal domain patterns, pain-function discordance, and exploratory early pain trajectories were described. Internal consistency of the scale and the perioperative anesthesia and analgesia context were additionally evaluated. Results: The cohort contributed 1,729 records. Pain declined from a median of 5.50 [interquartile range (IQR), 4.25-6.50] during days 1-7 to 2.33 (IQR, 1.00-4.00) during days 15-30, whereas functional limitation was 4.82 (IQR, 3.86-5.94) and 3.00 (IQR, 1.71-4.70), respectively. During days 15-30, 11/88 patients (12.5%) had relatively low pain but persistent functional limitation under exploratory, distribution-informed thresholds. An exploratory two-class model yielded an improving class (79/89) and a persistent-high-pain class (10/89). Among 79 patients with trajectory and later outcome data, residual pain during days 31-90 occurred in 6/9 patients in the persistent-high-pain class and 11/70 in the improving class. Internal-consistency coefficients across windows ranged from 0.900 to 0.950 for the symptom domain and from 0.737 to 0.909 for the function domain. Conclusions: Recovery during the first 90 days after the Nuss procedure was multidimensional, with functional limitation and bar awareness improving more slowly than pain. Exploratory trajectory findings also indicated heterogeneity in early recovery. Multidomain follow-up may provide a more complete view of recovery, and prospective studies with standardized analgesia, neuropathic-pain measures, and longer follow-up are warranted.

items.title: From risk factors to individualized prediction: development and internal validation of a machine learning model for early identification of postoperative pneumonia after lung cancer surgery
items.abstract: Background: Postoperative pneumonia (POP) remains one of the most common infectious complications following lung cancer surgery and is associated with substantial morbidity. Although several risk factors for POP have been identified, clinically applicable approaches for early individualized risk stratification remain limited. This study aimed to develop and internally validate machine learning models for early prediction of POP using routinely available perioperative variables. Methods: In this prospective single-center cohort study, 258 consecutive patients undergoing pulmonary resection for non-small cell lung cancer or pulmonary carcinoid tumors were screened, of whom 200 were included in the final study cohort. POP was defined by newly developed postoperative radiographic abnormalities accompanied by clinical signs of infection requiring antibiotic therapy. Machine learning models, including logistic regression (LR), Naïve Bayes (NB), random forest (RF), and XGBoost (XGB), were developed to predict POP using demographic, clinical, laboratory, surgical, and postoperative day 1 radiographic variables. Model performance was assessed using nested leave-one-out cross-validation and quantified by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC). A nomogram was constructed from the best-performing model to facilitate individualized risk estimation. Different decision thresholds were explored to evaluate clinically relevant trade-offs between sensitivity and specificity. Results: POP occurred in 47 of 200 patients (23.5%), while no POP-related mortality was observed. LR demonstrated the best predictive performance (AUROC 0.701±0.070), followed by NB (0.698±0.103), RF (0.656±0.217), and XGB (0.589±0.179). The most influential predictors included advanced age, perioperative changes in C-reactive protein concentration (ΔCRP), elevated preoperative CRP levels, prolonged operative duration, and abnormal postoperative day 1 chest radiographic findings. At a decision threshold of 25%, the model correctly identified 25 of 47 POP cases (53.2%), whereas increasing the threshold to 32.5% reduced false-positive classifications from 42 to 24 at the expense of missing an additional four POP cases. Conclusions: Machine learning models based on routinely available perioperative variables enabled early individualized prediction of POP following lung cancer surgery. LR provided the best balance between predictive performance, stability, and interpretability, allowing the development of an interpretable nomogram for individualized risk estimation. The model may have potential to support risk-adapted postoperative surveillance and more efficient allocation of healthcare resources; however, external validation is required before clinical implementation.

items.title: Interdisciplinary thoraco-plastic surgery for chest wall reconstruction: a single-center quality control project and clinical practice review
items.abstract: Thoracic defects arise from a broad spectrum of causes, including tumours, congenital deformities, infections, and radiation-induced damage. Their surgical management is often challenging and typically requires close interdisciplinary cooperation, particularly between thoracic and plastic surgeons. This retrospective project included all patients who underwent thoracic wall resection and subsequent reconstruction at the University Hospital Basel between January 2013 and January 2025. During this 12-year period, 89 patients with chest, lung, pleura, and breast pathologies underwent thoracic reconstruction. The proportion of patients with an oncological diagnosis was 17% (n=15). Overall, there were 63 men (71%) and 26 women (29%). The mean age was 64±13 years.
