Pectoralis major flaps were used in 34 patients; latissimus dorsi (LD) flaps were used in 25 patients, with additional pectoralis major flaps in 2 patients and a combination of pectoralis flap reconstruction with a vertical rectus abdominis myocutaneous (VRAM) flap in 3 patients. Isolated VRAM reconstruction was performed in 4 patients, and in one patient, transverse rectus abdominis myocutaneous (TRAM) flap reconstruction was performed. In 2 patients, the serratus anterior muscle was used, and in one patient each, a vastus lateralis flap and an obliquus externus flap were applied for defect coverage. In 16 patients, the defect was covered plastically by local skin rotation. Chest wall reconstruction following extensive thoracic resection is safe and effective when guided by a structured, stepwise approach and close interdisciplinary collaboration.

items.title: Lactate dehydrogenase to albumin ratio as a potential indicator of pathological response and prognosis in non-small cell lung cancer patients undergoing neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy followed by surgery
items.abstract: Background: In recent years, neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy followed by radical resection has become a new treatment option for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, there remains a paucity of simple yet effective biomarkers for assessing pathological response and long-term prognosis. This study aimed to investigate the potential value of serum lactate dehydrogenase to albumin ratio (LAR) in this clinical setting. Methods: The clinicopathological data of 81 consecutive patients with NSCLC who received neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy and radical surgery at Xuanwu Hospital, Capital Medical University between January 2019 and December 2024 were retrospectively analyzed. Baseline LAR, post-treatment LAR, and the ratio of baseline to post-treatment LAR were calculated and evaluated for their associations with pathologic response and event-free survival (EFS). Results: Of the 81 patients, 48 (59.3%) achieved major pathological response (MPR). MPR patients had significantly lower post-treatment LAR and a higher baseline to post-treatment LAR ratio than non-MPR patients, whereas baseline LAR showed no significant difference. Post-treatment LAR and baseline to post-treatment LAR ratio discriminatedMPR with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.747 and 0.719, respectively. Multivariate logistic regression identified post-treatment LAR [odds ratio (OR) =0.498, P=0.02] and radiological response (OR =6.297, P=0.008) as independent factors associated with MPR. Multivariate Cox regression demonstrated that higher post-treatment LAR [hazard ratio (HR) =1.664, P=0.003] and non-MPR status (HR =3.498, P=0.004) were independent prognostic factors for poor EFS. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis further revealed a positive association between post-treatment LAR and EFS risk, with higher LAR corresponding to increased HRs. A nomogram based on these two EFS prognostic factors demonstrated good calibration at 24 months with internal bootstrap validation (C-index =0.769). Conclusions: Post-treatment LAR could serve as a potential indicator for response assessment and long-term prognostication in NSCLC patients undergoing neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy. Its simplicity, cost-effectiveness, and accessibility through routine laboratory testing render it a promising candidate for integration into clinical practice.

items.title: Risk factors and clinical implications of sternal dehiscence following clamshell incision in bilateral lung transplantation
items.abstract: Background: Clamshell incisions provide excellent exposure for bilateral lung transplantation (BLT) but carry an inherent risk of sternal dehiscence. This study aimed to identify the risk factors for sternal dehiscence and evaluate its impact on pulmonary function. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 129 adult patients who underwent BLT via clamshell incision between 2007 and 2024. Sternal dehiscence was defined as radiographic nonunion of the sternum confirmed by chest computed tomography scan at least 3 months postoperatively, or any sternal dehiscence requiring surgical correction regardless of the time interval. Risk factors were identified using Firth's penalized likelihood logistic regression analysis. Pulmonary function tests were compared between patients with and without dehiscence at 1 year postoperatively and the last follow-up. Results: Sternal dehiscence occurred in 15 patients (11.6%), of which 11 (8.5%) were classified as major cases. Multivariable analysis identified male sex as an independent risk factor associated with dehiscence [odds ratio (OR) 8.89, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.27-108.74, P=0.02], whereas perioperative tracheostomy was independently associated with a lower incidence (OR =0.12, 95% CI: 0.02-0.53, P=0.004). Surgical closure techniques, including wiring and parasternal fixation, were not significantly associated with dehiscence (P=0.73 and P>0.99, respectively). No significant differences in pulmonary function were observed between groups at 1 year postoperatively and last follow-up. Conclusions: Male sex was independently associated with sternal dehiscence following BLT, whereas perioperative tracheostomy was associated with a lower incidence; these findings should be regarded as hypothesis-generating given the observational design. Pulmonary function during the follow-up period was not significantly associated with sternal dehiscence in this cohort. Surgeons may consider reinforced closure in male patients, while the protective role of tracheostomy warrants further study.

items.title: Neutrophil to lymphocyte ratio (NLR) predicts pathological response to neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy in resectable esophageal cancer: a retrospective study
items.abstract: Background: Neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy (nICT) has demonstrated promising efficacy in locally advanced esophageal cancer. The pretreatment neutrophil to lymphocyte ratio (NLR) has shown prognostic value across various solid tumors. This study aimed to evaluate the predictive value of pretreatment NLR for pathological response in patients with resectable esophageal cancer receiving nICT. Methods: A total of 295 patients with resectable esophageal cancer who underwent nICT followed by surgery were retrospectively analyzed. Pretreatment NLR was calculated from peripheral blood counts. Pathological response was assessed using the Becker tumor regression grading (TRG) system. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was conducted to evaluate the predictive performance of NLR. Multivariable logistic regression and bootstrap internal validation were performed to assess its independent predictive value. Results: Pretreatment NLR was significantly higher in non-pathological complete response (non-pCR) patients than in pathological complete response (pCR) patients (P=0.04). A weak positive correlation was observed between NLR and TRG (r=0.130, P=0.03). The area under the ROC curve (AUROC) of NLR for predicting non-pCR was 0.586 [95% confidence intervals (CI): 0.510-0.663, P=0.04], with an optimal cutoff value of 3.59 (sensitivity 37.6%, specificity 79.3%, positive predictive value 89.0%, negative predictive value 24.1%). The combination of NLR with clinical stage improved the AUROC to 0.633 for predicting non-pCR. In the esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) subgroup (n=271), NLR demonstrated improved predictive performance for both non-pCR (AUROC =0.609, 95% CI: 0.530-0.687) and non-major pathological response (non-MPR) (AUROC =0.570, 95% CI: 0.512-0.642). Integration with clinical T and N categories further increased the AUROC to 0.654 for non-pCR and 0.626 for non-MPR. Multivariable logistic regression confirmed that NLR was an independent predictor of non-pCR [odds ratios (OR) =1.325, 95% CI: 1.005-1.747, P=0.046], and bootstrap validation supported its robustness. Conclusions: Elevated pretreatment NLR is associated with poorer pathological response to nICT in patients with resectable esophageal cancer, particularly in ESCC. When combined with clinical staging, NLR may serve as an accessible adjunctive tool to identify patients with a low probability of pCR.

items.title: Noninvasive ventilation for non-expandable lung after pleural surgery: a single-center retrospective study
items.abstract: Background: Non-expandable lung (NEL) is a well-recognized complication of pleural surgery, characterized by failure of the lung to fully re-expand and appose to the parietal pleura, resulting in a persistent pleural space and substantial morbidity. Management of NEL remains challenging, and although the physiological rationale suggests that positive airway pressure could enhance alveolar recruitment and facilitate pleural apposition, the role of noninvasive ventilation (NIV) in treating this condition remains poorly studied. This study aimed to evaluate the potential benefit of NIV on radiological outcomes, as well as its feasibility and safety, for NEL following pleural surgery. Methods: This retrospective, single-center observational study included patients who received NIV for NEL following pleural surgery between May 2022 and February 2026. The primary outcome was lung re-expansion after NIV, assessed by chest radiography on day 1 (D1) and day 3 (D3), and at 4 weeks (W4) after discharge. Secondary outcomes included duration of chest tube drainage, length of hospital stay, pulmonary complications, NIV-related adverse events, recurrence of pleural effusion, 30-day mortality, home NIV prescription, and treatment adherence. Results: A total of 52 patients, with a median age of 73 years, were included in the final analysis. The etiology of pleural effusion was malignant in 71.2% of cases, and video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) was the predominant surgical approach. Complete re-expansion increased progressively, from 42.3% (22/52) at D1 to 73.1% (38/52) at D3 and 86.6% (45/52) at W4 after discharge, while the failure rate decreased correspondingly from 13.5% (7/52) to 3.8% (2/52) over the same follow-up period. Partial re-expansion also followed an inverse trend (44.2% at D1, 19.2% at D3, 9.6% at W4). The median durations of chest tube drainage and hospital stay were each 4 days. Pulmonary complications occurred in 2 patients (3.8%), recurrence of pleural effusion in 3 patients (5.8%), and no 30-day mortality was observed. NIV was well tolerated, with only minor adverse events; treatment adherence reached 94.2%, and 32.7% of patients were discharged with home NIV. Conclusions: In this preliminary, single-center, uncontrolled experience, NIV was feasible and associated with progressive radiological lung re-expansion in patients with established NEL following pleural surgery, with infrequent adverse events. These findings provide a preliminary proof of concept supporting NIV as a potential adjunct to standard postoperative care in this indication. Prospective, multicenter, randomized controlled trials, stratified by the mechanism of NEL, are needed to confirm this potential benefit and identify the patients most likely to benefit.
items.limitations: These results should be interpreted in light of several important limitations. First, the retrospective, single-center, uncontrolled design carries a risk of selection bias and confounding. No comparator group was included (e.g., patients who received standard pleural drainage without NIV during the same period), precluding differentiation of the specific effect of NIV from the natural course of NEL or from standard postoperative care alone; this limitation applies in particular to the primary outcome of lung re-expansion and should be addressed in future studies with a concurrent comparator, ideally randomized or, failing that, a historical comparator if eligible patients can be identified within our institution. The method of selecting patients for NIV (collegial clinical judgment during the daily multidisciplinary meeting, without a formalized written protocol with predefined inclusion thresholds) was not comprehensively documented over the entire study period, and the number of patients with a postoperative re-expansion defect who did not receive NIV during this period could not be established; selection bias therefore cannot be excluded. Second, as a preliminary single-center study, the diagnosis of NEL relied on clinical and radiological assessment during multidisciplinary meetings rather than on predefined objective diagnostic criteria (pleural manometry, CT, pleural ultrasound, or documented intraoperative VATS findings), which were not systematically available in this retrospective cohort. Despite these limitations, our study provides a preliminary proof of concept that justifies the conduct of prospective controlled trials. The next step should be a multicenter randomized trial comparing NIV combined with standard care versus standard care alone, with stratification according to NEL mechanism using a validated classification and blinded radiological reading, incorporation of assessment by pleural ultrasound or CT, a standardized titration and weaning protocol, and inclusion of patient-reported outcome measures (dyspnea, quality of life). In this preliminary, single-center, retrospective, and uncontrolled experience, the initiation of NIV in patients with an already established postoperative re-expansion defect (NEL) following pleural surgery, an indication distinct from the preventive use of NIV previously reported in the literature, was followed by progressive and sustained radiological improvement, a low rate of observed adverse events, and high treatment adherence. Given the retrospective, single-arm design without a comparator group, these findings describe a temporal association between NIV initiation and the observed radiological course, rather than a demonstrated therapeutic effect, and the descriptive, uncontrolled nature of our safety data does not permit the conclusion that NIV is safe in this indication. Within these limitations, our results provide a preliminary proof of concept suggesting that NIV may represent a feasible a

items.title: Real-world implementation of video-assisted thoracic surgery for lung cancer: a decade-long regional propensity score-weighted cohort study
items.abstract: Background: The perioperative advantages of video-assisted thoracic surgery (VATS) over thoracotomy are established, but the real-world introduction of a minimally invasive program is shaped by patient selection, technical maturation, conversion and secular change in care. We evaluated the decade-long implementation of VATS within a regional thoracic surgery service and estimated its association with early postoperative outcomes. Methods: This is a retrospective cohort study of anatomical lung resections performed over the first decade [2009-2018] of a VATS implementation program at two tertiary hospitals covered by a single thoracic surgery department. The primary exposure was the approach with which the operation was started under an intention-to-treat analysis strategy, and the outcomes were 90-day mortality, a composite of major morbidity and perioperative mortality, and 30-day readmission. Propensity score weighting used preoperative covariates, including calendar year and hospital. Covariate balance before and after weighting was assessed by absolute standardized mean differences. The average treatment effect (ATE), reported as risk difference with 95% confidence interval (CI), was the primary estimand, with average treatment on the treated (ATT) and average treatment effect on the overlap population (ATO) as sensitivity estimands. An exploratory analysis comparing conversion with upfront thoracotomy was carried out under the same prespecification. Results: A total of 964 out of 1,404 anatomical lung resections met the inclusion criteria. The series included 472 operations begun thoracoscopically, of which 97 were converted (20%), versus 492 upfront thoracotomies. Completed VATS rose from 16.7% of anatomical resections in 2009 to 53.7% in 2018, while conversion annual rates fell from 50.0% to 6.5%. Converted procedures had the highest crude rate of every adverse outcome. Under intention to treat, an intended VATS approach was not significantly associated with 90-day mortality (ATE -1.9 percentage points; 95% CI: -4.7 to +0.9; P=0.17), major morbidity and mortality (ATE -4.6 points; 95% CI: -9.4 to +0.2; P=0.06) or readmission (ATE -2.0 points; 95% CI: -5.9 to +2.0; P=0.33); for the composite outcome, the ATT (P=0.04) and ATO (P=0.047) estimands reached significance. In the as-treated analysis, all three outcomes were significant in favor of completed VATS. No statistically significant differences were detected between conversions and upfront thoracotomies in the exploratory analysis. Conclusions: Across a decade-long regional implementation trajectory, adoption of VATS rose and conversion fell. When conversions are analyzed in the arm in which the operation was begun, the association between an intended thoracoscopic approach and better perioperative outcomes is attenuated and no longer significant. These findings do not question the perioperative advantages of thoracoscopic lobectomy, but the benefit attributable to adopting a thoracoscopic strategy at service level is smaller and less certain than that observed among the operations it completes.

items.title: Long-term survival patterns and prognostic stratification in patients with unresectable locally advanced squamous cell lung cancer receiving definitive chemoradiotherapy: a 14-year single-center real-world cohort
items.abstract: Background: Real-world data with more than 10 years of follow-up among Chinese patients with unresectable locally advanced squamous cell lung cancer (SqCLC) treated with definitive chemoradiotherapy are scarce. This single-center cohort with complete 14-year longitudinal surveillance was constructed to map long-term survival kinetics, screen independent prognostic markers, and depict full disease trajectories, so as to facilitate stratified surveillance and personalized therapeutic management. Methods: This retrospective single-center real-world cohort enrolled 260 stage IIIA–IIIC unresectable SqCLC patients receiving definitive chemoradiotherapy between 2012–2019. Kaplan-Meier curves were used to estimate overall survival (OS), first progression-free survival (PFS1), and post-salvage second progression-free survival (PFS2); the log-rank test was applied for inter-group comparison. Multivariable Cox proportional-hazards regression (enter method) was utilized to screen independent prognostic factors, and a clinically-oriented 12-month PFS1 cutoff was used for risk stratification. Results: With maximum follow-up exceeding 14 years (data cut-off June 1, 2026), the 10-year OS rate was 35.0%. The survival curve exhibited a distinct three-phase trajectory: a high-risk phase during the first 3 years accounting for approximately half of all events, a decelerating decline from year 3 to 10, and a stable plateau beyond 10 years, with OS rates at 10 and 14 years both approximating 35%. Multivariable analysis identified age <65 years, peripherally located tumors, absence of radiation pneumonitis, objective response to first-line therapy, and PFS1 ≥12 months as independent protective factors for OS, among which PFS1 ≥12 months yielded the strongest effect [hazard ratio (HR) =2.70, P<0.001]. First disease progression occurred in 86.0% of patients, of whom 32.0% presented with oligometastatic lesions (defined as ≤5 metastatic lesions confined to limited anatomic sites without widespread disseminated disease); those receiving active local salvage therapy achieved a 14-year PFS2 rate of 48.0%. An interval of ≤3 months from diagnosis to radiotherapy initiation was associated with a significantly higher objective response rate (ORR) compared with >3 months (73.0% vs. 57.0%, P<0.05). Conclusions: A 10-year survival rate of 35% is achievable in patients with locally advanced unresectable SqCLC after definitive chemoradiotherapy, with substantially reduced risks of recurrence and all-cause mortality beyond the 10-year landmark. A PFS1 ≥12 months serves as a simple and robust prognostic biomarker for long-term survival, and active local salvage of oligometastatic lesions enables durable disease control. Surveillance schedules and consolidation strategies may be tailored according to patients’ progression-free status at 12 months.
items.limitations: Several inherent limitations of this retrospective analysis warrant explicit acknowledgment. First, the single-center design and the predominantly northern China study population limit the external generalizability of our findings to other ethnic or nationwide cohorts. Second, the absence of molecular biomarkers—including PD-L1 expression, EGFR, and ALK mutation status—precludes subgroup analysis of long-term survival benefits from immunotherapy or targeted agents, and impedes mechanistic exploration of the survival plateau at the molecular level. Third, a proportion of censored events arose from competing risks, such as cardiovascular disease and second primary malignancies, which may slightly attenuate the accuracy of 10-year plateau survival estimates. Fourth, the wide enrollment window [2012–2019] introduced heterogeneity in imaging surveillance modalities (e.g., variable PET/CT availability), potentially affecting the timeliness of progression ascertainment.

items.title: The ligament of Marshall as a therapeutic target in atrial fibrillation: from anatomy to catheter-based and surgical management—a narrative review
items.abstract: Background and Objective: Long regarded as an inconsequential embryological remnant, the ligament of Marshall (LOM) is now recognized as a treatable component of the atrial fibrillation (AF) substrate. This review synthesizes the anatomical, electrophysiological and clinical evidence behind that shift and compares the two routes to the LOM: percutaneous retrograde ethanol infusion into the vein of Marshall (EIVOM) during catheter ablation, and direct division during thoracoscopic surgery. Both act on the same epicardial structure; only the route of access differs. Methods: A structured literature search of PubMed, Embase and Web of Science covered the embryology, anatomy, histology and electrophysiology of the LOM and clinical studies of both routes. Two authors screened and selected records independently. Given the heterogeneity of study designs, findings were synthesized narratively. Key Content and Findings: The LOM is a neuro-muscular remnant of the embryonic left superior vena cava that contributes to AF through three mechanisms: triggers arising from insulated myocardial “Marshall bundles”, autonomic modulation via adjacent ganglionated plexi, and preferential conduction across the mitral isthmus. Five randomized trials of EIVOM-based strategies have enrolled more than 1,100 patients; pooled analysis shows improved 12-month freedom from any atrial arrhythmia (risk ratio 1.16, 95% confidence interval: 1.04–1.29; number needed to treat 10) and less repeat ablation, without excess major complications (2.5% vs. 2.8%) but with more overall complications and longer fluoroscopy. Crucially, no trial has tested ethanol infusion in isolation; the observed benefit reflects composite lesion sets. Thoracoscopic division interrupts the entire ligament independent of venous anatomy but has never been a randomized variable; randomized evidence for thoracoscopic and hybrid strategies overall ranges from neutral (CASA-AF) to positive (CONVERGE, HARTCAP-AF). Guidelines recognize both as options in selected patients without mandating routine LOM division. Conclusions: The LOM is a reproducible, anatomically defined target reachable percutaneously or by surgical division within a comprehensive AF ablation strategy. The supporting evidence is markedly asymmetric: randomized data exist for EIVOM-based strategies but never for ethanol infusion alone, none at all for surgical division, and the two routes have never been compared head-to-head. Its incremental benefit beyond pulmonary vein and posterior wall isolation remains undefined.
items.limitations: Its principal limitation lies in the structure of the underlying evidence, and the asymmetry is worth stating precisely. Randomized evidence exists for EIVOM-based ablation strategies—five trials and more than 1,100 patients—but it has never been generated for ethanol infusion in isolation, because in every trial the infusion was delivered as one component of a composite lesion set. No randomized evidence at all exists for surgical division of the ligament; the surgical literature consists of anatomical rationale and small observational series in which division was bundled with other lesions. And the two routes have never been compared head-to-head. Any statement that one is superior to the other is therefore an inference from indirect evidence, not a finding.

items.title: Lung transplantation outcomes in patients with coal workers’ pneumoconiosis compared with non-occupational interstitial lung disease: a single-center cohort study
items.abstract: Background: Coal workers' pneumoconiosis (CWP) is a lung disease caused by long-term coal dust exposure. Appalachian miners experience disproportionately high disease prevalence and mortality. Lung transplantation offers outcomes comparable to other interstitial lung diseases (ILDs), yet limited data exist on patients with CWP. This study examines regional disease burden and lung transplant outcomes for CWP at our institution compared with non-occupational ILD. Methods: A retrospective cohort study evaluated lung transplant recipients with CWP, autoimmune-ILD (A-ILD), and nonautoimmune-ILD (NA-ILD) at the University of Kentucky from 2017 to 2025. Patients were categorized by ILD etiology, and demographic, clinical, and post-transplant outcome data were collected from institutional records under institutional review board-approved protocols. Continuous variables were analyzed using one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) or the Kruskal-Wallis test. Categorical variables were compared using Pearson's Chi-squared test or Fisher's exact test. Survival was evaluated using Kaplan-Meier analysis. Results: Among 67 lung transplant recipients, 23 had CWP, 11 had A-ILD, and 33 had NA-ILD. CWP recipients were exclusively male and had a lower body mass index (BMI). Transplant recipients across all cohorts were predominantly male. Rates of acute kidney injury (AKI), renal replacement therapy (RRT), and hospital stay were similar across groups. Bronchial stenosis post-transplant was significantly more common with cardiac-death donors. Survival analyses suggested similar survival between the cohorts. Conclusions: This study observed no statistically significant differences in survival or postoperative complications in patients with CWP compared to those with non-occupational ILD. Female underrepresentation was found despite modern increases in women in coal-mining fields. Post-transplant complications of bronchial stenosis requiring dilatation ± stent were more likely in those who received organ donation after circulatory death (DCD). Limited impact of pre-transplant comorbidities was also noted. Despite small, single-center design, results suggest lung transplantation as a feasible treatment option in carefully selected patients with advanced CWP and highlight the need for larger multicenter studies.
items.limitations: There are limitations to this study that should be considered when interpreting these results. First, this was a retrospective, single-center study, which limits generalizability to other transplant centers. Second, the overall sample size was somewhat small, which reduced statistical power. Stratification between CWP, A-ILD, and NA-ILD also reduced per-group power. Third, the population was overwhelmingly white and predominantly from the Central Appalachian region, which, although this population was of particular interest to this study, may limit applying these results to other more diverse populations.

items.title: SNORD42A serves as an oncogenic biomarker in non-small cell lung cancer
items.abstract: Background: Despite substantial advances in therapeutic strategies, non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains the leading cause of cancer-related death worldwide. The poor prognosis of NSCLC is largely due to the limited efficacy of existing clinical treatments and the lack of reliable and effective molecular therapeutic targets. Studies have shown that small nucleolar RNAs (snoRNAs) play pivotal regulatory roles in multiple pathological processes involved in tumor formation and malignant progression. However, the specific biological functions and underlying molecular mechanisms of individual snoRNAs in the occurrence and development of NSCLC remain largely unclear, highlighting the need for systematic exploration. Methods: A reanalysis of genome-scale clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR)-Cas9 knockout screening data covering all annotated snoRNAs in NSCLC cell lines was performed. Colony formation assays confirmed the functional role of SNORD42A in NSCLC cells. A combined bioinformatic analysis of our internal sequencing data and public datasets further identified the molecular locus of SNORD42A in the pathogenesis of NSCLC. Results: Genome-wide screening identified SNORD42A as a key candidate snoRNA regulating NSCLC cell proliferation. Both the in-house snoRNA sequencing data and bioinformatics analysis of The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) cohort demonstrated that SNORD42A was significantly overexpressed in clinical NSCLC tissues compared with paired adjacent normal lung tissues, indicating its potential oncogenic role in NSCLC. Functional validation experiments further demonstrated that SNORD42A knockdown markedly inhibited the clonogenic capacity of NSCLC cells. Moreover, an integrative bioinformatics analysis of TCGA data revealed that SNORD42A expression was closely correlated with cell cycle regulation and cellular senescence signaling pathways, and its expression level was significantly associated with the clinical prognosis of patients with NSCLC. Conclusions: SNORD42A functions as a pro-tumorigenic factor that promotes NSCLC progression, with its effects potentially linked to alterations in cellular protein synthesis. This study revealed the functional importance of SNORD42A in NSCLC malignancy, suggesting that SNORD42A may serve as a novel prognostic biomarker and a promising therapeutic target for the treatment of NSCLC.

Evaluating robotic-assisted bronchoscopy for bronchus-unconnected peripheral pulmonary nodules: diagnostic efficacy and safety
items.abstract: Background: Bronchus-unconnected peripheral pulmonary lesions (PPLs) pose diagnostic challenges due to lack of direct airway access and computed tomography (CT)-to-body divergence (CTBD). We evaluated robotic-assisted bronchoscopy (RAB) combined with the intraprocedural CT-guided navigation with ventilatory strategy for atelectasis (ICNVA) strategy. Methods: This prospective, single-arm study enrolled patients (18-75 years) with pulmonary nodules (6-30 mm) lacking a bronchus sign. All underwent RAB with the ICNVA strategy, integrating preoperative mapping, intraprocedural breath-holds to minimize atelectasis, and real-time CT confirmation. The primary endpoint was tool-in-lesion (TIL) rate. Secondary endpoints included diagnostic yield, center strike rate, CTBD, and safety. Results: Thirty patients were enrolled (mean age 55.6±10.7 years). Lesions had a mean diameter of 14.0±4.3 mm and a median distance to the nearest bronchus of 18 mm. The ICNVA strategy resulted in a mean CTBD of 13.4 mm. We achieved a 100% (30/30) navigational success rate (TIL) and a 66.7% (20/30) center strike rate. The overall diagnostic yield was 90% (27/30), with 90.9% (20/22) sensitivity for malignancy. Pneumothorax occurred in 2 patients (6.7%) and mild hemorrhage in 7 (23.3%), with no severe adverse events occurred. Conclusions: RAB combined with the ICNVA strategy demonstrates high diagnostic yield and safety for bronchus-unconnected PPLs. This approach effectively mitigates CTBD, enabling precise localization and sampling of lesions traditionally considered difficult to access.

Effects of leritrelvir for adults with mild-to-moderate coronavirus disease 2019: A multicenter real-world study
items.abstract: Background: Real-world evidence for leritrelvir, a single-component 3C-like protease inhibitor, in adults with mild-to-moderate coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) remains limited. We evaluated the association of early leritrelvir use with symptom resolution, negative viral-test conversion, and adverse events in routine clinical practice. Methods: This prospective, multicenter, nonrandomized, open-label observational cohort study was conducted at 141 sites in China (mainland ). Among 1,527 adults with mild-to-moderate COVID-19, 1,388 received leritrelvir (400 mg three times daily for 5 days) plus standard care and 139 received standard care alone. The primary endpoint was time to sustained resolution of 11 predefined symptoms. The key secondary endpoint was time to negative severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) nucleic acid test (NAT) conversion. All participants contributed a primary time-to-event record. We estimated unadjusted and multivariable-adjusted Cox models and performed 1:1 propensity score (PS) matching (136 participants per group). Results: For sustained symptom resolution, the unadjusted hazard ratio (HR) was 1.41 [95% confidence interval (CI): 1.18-1.68; P<0.001], the multivariable-adjusted HR was 1.66 (95% CI: 1.38-1.99; P<0.001), and the PS-matched HR was 1.81 (robust 95% CI: 1.43-2.29; P<0.001). In the matched cohort, median time to symptom resolution was 6 days with leritrelvir and 8 days with standard care alone. For negative NAT conversion, the corresponding HRs were 1.20 (95% CI: 1.01-1.43; P=0.04), 1.22 (95% CI: 1.01-1.47; P=0.04), and 1.47 (robust 95% CI: 1.21-1.79; P<0.001); matched medians were 3 and 4 days. Adverse events occurred in 22.41% and 19.42% of the unmatched groups, respectively. Conclusions: In this prospective, multicenter, nonrandomized cohort, leritrelvir use was associated with earlier sustained symptom resolution and negative SARS-CoV-2 NAT conversion than standard care alone. Although the direction of association was consistent across multivariable-adjusted and PS-matched analyses, residual confounding, open-label symptom assessment, nonproportional hazards, incomplete follow-up, and the absence of severe-outcome events preclude causal, subgroup-specific, or severe-outcome conclusions.
items.limitations: This study has several limitations. First, treatment allocation was nonrandom and the groups were markedly unequal in size and baseline risk. Confounding by indication and selection bias are major limitations because measured and unmeasured factors may have influenced both treatment choice and outcomes. Although multivariable adjustment and PS matching addressed measured covariates, residual imbalance remained in several chronic disease covariates after PS matching and may have introduced residual confounding. Second, the primary endpoint was a participant-reported 11-symptom composite in an open-label study.

items.title: Clinical outcomes with initial oral triple and dual therapy in echocardiography-defined connective tissue disease-associated pulmonary hypertension: a retrospective single-center cohort study
items.abstract: Background: Connective tissue disease-associated pulmonary hypertension (CTD-PH) is a serious complication, but evidence on early oral treatment intensification in patients followed primarily by echocardiography is limited. We evaluated outcomes associated with initial selexipag-containing oral triple therapy vs. dual therapy in echocardiography-defined CTD-PH. Methods: This single-center retrospective cohort included consecutive adults who initiated PH-targeted therapy between April 2020 and June 2025. Treatment was selected by treating physicians in routine care and was not randomized: dual therapy comprised macitentan plus tadalafil, whereas triple therapy additionally included selexipag. Baseline clinical, laboratory, and echocardiographic variables were obtained from standardized institutional assessments and reassessed at week 26. The primary endpoint was the change in the number (0–3) of European Society of Cardiology/European Respiratory Society (ESC/ERS) noninvasive low-risk criteria met: World Health Organization functional class (WHO-FC) I–II, 6-minute walk distance (6MWD) >440 m, and B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) <50 ng/L or N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) <300 ng/L. Complete cases with all three components available at both time points were analyzed without imputation. Disease-progression events were recorded through 30 weeks, and adverse events were assessed during follow-up. Results: Of 119 patients, 59 received triple therapy and 60 received dual therapy. The groups had similar baseline functional and biomarker profiles (6MWD, 290.0 vs. 286.9 m; NT-proBNP, 1,455 vs. 1,473 pg/mL); mean age was 45.5 vs. 47.2 years in the triple and dual therapy group respectively, and 93% vs. 83% were women. At week 26, the change in low-risk criteria differed between groups (P=0.003), with 57.6% vs. 33.3% meeting all the three criteria. Mean 6MWD increased by 156 vs. 104 m (adjusted difference, 52 m; 95% confidence interval (CI): 29–78; P<0.001), and WHO-FC distributions differed at week 26 (P=0.007). Exploratory analysis yielded an hazard ratio (HR) of 0.75 (95% CI: 0.39–1.43) for the first disease-progression event. At least one adverse event occurred in 53/59 (89.8%) vs. 47/60 (78.3%) patients; diarrhea occurred in 24/59 (40.7%) vs. 19/60 (31.7%), nausea in 21/59 (35.6%) vs. 16/60 (26.7%), and jaw pain in 16/59 (27.1%) vs. 11/60 (18.3%), with no significant between-group differences. Conclusions: In this real-world cohort of patients with echocardiography-defined CTD-PH, initial selexipag-containing oral triple therapy was associated with greater improvement in noninvasive ESC/ERS risk status and functional outcomes than dual therapy over 26 weeks, supporting further evaluation of noninvasive risk-guided oral treatment intensification in CTD-associated pulmonary vascular disease. However, given the small, single-center, nonrandomized retrospective design, these findings cannot establish superior efficacy or safety and require prospective multicenter confirmation with systematic hemodynamic assessment.

items.title: The effects of Mycobacterium tuberculosis genotypes on clinical phenotypes revealed by whole-genome sequencing technology in China
items.abstract: Background: (MTB) lineages and tuberculosis (TB) clinical phenotypes remain inconsistent across studies, primarily because conventional genotyping techniques lack the resolution to distinguish fine-scale sublineages. This study aimed to rigorously verify the clinical characteristics and prognostic significance of predominant Beijing-lineage strains circulating in China using high-resolution genomic evidence. Methods: In total, 173 patients with TB were enrolled in the study, and whole-genome sequencing (WGS) was performed on 213 clinical MTB isolates; mixed-strain infections were excluded from subsequent analyses. Phylogenetic sublineage classification was performed based on single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) profiling. Multivariate logistic regression was used to independently assess the associations between MTB genotypes, clinical manifestations, and treatment outcomes, after adjusting for demographic and clinical confounding factors. Results: Among the 172 valid isolates, 80.8% were classified as East Asian Beijing lineage (lineage 2), 18.0% as Euro-American lineage (lineage 4), and 1.2% as Indo-Oceanic lineage (lineage 1). Compared with the non-Beijing strains, the Beijing strains were independently associated with an increased risk of pulmonary cavitation [adjusted odds ratio (aOR) =4.76, 95% confidence interval (CI): 2.01-11.26, P=0.006], as well as a decreased risk of disseminated TB (aOR =0.40, 95% CI: 0.17-0.95, P=0.04). No significant association was observed between the Beijing genotype and treatment failure, whereas cavitary disease was an independent predictor of treatment failure. Conclusions: MTB genetic diversity contributes substantially to heterogeneity in TB clinical phenotypes. WGS enables precise sublineage identification and facilitates robust genotype-phenotype analysis. These findings support the implementation of genomic surveillance to optimize individualized clinical management and inform targeted TB prevention strategies in endemic regions.

items.title: Artificial intelligence in esophageal cancer radiotherapy: a literature review
items.abstract: Background and Objective: Radiotherapy is a key component in the management of esophageal cancer (EC). Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative tool for optimizing radiotherapy workflows. Numerous AI-based tools are being developed to improve efficiency and facilitate the personalization of radiation oncology. This study aimed to provide an up-to-date review of the literature on recent advances in AI applications across the EC radiotherapy workflow. Methods: The PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science databases were searched to retrieve original English-language articles published from January 1, 2020 to May 26, 2026. The following search terms were used: "Esophageal neoplasms", "esophageal cancer", "oesophageal cancer" AND "artificial intelligence", "AI" AND "radiation oncology", "radiotherapy", "radiation", "chemoradiotherapy". The included studies covered different steps in the radiotherapy workflow; that is, initial treatment decision-making, treatment planning and preparation, treatment delivery, and post-treatment follow-up. Key Content and Findings: A total of 105 studies covering the different stages of the radiotherapy workflow were included in the review. Most studies focused on initial treatment decision-making, primarily benefit-risk stratification through predictive modeling of treatment outcomes and treatment-related toxicities, followed by treatment planning and preparation, particularly automated segmentation and treatment planning. Conversely, few studies investigated AI applications in treatment plan approval and quality assurance, or treatment delivery. Notably, most of the included studies were retrospective, with substantial heterogeneity in study designs, methodologies, and reporting. Conclusions: AI demonstrates substantial potential to facilitate clinical decision-making while improving the efficiency and accuracy of radiotherapy workflows. Future research should prioritize multicenter prospective studies, standardized methodological and reporting frameworks, and explainable AI (XAI) to improve the reliability, transparency, and clinical translation of AI models.
items.limitations: These limitations may introduce selection biases, promote local overfitting, and limit generalizability across institutions, while also raising concerns about algorithmic fairness. The applicability of these models to other populations, particularly patients with esophageal adenocarcinoma or gastroesophageal junction tumors, may be limited, as differences in tumor biology, anatomical characteristics, and treatment protocols may affect model performance. The publicly available datasets, such as TCIA, The Cancer Genome Atlas esophageal carcinoma (TCGA-ESCA) dataset, and the Cancer Moonshot Biobank Gastroesophageal Cancer Collection (CMB-GEC), have facilitated data sharing and integration, enabling standardized benchmarking and comparison of different AI methods. However, the collection and aggregation of robust datasets remain major challenges, largely due to data heterogeneity and privacy and legal concerns. Establishing trust in AI systems is also essential, particularly given the “black-box” nature of AI algorithms and, more specifically, deep learning models. This concern is especially relevant to AI-based decision-support systems, in which system errors may result in patient harm, limitations may be poorly understood, and model outputs may lack sufficient interpretability. Despite substantial research, no AI-assisted decision-making system is currently ready for clinical implementation. XAI has been actively researched; however, the lack of transparency in AI continues to hinder the interpretability of model outputs, understanding of prediction failures, and the troubleshooting of issues. Other major challenges include the paucity of prospective multicenter validation and randomized clinical trials, as well as the lack of seamless integration with clinical treatment-planning systems and ART workflows. Future research should focus on the establishment of multicenter collaborative databases, multimodal data integration, and adherence to internationally recognized methodological and reporting guidelines to address the remaining challenges. Additionally, due to space limitations, the tables present only the results of the representative models. Nevertheless, cross-study comparisons of model performance metrics should be interpreted cautiously. We conducted a narrative review of the recent literature on the application of AI in EC radiotherapy. AI demonstrates substantial potential to support clinical decision-making while improving the efficiency, accuracy, and quality of EC radiotherapy workflows. However, several challenges remain, including the predominance of retrospective and single-center studies, limited external validation, substantial methodological and reporting heterogeneity, and poor model interpretability.

items.limitations: This text provides an independent assessment of these recommendations, their limitations, and their place within the broader field of sleep-disordered breathing. Across four Delphi rounds, response rates exceeded 93%, and 68 of 75 candidate items met the predefined 80% agreement threshold, later consolidated into 54 statements. The process included role separation (steering group members who drafted statements did not vote, and panelists did not participate in evidence extraction) and a three-level evidence-basis label (E1–E3) distinguishing direct PS evidence from indirect extrapolation and expert opinion. Three substantive points merit emphasis. First, the consensus draws a hard line between PS and mild OSA, rejecting the relaxed AHI threshold below 15 events/hour that some clinicians have used, and clarifying that loudness is neither necessary nor sufficient for the PS phenotype. Several important limitations should be kept in mind when applying these statements. Twenty-seven of 30 panelists were otolaryngologists; only three were sleep medicine physicians, and all practiced in tertiary Chinese centers. Dental sleep medicine specialists, who fit and titrate MADs, were absent, as were pulmonologists, primary care clinicians, behavioral sleep specialists, and, importantly, patients and bed partners. This composition likely tilted the panel toward anatomical and procedural perspectives while underweighting feasibility, adherence, and patient-preference data that determine real-world outcomes. A scoping review of Chinese OSA patients’ treatment trajectories found that patient preferences, cultural norms, and healthcare access shape adherence profoundly, dimensions an otolaryngologist-dominated panel may not fully capture.

items.abstract: The clinical management of mild-to-moderate Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) has transitioned from crisis-driven intervention to routine outpatient care, yet available therapeutic options remain insufficient to meet full clinical demand.Although Omicron-lineage infections are mostly mild and self-limiting, older adults, patients with multiple chronic illnesses and immunocompromised persons retain substantial risks of clinical deterioration, hospital admission and death (1,2).Oral early-phase antivirals therefore continue to serve important public-health functions, though two widely deployed agents carry notable practical drawbacks.Nirmatrelvir-ritonavir produces extensive, clinically relevant drug-drug interactions via ritonavir-mediated cytochrome P450 3A (CYP3A) inhibition, whereas molnupiravir delivers only modest clinical benefit alongside theoretical concerns over mutagenic potential (3-5).An oral single-agent main-protease inhibitor dispensing with pharmacokinetic boosting has long represented a desirable but unvalidated therapeutic objective (6).In this issue of the Journal of Thoracic Disease, Cheng and colleagues report a real-world assessment of leritrelvir based on a prospective, multicentre, open-label cohort of 1,527 adults with mild-to-moderate COVID-19 across 141 mainland Chinese sites, comparing early leritrelvir administration against standard care alone (7).Their findings merit careful, impartial appraisal; they do not constitute definitive clinical endorsement, but instead furnish a translational bridge between positive phase-3 placebo-controlled trial outcomes and the heterogeneous conditions of everyday clinical practice.This cohort study enrolled 1,388 participants receiving oral leritrelvir (400 mg three-times-daily for five days) plus standard care and 139 participants managed by standard care only, during a period dominated by Omicron subvariants EG.5 and JN.1 (7).Investigators deployed three complementary analytical strategies: unadjusted analysis, multivariable regression adjustment and 1:1 propensity-score matching.Across these approaches, leritrelvir-treated participants achieved sustained symptom resolution approximately two days earlier and SARS-CoV-2 nucleic-acid negativity roughly https://jtd.amegroups.org/about/editorialTeam
items.limitations: This booster creates Paxlovid’s principal clinical limitation: CYP3A perturbation generates hazardous interactions with anticoagulants, antiarrhythmics, immunosuppressants, calcium-channel antagonists, statins and psychotropic medications, precisely the polypharmacy regimens common among high-risk candidates for antiviral therapy. International clinical guidance required extensive revision to incorporate drug-interaction checklists, and numerous eligible patients were consequently denied access to nirmatrelvir-ritonavir. Chinese antiviral-drug development pursued two parallel pathways. Simnotrelvir retains ritonavir boosting; supported by positive phase-3 randomised data, it entered the domestic market in early 2023 as China’s first oral 3CLpro inhibitor. Leritrelvir (development code RAY1216), developed by Guangdong Raynovent Biotech, adopts an alternative chemical framework as an α-ketoamide peptidomimetic agent optimised for monotherapy use. Indication-based confounding constitutes the most substantial limitation. The approximate 10:1 imbalance between treated and control groups reflects non-random clinical prescribing; unmeasured variables such as baseline symptom severity, healthcare access or clinical practice patterns may independently modify recovery trajectories. Propensity-score matching balances only recorded covariates, and residual imbalances for cardiovascular disease, diabetes and hepatorenal disease persist even after matching. Additionally, the primary endpoint relies on participant-reported composite symptom assessment within an open-label framework, introducing reporting bias that may overestimate treatment-associated benefit. Incomplete follow-up represents a further caveat.

items.abstract: Background The clinical phenotypes, prognosis, and heterogeneity of mild-to-moderate chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) have not been systematically evaluated. Research question Do different clinical phenotypes of mild-to-moderate COPD have different prognoses? Study design and methods We analysed the baseline and 3-year follow-up data of participants with mild-to-moderate COPD from a prospective community-based cohort study. Mild-to-moderate COPD was defined as a forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV 1 ) / forced vital capacity ratio of 1 ≥ 50% of the predicted value. The clinical phenotypes included respiratory symptoms, exacerbation history, emphysema, air trapping, and airway remodelling. Respiratory health outcomes included exacerbations and lung function decline over the 3-year follow-up. Results Overall, 806 participants with mild-to-moderate COPD were included, of whom 712 (88%) completed the 3-year follow-up. Participants with mild-to-moderate COPD had more severe emphysema, air trapping, and airway remodelling; increased exacerbation risk; and faster annual FEV 1 decline than those with preserved spirometry. The severity of airflow obstruction, respiratory symptoms, emphysema, and air trapping, as well as the eosinophilic phenotype, had low overlap in mild-to-moderate COPD. There was significant individual variation in the annual FEV 1 decline rate and exacerbation incidence among participants with mild-to-moderate COPD. Emphysema and air trapping were associated with faster FEV 1 decline and higher exacerbation risk. Respiratory symptoms and exacerbations in the previous year were associated with a higher acute exacerbation risk but not with faster lung function decline. Interpretation Mild-to-moderate COPD exhibited distinct clinical phenotypes with significant prognostic heterogeneity. Accurate phenotype identification is essential for targeted intervention, clinical precision management, and prognostic improvement.

items.title: Subspecialty ILD Clinic Care is Associated with More Guideline-Concordant Evaluation and Improved Outcomes Compared to Other Ambulatory Settings: A Retrospective Cohort Study
items.abstract: Background Subspecialty interstitial lung disease (ILD) clinics are associated with improved outcomes, yet access remains uneven. Even within tertiary health systems, patients with ILD are managed across diverse ambulatory settings, with unclear implications for care and outcomes. Research question Within a single academic health system, do patient characteristics, care delivery, and outcomes differ between individuals with ILD managed in a subspecialty ILD clinic versus other ambulatory settings? Study design and methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults with ILD at a large academic medical center. Identified patients were stratified by care in a subspecialty ILD clinic versus non-specialty setting. Demographic, diagnostic testing, treatment, health care utilization, and survival data were extracted from the electronic health record. Diagnostic and treatment measures were analyzed using multivariable logistic regression. Hospitalization, emergency department visit, and death were analyzed as time-to-event outcomes. Results Among 6,637 patients with ILD, 4,371 (66%) were seen in the subspecialty ILD clinic. The 2,266 patients (34%) managed in non-specialty settings were more likely to identify as Black or Latinx, reside in more socioeconomically deprived neighborhoods, and have an unspecified ILD diagnosis (all p Interpretation Within a single health system, subspecialty ILD clinic care was associated with more guideline-concordant care and improved outcomes. Differences in access to subspecialty expertise may contribute to inequities in care delivery, underscoring the need for scalable strategies, referral optimization, telemedicine, and clinical decision support, to extend ILD expertise and improve outcomes.

items.title: Azithromycin Exposure and Incident Nontuberculous Mycobacterial Isolation in Bronchiectasis and COPD: A Nationwide Nested Case-Control Study
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Azithromycin reduces exacerbations in chronic airway disease, but whether it alters the risk of nontuberculous mycobacterial (NTM) isolation is unresolved. RESEARCH QUESTION: Is azithromycin exposure in the preceding year associated with incident respiratory NTM isolation in non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis and in COPD? STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: Two nationwide register-based nested case-control analyses in Denmark. Case patients had a first positive respiratory culture for NTM; controls, alive and free of prior NTM isolation on the index date, were matched 1:20 on age, sex, and comorbidity index. The prespecified exposure was at least 3,000 mg of azithromycin with at least two prescriptions redeemed in the preceding 12 months, with a 3-month lag. Conditional logistic regression was adjusted for inhaled and oral corticosteroids. Exploratory analyses examined an active comparator at matched thresholds, recency, and outcome stringency. RESULTS: The analyses comprised 173 cases and 3,409 controls (bronchiectasis) and 365 and 7,300 (COPD). Under the prespecified definition, azithromycin was not associated with incident NTM isolation (bronchiectasis: OR, 1.31; 95% CI, 0.79-2.18; COPD: 1.29; 0.78-2.13). In COPD, the OR was 1.61 (1.14-2.28) for one or more prescriptions and 1.29 (0.78-2.13) for two or more. The COPD association was concentrated within 90 days of the index date (2.55; 1.73-3.76) and attenuated with microbiological stringency (definite isolates: 0.77; 0.27-2.20). Non-macrolide antibacterials were more strongly associated than azithromycin at every matched threshold in bronchiectasis (one or more prescriptions: 1.90 [1.36-2.65] vs 1.15 [0.75-1.75]), and at the two higher thresholds in COPD (two or more: 1.48 [1.17-1.86] vs 1.24 [0.75-2.05]). INTERPRETATION: Azithromycin was not associated with NTM isolation under the prespecified definition. Associations under broader definitions were not dose-dependent and clustered close to the index date, more consistent with indication-driven testing than a drug effect, although in COPD an association with any exposure persisted after accounting for other antibacterials.

items.title: Population-based Prevalence of Bronchiectasis in the United States
items.abstract: Background Bronchiectasis is a chronic, heterogeneous lung disease of rising prevalence; however, contemporary epidemiological data are lacking. Furthermore, paediatric prevalence and cystic fibrosis (CF)-related bronchiectasis prevalence are frequently absent from existing literature. Research question What is the prevalence of bronchiectasis in the United States? Study design and methods This retrospective, observational study utilised data from the Optum® Clinformatics® Data Mart claims database to estimate the age- and sex-standardised prevalence of bronchiectasis in the US in people of all ages and paediatrics (aged Results In the overall population, 94,392 cases of bronchiectasis were identified (median age, 76 years). Five-year prevalence was 221.6 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 220.1-223.1) per 100,000 persons and increased with age. Prevalence was higher among females (274.6 per 100,000 persons), Asians (302.3 per 100,000 persons) and Medicare Advantage enrolees (528.6 per 100,000 persons). In total, 1.4% of the overall population had a diagnosis of cystic fibrosis. Five-year prevalence in the paediatric population (including 465 cases; median age, 12 years) was 11.9 (95% CI: 10.8-13.1) per 100,000 persons. Paediatric prevalence was similar between sexes, higher in Caucasians and higher in those with non-CF-related bronchiectasis than CF-related bronchiectasis. Interpretation This current study reports that bronchiectasis prevalence continues to increase in the US compared with previous studies, with a consistently higher prevalence in females and Asians, and that a lower proportion of individuals have CF-related bronchiectasis compared with non-CF-related bronchiectasis.

items.title: Giving or Taking? Ethical Guidance for Hospital Administrators Involved in Organ Procurement
items.abstract: Organ procurement from unrepresented decedents is legal in the United States, and some states even designate "the hospital administrator" as having the right to authorize donation. However, there is little guidance for an administrator to consult in their effort to make a socially responsible decision. In this case study, we review the arguments in favor of deferring, deciding against, or deciding in favor of authorization. We contend that that there are three reasons involving uncertainty, inequity, and the risk of mistrust that should give an administrator pause in endorsing organ procurement. We ultimately recommend that organ recovery should not be authorized unless there is (1) strong evidence that a diligent search for surrogates has been undertaken, establishing a reasonable amount of certainty that none are forthcoming, and (2) some evidence suggesting that the decedent would favor organ donation.

items.title: Pretransplant Pulmonary Hemodynamics, Explant Histology, and Primary Graft Dysfunction after Lung Transplantation for Silicosis
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Silicosis associated with progressive massive fibrosis (PMF) is a major cause of end-stage lung disease among workers in the artificial stone industry. Patients with PMF are increasingly referred for lung transplant (LTx) evaluation and there is emerging evidence of pulmonary hypertension (PH) in patients with advanced PMF. RESEARCH QUESTION: Among patients with PMF referred for lung transplantation, what is the incidence of PH and what are accompanying histopathologic pulmonary vascular aberrations? STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: Retrospective single-center cohort study of prospectively-enrolled participants, providing granular data on the invasive hemodynamic profile of patients with silicosis-associated PMF, histopathologic data on pulmonary vascular aberrations, and clinical data on post-transplant complications. Clinical and sociodemographic variables were collected. Explanted lungs from patients with silicosis-associated PMF underwent detailed pulmonary vascular histopathologic review and were descriptively compared with PAH explants. The incidence of primary graft dysfunction (PGD) was evaluated and descriptive analysis performed to provide associations of clinical features and PGD incidence. RESULTS: PH was present in over 95% of 21 patients with silicosis-associated PMF who underwent LTx, with a hemodynamic profile similar to patients transplanted for PAH. . Silicosis explants showed confluent silicotic nodules, extensive fibrosis and hyalinization, obscuration or obliteration of vascular structures, and perivascular fibrohistiocytic infiltrates with extrinsic narrowing. Classic PAH-type arteriolar muscular hypertrophy and plexiform arteriopathy were uncommon. In exploratory comparisons, patients who developed PGD had more frequent pretransplant right ventricular dysfunction (71% vs 21%; risk difference 0.50, 95% CI 0.06-0.75) and a lower median TAPSE/RVSP ratio (0.27 vs 0.39; Hedges' g -0.93, 95% CI -1.88 to 0.02) than in those without PGD. INTERPRETATION: These findings suggest that PH in advanced silicosis with PMF is very common and represents a distinct pulmonary vascular phenotype characterized by extensive fibrotic vascular obliteration rather than the classic arteriopathy seen in PAH.

items.title: “Bold and necessary experiments:” The redelegation of authority and responsibility to nurses at the origins of cardiac intensive care
items.abstract: Coronary Care Units (CCUs) were at the forefront of the development of intensive care in the 1960s and 1970s. The development of CCUs, and intensive care more broadly, was enabled by the interplay of expanding medical technology and the evolving role of nurses vis-à-vis physicians. This paper examines the history the CCU at New York Hospital, the teaching hospital of Cornell University School of Medicine and School of Nursing, with a particular focus on role of nurses in the unit's success. Drawing from historical archives of New York Hospital and the Cornell University School of Nursing, this paper argues that that nurses were co-creators, alongside physicians, of the NYH CCU, and demonstrates how nurses drew from the NYH CCU experience to expand critical care services at the local and national level, including by advocating for the creation of the NYH medical intensive care unit (MICU), leading a CCU nurse training program to expand regional CCU capability, and contributing expertise to a federally-sponsored national conference on CCUs. A close reading of this history offers lessons and insights as intensive care medicine moves into an uncertain future, chief among them that work of caring for critically ill patients requires the thoughtful integration of new technologies with hands on care.

items.title: The impact of removing prior authorization for guideline-concordant maintenance inhaled medications for COPD: a population-based cohort study
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Most patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) do not receive maintenance inhaled therapies in concordance with evidence-based clinical guidelines. Long-acting muscarinic antagonists (LAMA), the recommended first-line therapy, is underused, while inhaled corticosteroids (ICS)/long-acting beta-agonists (LABA) are often used in discordance with clinical guidelines. In July 2020, British Columbia's (BC) universal drug plan removed prior authorization requirements for coverage for LAMA medications and restricted coverage for ICS/LABA. RESEARCH QUESTION: What is the impact of this policy change on guideline-concordant maintenance inhaled medication use? STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: In a population-based cohort study using provincial administrative health data, we identified patients with COPD using a validated case definition and followed them from January 2019 (18 months pre-policy) to December 2022 (30 months post-policy). Using interrupted time series analysis, we evaluated the monthly proportion of patients filling a prescription for ICS/LABA and LAMA, mean canisters dispensed, proportion of days covered (PDC), rates of ICS/LABA discontinuation, LAMA (re)initiation, and initiating LAMA as first maintenance therapy. We report absolute differences between observed and counterfactual outcomes at study end. RESULTS: The cohort included 47,583 patients with COPD (mean 71.5 years, 46.5% female, 31.7 months mean follow-up). Thirty months post-policy change, ICS/LABA use decreased by -1.3% (95% CI -2.4, -0.3) and LAMA use increased by 0.8% (95% CI 0.1, 1.6). There was no significant change in the number of ICS/LABA canisters dispensed, PDC or proportion discontinuing ICS/LABA. Mean LAMA canisters dispensed increased by 9.8 per 1,000 patients (95% CI 1.0, 18.7) and PDC increased by 1.5% (95% CI 0.5, 2.4). (Re)initiation of LAMA or initiating LAMA as maintenance therapy increased by 0.2% (95% CI 0.02, 0.3) and 34.8% (95% CI 22.3, 48.6), respectively. Total combined drug costs did not change. INTERPRETATION: Changes to drug coverage in BC were associated with improved guideline-concordant medication use.

items.title: Patient self-selection of in-person versus virtual pulmonary rehabilitation
The Impact of Undernutrition on Post-Tuberculosis Lung-Function: A Prospective Cohort Study
items.abstract: Background Undernutrition is the leading driver of tuberculosis worldwide, yet its effect on the lungs of people who complete treatment is not well defined. Research question Among adults treated for drug-sensitive pulmonary tuberculosis, is undernutrition associated with worse post-treatment lung function, radiographic severity, exercise capacity and respiratory quality of life, and does systemic inflammation mediate that association? Study design and methods Adults (≥18 years) with drug-sensitive pulmonary tuberculosis were enrolled at treatment initiation in India. We measured associations of baseline body mass index (BMI), mid-upper arm circumference (MUAC), and premorbid BMI with spirometry, chest radiograph score, six-minute walk distance and St George's Respiratory Questionnaire score. Plasma IFN-γ, TNF-α and IL-6 were measured at baseline and month 2; counterfactual mediation analysis partitioned the effect of undernutrition on lung function into direct and inflammation-mediated components. Results Of 156 participants analyzed, 76 (48.7%) had a ventilatory defect; 52 (33.3%) had airflow obstruction and 31 (19.9%) had restrictive spirometry. Each 1 kg/m 2 higher baseline BMI was associated with lower odds of any ventilatory defect (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.78; 95% CI, 0.67-0.90), and BMI below 16 kg/m 2 carried five-fold higher odds than BMI ≥18.5 kg/m 2 (aOR, 5.08; 95% CI, 1.76-16.02). MUAC and premorbid BMI showed similar associations. Lower BMI was associated with restrictive spirometry (aOR, 0.74 per kg/m 2 ; 95% CI, 0.59-0.89) but not airflow obstruction (aOR, 0.91; 95% CI, 0.80-1.03). Undernourished participants had higher baseline IL-6, which mediated 32% (FEV1) and 49% (FVC) of the association with impaired lung function. Interpretation Undernutrition before and at treatment initiation is a potentially modifiable determinant of post-treatment lung impairment, with systemic inflammation mediating part of the effect. Nutritional assessment belongs in routine tuberculosis care, and nutritional support should be tested to prevent lung-function impairment in tuberculosis survivors.

items.title: Efficacy and Safety of Ulinastatin in the Treatment of Patients with Sepsis: The ADJUST Trial
items.abstract: Background Urinary trypsin inhibitor (ulinastatin, UTI) has shown potential survival benefits in sepsis; however, conclusive clinical evidence is lacking. Research question In patients with sepsis, does adjunctive ulinastatin, compared with placebo, reduce 28-day all-cause mortality? Study design and methods In this multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, adult ICU patients with sepsis meeting Sepsis-3 criteria within 48 hours of admission were randomized (1:1) to receive intravenous UTI (400,000 IU every 8 hours) or placebo, for up to 10 days in addition to standard care. Randomization was stratified by site and septic shock. The primary endpoint was 28-day all-cause mortality. Secondary endpoints included ICU, hospital, and 90-day mortality, and ICU/hospital length of stay. Results Of 347 patients randomized, 340 (169 UTI, 171 placebo) received intervention and were included in the safety analysis; after 5 post-intervention withdrawals, 335 (165 UTI, 170 placebo) were included in the intention-to-treat analysis. At 28 days, death had occurred in 39 of 165 patients (23.6%) in the UTI group and in 39 of 170 patients (22.9%) in the placebo group (absolute difference, 0.7% [95% CI -8.4% to 9.7%]; P = .98; hazard ratio 1.03, 95% CI 0.66 to 1.61, P = .90). Secondary outcomes were similar in the two groups. Adverse events occurred in 56.8% (96/169) of UTI and 42.7% (73/171) of placebo patients (absolute difference 14.1%, 95% CI 3.6%-24.6%; P = 0.009). Interpretation In patients with sepsis, adjunctive UTI did not reduce mortality compared with placebo. Routine use of UTI for sepsis is not supported by these findings. Clinical trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov; https://clinicaltrials.gov; NCT02647554.

items.title: From Response to Remission in Adult Severe Asthma
A Young Man With Hypereosinophilia and Pseudochylothorax
items.abstract: Case presentation A 31-year-old man presented with a 2-month history of dry cough, progressive dyspnea, intermittent fever, and unintentional weight loss of 8 kg. He had no wheezing, hemoptysis, chest pain, palpitations, or skin rashes. He did not smoke and reported occasional alcohol intake. One year earlier, he had been diagnosed elsewhere with pleuro-pericardial TB based on an ultrasound showing right-sided pleural effusion, and 2-dimensional echocardiography showed pericardial effusion. Pleural fluid analysis showed a lymphocytic exudative pleural effusion with elevated adenosine deaminase levels (46 IU/mL). The patient received anti-tubercular therapy along with tapering corticosteroids, showing initial clinical improvement. He was employed as a soldier in the army, and his last posting was in northeast India, where he frequently consumed raw crabs pickled in alcohol. There was no other significant environmental history.

items.title: A 63-Year-Old Man With Dyspnea and Loculated Pleural Effusion
items.abstract: Case presentation A 63-year-old man with a past medical history of hypertension and end-stage renal disease receiving scheduled hemodialysis via a left upper extremity fistula sought treatment for shortness of breath of 1 to 2 years' duration that worsened acutely for 1 day after missing a hemodialysis session. In addition, the patient reported mild central chest pain without radiation. He otherwise was in his usual state of health and did not report fevers, chills, cough, sputum production, wheezing, abdominal pain, or hemoptysis. He reported history of tobacco use, having smoked one-half a pack of cigarettes for 15 years and quit about 15 years ago.

items.title: Mediastinal Mass With Recurrent Hemorrhagic Pleural Effusion
items.abstract: CASE PRESENTATION: A 55-year-old man was admitted with a 2-year history of recurrent dyspnea and exertional breathlessness, accompanied by intermittent blood-tinged sputum. During this period, he had been hospitalized 7 times at external institutions, where he underwent extensive investigations including fiberoptic bronchoscopy, endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial needle aspiration, mediastinoscopy, thoracoscopy, and CT imaging-guided biopsy of a mediastinal mass. Empirical antituberculosis therapy also was administered, but no definitive diagnosis was established.

items.title: Persistent Severe OSA Despite Ongoing CPAP Therapy
items.abstract: Case Presentation A 51-year-old man was referred to our sleep medicine clinic for reevaluation of previously diagnosed OSA. The diagnosis had been established approximately 4 years earlier, at a body weight of 105 kg (BMI, 31.7 kg/m 2 ). At that time, cardiorespiratory polygraphy documented severe OSA, with an apnea-hypopnea index of 97 events/h. Mean nocturnal oxygen saturation (Spo 2 ) was 91%, and the cumulative time spent with Spo 2 < 90% accounted for 38% of the total recording time, indicating a substantial nocturnal hypoxemic burden. Nocturnal CPAP therapy had been prescribed, delivered through an oronasal mask at a fixed pressure of 11 cm H 2 O.

Bilateral Pulmonary Nodules After Lung Transplantation
items.abstract: Case presentation A 64-year-old man who underwent bilateral orthotopic lung transplant for emphysema related to α1-antitrypsin deficiency 8 months ago presented to the clinic for assessment of bilateral pulmonary nodules identified on routine postlung transplant surveillance without any symptomatic concerns. The donor was positive for cytomegalovirus and positive for Epstein-Barr virus, and the recipient was negative for cytomegalovirus and positive for Epstein-Barr virus. He denied any fever, chills, cough, chest pain, dyspnea, weight loss, or night sweats. The patient lived in South Florida with no recent travel history outside the United States or infectious contacts. His posttransplant course was complicated with antibody-mediated rejection at 1.5 months after lung transplant. Antibody-mediated rejection was successfully treated with our institutional multimodal regimen, including a combination of plasmapheresis, carfilzomib, and anti-thymocyte globulin followed by monthly IV immunoglobulin and tocilizumab injections. Also, because of calcineurin inhibitor (CNI)-related renal dysfunction, the patient's immunosuppression was converted to a belatacept-based CNI-sparing regimen in addition to prednisone, with a tacrolimus goal trough of 4 to 6 ng/mL. He was also placed on mycophenolic acid, which was soon held because of neutropenia.
